["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Not sure, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Independence Brewing Company in Mumbai stands out for its fantastic craft beer selection, delicious Indian-inspired bar snacks, and lively ambiance, making it a top destination for those seeking a fresh and flavorful pub experience in the city.

### Exceptional Fresh Beers

The brewery is highly praised for its variety of freshly brewed beers, with options ranging from Belgian Wit to more unique offerings like mango cider and experimental blends. Patrons consistently commend the beers for their originality and refreshing taste, noting that a taster menu lets you sample before choosing your pint. The staff Ajit is knowledgeable and eager to help guests pair their brews with different dishes.

### Achari Masala Peanut: An Addictive Bar Snack

The achari masala peanut is a standout snack at Independence Brewing Company, offering a twist on classic bar peanuts by infusing them with tangy, spicy achari (pickle) flavors. The combination of the crisp nuts and zesty masala makes it a perfect companion to cold, fresh beer—balancing bitterness and enhancing the overall tasting experience.

### Masala French Fries: Super Crisp and Tasty

Guests consistently rave about the masala French fries, describing them as super crisp and loaded with bold spices that elevate their flavor. Served piping hot, these fries hold their crunch and pair excellently with the beer selection, making them an ideal choice for both solo and group outings. The fries' seasoning provides a delicious contrast to the refreshing and smooth beers, turning a classic side into a memorable highlight of the meal.

### Atmosphere and Service

The brewery boasts a welcoming vibe, with friendly, attentive staff and attractive decor that adds to the festive spirit. The bar’s ambiance is enhanced by its cozy seating and sometimes rooftop views, giving guests a relaxed setting for socializing or unwinding. Service is usually prompt and helpful, though some visitors note occasional lapses during busy periods.

### Overall Impressions

Independence Brewing Company excels at balancing creative Indian snacks, exceptional craft beers, and a vibrant atmosphere to create a memorable experience for anyone visiting Mumbai’s bar scene. Its achari masala peanut, masala French fries, and crisp, fresh beers form the perfect trio for an enjoyable evening with friends or family., name_person=Gaurish Gupta}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=a month ago, review=We visited Independence Brewing Company on a Saturday night, and as expected, the place was buzzing with energy. There was a waiting queue, but honestly, it was absolutely worth it. What made the entire process smooth was their online queue management system — you can check your position in real time, monitor how many people are ahead, and plan your waiting comfortably. This small but smart feature really sets them apart and shows how well they manage weekend rush.

Once we got in, the ambience immediately set the tone — lively, upbeat, and perfect for a weekend hangout. The service team was efficient even on a packed night, and the food came out quicker than we expected.

We ordered a bunch of starters and everything turned out great. The Peri Peri Fries had just the right balance of spice and crispiness. The Chicken Popcorn was juicy, crunchy, and very addictive. The Pollo Aglio Olio was simple yet flavourful, and the Spaghetti Bolognese was rich and satisfying — a great choice for pasta lovers.

The drinks were the true highlight. We tried two of their beers: Happy High and King Jovial. Both were unique in flavour, smooth to drink, and exactly what you expect from a place known for craft beer culture. Each beer had its own personality, and it’s clear that they take brewing seriously.

For the non-alcoholic options, their mocktails didn’t disappoint at all. The Mandarin & Chilli mocktail was refreshing with a bold twist of spice — one of the most interesting mocktails I’ve tried recently. And the Indian Gooseberry Cooler was so good that we ended up ordering it twice. Light, tangy, cooling, and incredibly refreshing.

Overall, our experience at Independence Brewing Company was fantastic from start to finish. Despite the Saturday night crowd, the place runs smoothly, the atmosphere is vibrant, the food consistently good, and the drinks truly stand out. Whether you’re looking to try unique beers, enjoy a fun night out, or simply indulge in great food, this place is definitely worth visiting.

Waiters weren't able to recommend me some popular dishes or able to answer basic questions such as most ordered dishes., name_person=Smit Nandu}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=My honest opinion - this restaurant is best for dinners. We had lunch so could not appreciate the nighttime lights of Powai. The restaurant had an easy to locate as the Google Maps directions were precise. It’s not exactly in the centre of the Hiranandani shopping district in Powai where most of the restaurants are clustered. But the this restaurants can’t give you the view Yuhi does. The menu is pretty exhaustive - a mixed bag of every cuisine - Indian, Mediterranean, continental, pan Asian and so is the drinks menu - alcoholic and non-alcoholic. The starters portions are generous. Enough for 4 to savour. The restaurant itself is very simple in its layout and decor. Nothing flashy and over the top which works for me. At capacity I think it can easily take in up to a 100 guest or maybe more. The food was great especially the mushroom risotto. The balance of vegetarians d non-vegetarian is prefect so both kinds have plenty to choose from. My only grouse with Yuhi which applies to most restaurants in Mumbai, please serve 300 mL of wine and Sangria for those prices that you charge. And yes some imported beers at reasonable prices will only drive in more customers - just a suggestion. Yuhi is prefect for birthday parties and any family occasion or ones with friends and you can get loud as it’s a rooftop restaurant so yes perfect for a good time…The prices are like any other restaurant in Mumbai so you know what I am trying to say… And a note of thanks to our server Rihan who looked after us really well and was quick to respond. And thanks for handing over the iPhone my wife forgot to pick up on our way out. Good service, friendly staff, nice food. Paneer: Stale and chewy.

Curd: Sour and clearly gone bad.

Pastries: The first round was average; the second round (on request) was stale.

Gravies: Every dish tasted identical – as if they used the same base gravy for all.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Hummus_Bayroute, Fatar_Baklava, Harissa_Chicken_Kebab, Ispanak_Mantar_Pide], GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=I recently visited Bayroute Powai, and it was an amazing experience!
The ambience was elegant and gave true Mediterranean vibes.

**Appetizers:** The *Lavash Kebab* and *Kebab Halabi* were absolutely delicious — soft, juicy, and full of flavour.

**Drinks:** Tried *Smoky Rum N Raisins* and *Palm Islands*, both were refreshing and beautifully presented.

**Main Course:** *Shawarma Al Bayroute* and *Arayes Tavuk* were perfectly cooked — rich taste, great portion size, and authentic flavour.

**Dessert:** *Apple Crumble Cheesecake* was the highlight — creamy, perfectly balanced sweetness, and a must-try!

Overall, a great experience with top-notch food and service. Definitely one of the best spots in Powai for Mediterranean cuisine!, name_person=Rahul Gupta}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Hummus_Bayroute], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Lovely dinner experience. The overall theme is Turkish with very welcoming interiors. Loved the hot air balloon themed decor. The outside area is also nice for gatherings.

Although above average on cost, each of their offerings do stand out in terms of presentation and the experience. No wonder it takes around 20 mins prep time, the wait is much worth it.

The Al Meshwi non-veg platter was more than enough for the three of us with assortment of starters. The different dips and pickled vegetables provided were also very fresh.

The star of the day was Machboos Al Kuzu, which is a very rich lamb and rice dish similar to the Yemeni Mandi. I wish they had not discontinued the regular Mandi, which was lighter on stomach for picky eaters.

To end it we had their signature Baklava, the presentation of which stunned us with quite a showmanship with flash frozen rose flower. It tasted amazing paired with gulkhand icecream.

Happy with the service with very knowledgeable people who patiently explained to us what each dish was. Great for family outings. Would love to go again !, name_person=Jyothis Thaliath}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Just had the most incredible dining experience at this stunning Middle Eastern restaurant in Powai, Mumbai! 🤩 The moment I stepped in, I was transported to the vibrant streets of the Middle East, surrounded by mesmerizing decor and plush ambiance 🌿✨.

I started with not one, but TWO signature drinks - "Let's Date" and "Honey on Fire" 🍹🔥. Both were absolute perfection, with the sweetness of dates and honey balanced by the subtle kick of spices. Definitely a must-try for any cocktail enthusiast! 🍸

For the main course, I indulged in some finger-licking goodies:
- *Kataifi Prawns*: Crispy, succulent prawns wrapped in kataifi pastry, bursting with flavors of the Middle East 🍤
- *Kebab Joojeh*: Tender, juicy chicken kebabs marinated in a blend of spices and yogurt, grilled to perfection 🍗
- *Harissa Chicken Manakeish*: Spicy harissa chicken on a bed of crispy dough, topped with melted cheese and herbs - a flavor bomb! 🧀
- *Moroccan Lemon Olive Chicken*: Zesty, herby, and utterly delicious, this dish was a masterclass in balancing flavors 🍗

And no meal is complete without dessert! 🍰 I ended my meal with the classic *Turkish Baklava*, layers of flaky phyllo pastry, crunchy nuts, and sweet honey... it was love at first bite! ❤️

The aesthetic ambiance, complete with air balloons, added to the magic of the evening. The courteous staff made sure we felt right at home. 🌟

Perfect spot for a date or a night out with friends! 📅👫 Highly recommend! 👏, name_person=Kshitija Bhosale}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Visited Bayroute, a premier Middle Eastern restaurant, and had such a lovely experience. The ambiance is beautiful warm lighting, elegant decor, & a very comfortable vibe. The staff was really helpful and attentive throughout our visit.
We tried two mocktails Reyhan and Watermelon Cooler, both refreshing and nicely made.
For food, we had Feta and Pine Nut Stuffed Falafel, Harissa Chicken Kebab, Musabbaha, and Koshari. The falafel was crispy on the outside and soft inside with a rich filling of feta and pine nuts. The chicken kebab had a nice smoky flavour and was perfectly spiced. Musabbaha was creamy and smooth, while Koshari was comforting and full of textures a must-try if you enjoy wholesome flavours.
Ended our meal with Baklava, which was light, flaky, and just the right amount of sweet.
Overall, a wonderful dining experience perfect for anyone who loves Middle Eastern food., name_person=Pooja Fulsundar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Hummus_Bayroute, Kebab_Halabi, Mezze_Platter, Chocolate_Kunafa], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_PARKING_LOT, Free_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_STREET_PARKING, Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET, Free_parking_garage, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_PARKING_GARAGE], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION, Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=2 months ago, review=I had an incredible lunch at Bayroute, Powai, exploring their newly launched Kebabs & Mezze menu. The ambiance has a beautiful Middle Eastern touch, creating a warm and premium dining experience. 🕌✨

I tried their Honey On Fire cocktail and Greek Goddess mocktail both beautifully presented and perfectly crafted. The Aleppo Kebab (Chicken) was juicy and flavorful, while the Moroccan Charmoula Prawns were zesty and spiced to perfection. The Bayroute Muhammara (V) with pita and fresh veggies was rich and smoky truly one of the best mezze I’ve had.

Recently, I had the chance to visit China Valley, a spot that combines a good ambience with the convenience of valet parking. The experience was overall enjoyable, though there were a few hiccups along the way.

Ambience and Service:
The ambience at China Valley is inviting, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a meal. The service, however, was just okay. The staff was polite, but there was a bit of a mix-up when they brought out the appetizer and soup together, which felt a little rushed.

The Food:

For appetizers, the Tortellini Skewers were an absolute standout — perfectly cooked and full of flavor. Moving on to mains, we enjoyed the Tagliolini Ai Porcini, which was rich, creamy, and full of flavors from the porcini mushrooms. The Pizza Salsiccia was another highlight, with a crisp base, generous toppings, and just the right amount of spice from the sausage.

We ended the meal on a sweet note with their Tiramisu, it had a well-balanced coffee flavor — a perfect finish.

I'll definitely be returning, especially for their pizzas, live music and their cozy Sunday vibe., name_person=Achyut Panigrahi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Ordered a pasta and a pizza.
Pasta was good and pizza was okay.
Giving a single star review for a reason!
Went for my wife's birthday, was going okay until the pizza and pasta. To celebrate the birthday we ordered a portion of tiramisu. It came with her name written on the plate and on the side the waiter brought a plate with knife and a fork. I looked closely to find a COCKROACH on the knife!! It was a horrible experience!!!, name_person=Saacheen Pol Music}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA, Bar_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_BAR_AREA, Outdoor_patio_/_terrace, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_OUTDOOR_PATIO], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=7 months ago, review=We recently visited the place. First of all, the ambience and vibe is so good. The place is well maintained and there is an open sitting area as well outside the restaurant.

The menu had many Italian items, but the names were so complicated that we had to Google search or ask the staff about them. 😅

Overall we found the food was good and within reasonable prices compared to other expensive Italian restaurants in Mumbai. But the service is slow, so each order took about 20 mins to half an hour to service., name_person=Asish A}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000}, time_line=6 months ago, review=If you’re ever feeling too happy or content with life, here’s a tip: order food from Mia Cucina, Powai. That should ruin your evening in no time.

Let me start with what they dare to call a Feta Salad – a sad mess of wilted lettuce dumped in a bowl, tossed with exactly one (yes, one!) lonely crumb of feta. The rest of the dish looked and tasted like it had been prepped last week, left out, and then remembered just in time to be shoved into a box and sent out. You know it’s bad when even the croutons taste defeated.

Now for the “complimentary garlic bread” – I’m not sure what’s worse: the fact that it was stale, or that someone decided a dollop of butter in the middle qualified as effort. It felt like an afterthought, or maybe a dare.

The final straw was the Aglio Olio – a dish that’s meant to be simple and comforting. Instead, what arrived was a dry, clumpy mess that required us to literally use our own olive oil and dressing just to make it semi-edible. After a few bites of that, we gave up and dumped the rest of the food in the bin. Yes, it was that bad.

The damage? ₹3000 down the drain. And we ended up ordering a whole new meal from Smoke House Deli because we were that disappointed and still very hungry.

To make matters worse, the customer service was laughable. A guy named Marshal, who claimed to be from their PR team, kept parroting the same line: “The chef has admitted fault and we’ll resend the food.” Excuse me, but why on earth would we want more food from a kitchen that couldn’t get a basic salad or pasta right the first time? That’s not customer care – that’s adding insult to indigestion.

To anyone considering ordering from Mia Cucina Powai – don’t. Spare yourself the disappointment, the waste, and the utter lack of accountability. There are too many good places out there for you to gamble your money and appetite on this one.

You’ve been warned., name_person=Myron Mendes}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Food+music+ambience+drinks+service=Mia cucina(perfect)}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The spaghetti bolognese gave the 2 people who ate it mild food poisoning.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=I had ordered an appetizer, one lasagna, one pizza along with some good wine.}"]

Chili’s has always been known for its dependable food quality, and that part still remains intact. We ordered the Chicken Platter, which comes with a nice customisation option. The portion size was good, the flavours were balanced, and everything was served hot and well-prepared. It’s the kind of comfort food Chili’s is known for, and it didn’t disappoint.

For drinks, I tried their Mango Mocktail, and it was easily one of the highlights of the evening. Refreshing, smooth, and perfectly sweet — I liked it so much that I ended up ordering it twice. Their beer selection was also good, maintaining the familiar Chili’s standard.

However, a few things held the experience back from being a full 5-star visit. The first noticeable issue was the pre-added 10% tip on the bill. While I fully support tipping for good service, adding it automatically and at a relatively high percentage didn’t feel right — especially considering the level of service we received. The service wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t exceptional enough to justify a mandatory 10% charge. Tips should always feel voluntary and earned, not forced.

The ambience also felt different compared to the older Chili’s outlets. One thing that always made Chili’s special was its distinct American pub-style vibe — warm lighting, rustic interiors, and a lively but cozy atmosphere. The Powai outlet, unfortunately, doesn’t quite capture that same charm. The décor and layout feel more like a typical modern Indian pub, lacking the signature Chili’s personality that many of us associate with the brand. It’s decent, but it doesn’t stand out the way earlier Chili’s interiors used to.

That said, the environment is still comfortable for dining, and the place is clean, spacious, and well-maintained. The overall quality of food and drinks remains trustworthy, and if you’re looking for a casual evening out with good food, Chili’s Powai is still a reliable choice.

In summary, the experience was enjoyable — great food, excellent mocktails, and a relaxed vibe — but with room for improvement in service transparency and ambience. Parking:
No stress here—R City offers six floors of parking space, which is a huge plus, especially on weekends.

Mall Vibes:
R City Mall itself is huge and packed with branded outlets and a bustling food court. Perfect for a full day out.

Ambience at Grandmama’s Cafe:
Very cozy and aesthetic setup. Although it was a weekend and a bit busy, the space still felt inviting and warm.

Service:
Quick and prompt. The staff was attentive, and food came without much wait time.

What we tried:
•	Avocado Toast – Fresh, crispy bread, flavourful toppings, served with a small salad. Really nice.
•	Corn Ribs – On the drier side. Not the best, but okay to try once.
•	Watermelon Basil Mocktail – Refreshing and packed with flavour.
•	Falafel Wrap – Good in taste and well-balanced.
•	Khow Suey – This was more like Thai curry with noodles. It didn’t feel like the authentic Khow Suey, and would’ve been better served with rice. Taste was okay, not memorable.

Overall Experience:
The fast service and charming ambience made it a good experience. I’d recommend this place for couples, colleagues, families, or friends who are looking to relax and enjoy some casual café bites.

👍 Worth a visit if you’re in the area!, name_person=Siddhesh Kotian}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Paid_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_PAID_PARKING_LOT], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Tucked into a charming, homey setting, Grandmama’s Café offers the kind of warmth that makes you feel instantly at ease. From the cheerful décor to the comforting aroma of fresh food and coffee, everything about the place speaks of relaxed indulgence — and our experience didn’t disappoint.

We started with the Peri Peri Plancha Mushroom — a flavorful appetizer featuring chilli garlic tossed mushrooms, served with slices of herbed garlic panini. The mushrooms were juicy and well-seasoned, with the peri peri adding just the right kick. The panini was soft, aromatic, and perfect for scooping up the sauce.

Next up was the Pesto Basilico Spaghetti — a delightful bowl of spaghetti cooked in a rich, creamy basil pesto sauce, dotted with sautéed vegetables. The pesto was fresh, vibrant, and nutty, coating the pasta generously without being overwhelming. A satisfying choice for pesto lovers.

The Pan-Seared Chicken Momos brought in an Asian twist — Tibetan-style dumplings with a crispy sear, dressed in spicy chili oil and topped with scallions. The dumplings had a nice bite to them, and the chili oil added a bold layer of flavor without overpowering the dish.

For drinks, we went with a Cappuccino and a Café Latte.
•	The Cappuccino had a perfect balance of strong espresso and creamy froth, with a rich, nutty finish.
•	The Café Latte was smooth and mellow, with the milk softening the espresso’s bitterness into a comforting, warm hug in a cup.

To finish, we shared Grandmama’s Special Pizza — a house favorite made with their secret tomato sauce, mozzarella, English cheddar, and toppings like American corn, olives, bell peppers, jalapeños, and sun-dried tomatoes. The crust was crisp on the edges, and the combination of cheeses gave it a creamy, slightly sharp profile, balanced by the sweetness of corn and sun-dried tomatoes and the zing of jalapeños.

The ambience was truly one of the highlights — pleasant, inviting, and filled with a sense of casual elegance. The café feels like a perfect spot for both quiet conversations and cheerful catch-ups. Highly recommended by popular foodie Kunal Vijaykar, you cant go wrong with Gurukrupa, name_person=swayambharat}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=We recently visited Gurukrupa Restaurant in Powai, and it turned out to be such a delightful experience! The place has a warm and welcoming vibe, and the staff truly know how to make you feel comfortable from the moment you step in. Their hospitality was genuinely impressive — polite, attentive, and quick with service.

We ordered "Kori Roti" and "Fried Rice", and both dishes exceeded our expectations. The Kori Roti was absolutely authentic — rich, flavorful, and perfectly spiced with that signature Mangalorean touch. You could taste the freshness and effort put into every bite. The Fried Rice was equally delicious — perfectly cooked, aromatic, and packed with flavor. Together, the combination was simply mouthwatering.

Overall, Gurukrupa Restaurant is a gem in Powai — ideal for anyone who loves authentic South Indian and coastal food. Mysore Donne Chicken Biryani- This deserves a paragraph of its own! Served in the traditional donne (cup), the biryani was aromatic, flavorful, and the chicken was tender. Authentic Mysore style all the way.

Mangalorean Mutton Rayalseema - Tender mutton with robust spices. The meat was cooked beautifully and just fell off the bone.

Neer Dosa (2 orders!) - Soft, lacy, and perfect to scoop up all those amazing gravies
Prawns Pulimunchi - Tangy and spicy, exactly how it should be
Gad bad (Full) - A delightful end to the meal!

While the décor was beautifully done with festive vibes 🪔🎊 and the staff were courteous and attentive 🙏🏼, the food itself was a mixed bag.

There were plenty of dishes to choose from 🍽️, but unfortunately, only a few really stood out:

1. Mac & Cheese on Crostini 🧀🍞 – delicious!
2. Fish Orly 🐟 – crispy and well-seasoned
3. Mangsho Gondhoraj Finger (Chicken Starter) 🍗 – flavorful
4. Baked Florets (Au Gratin) 🥦🧄 – cheesy and comforting
5. ✅ The desserts were excellent 🍰🍮 – definitely the highlight of the meal.

However, most of the other dishes were strictly mediocre and didn’t quite live up to expectations 😕. Given the premium pricing, the buffet dinner really didn’t feel worth it 💸.

That said, the breakfast spread at the hotel is quite good 🍳🥐, so perhaps stick to that if you’re visiting.

👍🏼 Pros:
✨ Beautiful Durga Puja-themed décor
🧑‍🍳 Friendly and attentive staff
🅿️ Parking available within the hotel compound

👎🏼 Cons:

The ambiance is modern and cozy, making it perfect for a casual meal. The staff, especially Mr. Garrish and Ram, were extremely friendly and helped us with recommendations. We started with the Peach Paradise and Pinacolada mocktails, which were refreshing. The Italian Caprese Bruschetta was a great choice for starters, and for the main course, we enjoyed the Aloo Paratha, Paneer Paratha, and Spaghetti Pasta in creamy cheese, all served in generous portions. To top off the meal, we had the sizzling brownie with ice cream, which was a delightful dessert. Overall, the fusion of flavors was well done, and the service added to the good dining experience.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Lunch\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b9800\u20131,000\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS\":\"Highly recommend\",\"GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS\":[\"Vegetarian_options\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS\"]}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Rahul Gupta\",\"time_line\":\"a year ago\",\"review\":\"Curry N Pasta in Vile Parle offers a distinctive dining experience with its fusion of North Indian, Chinese, South Indian, Fast Food, Continental, Arabian, & American cuisines. The restaurant features a warm and modern ambiance that makes it both inviting and comfortable, whether you\u2019re there for a casual meal. The service is notable for its friendliness and efficiency; the staff is attentive and well-informed, ready to provide recommendations and ensure a pleasant dining experience.\\n\\nThe menu is a highlight, showcasing a creative blend of flavors. Signature dishes like the Tandoori Paneer Tikka, Chicken Reshmi Tikka, Mushroom Butter Masala, Chicken Kasturi Masala and many more. creating a unique and satisfying fusion. Another standout is the Butter Chicken Ravioli, which presents a flavorful twist on classic ravioli with its rich butter chicken filling. The portions are generous, making the dining experience both enjoyable and value for money.\\n\\nOverall, Curry N Pasta excels in delivering a creative and enjoyable culinary experience, merging Indian spices in a comfortable and friendly setting.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b91,400\u20131,600\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Puja Anjarlekar\",\"time_line\":\"a year ago\",\"review\":\"Curry N Pasta successfully marries the bold, vibrant flavors of Indian cuisine with the comforting, classic tastes of Italian food. Each dish was thoughtfully crafted, showcasing the best of both culinary worlds. Whether you\u2019re a fan of Indian curries or Italian pasta, this fusion restaurant offers a unique dining experience that is sure to delight your taste buds.\\n\\nRating\\n\\nFood: \u2605\u2605\u2605\u2605\u2606\\nService: \u2605\u2605\u2605\u2605\u2605\\nAmbiance: \u2605\u2605\u2605\u2605\u2606\\nOverall: \u2605\u2605\u2605\u2605\u2606\\n\\nHighly recommended for those looking to explore a unique fusion of flavors in a welcoming setting.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b9800\u20131,000\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":4}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Bhavin Parekh\",\"time_line\":\"a year ago\",\"review\":\"Curry & Pasta is an exellent restaurant of Parle International hotel, Vile parle east which offers an intriguing fusion of Italian and Indian cuisine, blending two beloved food traditions into a unique dining experience. The restaurant\u2019s concept of combining curry dishes with classic pasta is a refreshing twist, and it has quickly gained popularity among food enthusiasts looking for something different. The ambiance is cozy yet vibrant, with modern decor and warm lighting that gives it an inviting, casual feel. It\u2019s a comfortable place for both casual lunches and more relaxed dinners.\\nThe menu at Curry & Pasta offers an impressive variety of dishes from Indian, Italian amd Chinese cuisines. Standout items include:\\nWatermelon feta salad : refreshing and hydrating dish.\\nFully loaded nachos : crispy nachos topped with cheese and salsa was superb in taste.\\nFettuccini pasta : A perfect fusion of creamy mix sauces and pasta. The richness of the mix sauces blends seamlessly with the al dente pasta, creating a flavorful and indulgent dish.\\nLahori paneer tikka : This is a slightly cheesy, smoky rendition of paneer, perfectly marinated. The balance of flavors is spot-on, with just the right amount of heat and smokiness.\\nThe service is attentive, and the staff is friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. Curry & Pasta in Vile Parle East is an excellent choice for anyone looking to explore an innovative blend of Italian and Indian flavors. It\u2019s a great spot for a casual meal with friends or family, and the fusion of cuisines is bound to leave a lasting impression.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":4,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":4}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"Service is friendly and efficient, with staff happy to recommend dishes.\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"The place had a classy and elegant vibe that made our meal feel special.\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"They offer delicious, scrumptious and finger licking north Indian cusine.\",\"guided_block\":{}}"]

This restaurant boasts of a varied menu filled with Keralite cuisine right from Chicken, mutton to prawns, fish as well as vegetarian options. We take you through all the dishes served to us.

Chicken 'Just Kerala' Style Soup

Spicy soup flavoured with pepper and consisting of shredded chicken pieces which hits into you straightaway. Quite absorbing.

Prawns Fry (Highly Recommended)

Delicious prawns marinated alongside spices and deep fried. We were served eight pieces and you just couldn't get enough of it.

Chicken Chettinad with Kerala Poratha & Appam

A delicious spicy thick gravy cooked in aromatic sauces and garnished with coriander leaves. While we like Appam, the combination of Chicken Chettinad alongside Kerala Poratha was one to savour.

Chicken Biryani (Highly Recommended)

Chunks of chicken with masala layered between rice with fried onion. The biryani was scrumptious till the last bite and it was not very spicy as well. You have to eat this dish if you visit.

Coconut Souffle

We finished our meal with this wonderful dessert that is coconut souffle. It is a delicious creamy pudding made with tender coconut flesh and the presentation is also very good. Trust us, we can eat like 4-5 of these, that's how good it was.

We also had their zira water (which is good for digestion) as well as fresh lime soda. They also had thaal options in chicken, fish and vegetarian. The ambience was really good and peaceful and the interior is also very nice. Perfect restaurant if you want to eat authentic Kerala cuisine., name_person=The Hogger Bloggers}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Traditional_Kerala_Vegetarian_Thali], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=The place speaks for itself just as the name is. We ordered 3 course meals in dinner for a family of four
1)Chicken sampler was good but too salty for my liking

3) Naan and biryani were also mediocRe.

Now Starts the issues

1) Ordered prawns tawa fry and they were stale and were smelling bad had to return it, and they took it back too.

2)Service was very slow and poor.Mind it the restaurant was not full and still the service was absymal at best.

3)I can understand a waiting time of 15-20 mins since food is being cooked.But we had to wait 30 mins for the chocolate sampler which was just two pastries and one tart and was simply mediocre.The pastries were dry and not at all good it was as if someone has bought the pastries from a roadside cycle hawker and served it here.This came after reminding and waiting for 20+ mins

All in all an experience not worth remembering.Better to avoid it since  at that price point( prices are very high considering the experience)far better options are available nearby only where in the food and service both are great.

Highly recommend this gem for a fantastic meal and top-notch hospitality!, name_person=مدثر}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Brunch, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=2 years ago, review=10/10 for Service | Good location |  Good ambiance

I had been here for Sunday Brunch with a group of friends. The entire experience was good. The ambiance is pleasant and the food is also decent. Service is what made our experience pleasant. The junior staff there was very warm and friendly but there seniors had a lot of tantrums and ego.

The music and ambiance was beautiful, as it should be in a 4-5 star hotel and deserved 4 stars but i have given only 3 as the chairs there was not on good shape. They were having cracks and could break anytime. When we pointed this issue out with one of the chairs which was wobbling a junior female cleaner came to replace that. The chair was heavy and the senior male staff saw her struggling but no one cared to come ahead and help her.

Coming on the food the taste was okay and the variety was also good but the starters cold and the no one cared to reheat them.

We had done the booking through Nearbuy and the deal had a mocktail included but upon asking we were told that in mocktail there is only a hot spiced pineapple drink and that was pathetic. Even if there was a shikanji there it would have had been better.

The ala-crate mocktails were also tasting like taken from a road side juice center.

The overall experience was good but the only disappointments were the senior staffs attitude, beverages and cold starters.

But its worth giving a second visit here., name_person=Rahil Kotadia}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=We went here to try the Buffet at Solitaire restaurant located in Kohinoor Continental in Chakala, Andheri. The Ambience of the restaurant is good and the staff & service was great. I would like to thank the staffs that assisted us throughout the dinner.

The buffet had plenty of options in Veg as well as in the Non-veg section. the buffet included starters, chaat, main course, salad & desserts.
In starters, I tried the Fish chilly, chicken malai dilli tikka both non veg starters were tasty. the fish was tender & soft, the tikka was creamy & juicy. The veg kebab was delicious too, vegetarians can also try the veg cheese balls as well.

In the Mains, we had some Indian gravies with the parathas. the amritsari paneer was creamy n flavorful.. it went really well with the paratha. The chicken gravy with roti along with the pad thai noodles with the veg gravy was tasty too.

I loved the malpua rabdi & lemon tart in the dessert. these were some delicious desserts to try here.. the rabdi was thick, creamy & sweet just made for everyone to enjoy it., name_person=Nikhil Gupta}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a year ago, review=The speciality of this place is their Fusion with North Indian Food.
And I've tried few of their best fusions and I must say, I loved them all and so will you.

I started with their mocktails, Spiced Kokum and our very own Virgin Mojito, the mojito was as perfect as it can be, and the spiced kokum was surprisingly good.

My most favorite was their Stuffed Pita Harabhara Kebab, the Fusion of Hummus Pita and harabhara Kebab was delicious.

Also tried Zaitooni Tandoori Mushrooms and Naan Paneer Pizza, these fusions were also very tasty and unique.

For dessert we tried their Baked Madhuram which was a mix of Gulab Jamun, Boondi and loaded with Rabadi which was baked together. My sweet tooth was more than satisfied.

Below contains reviews ans pictures taken multiple times.\\nHoli - The festival of colors. The same resembles to the food we eat. On this festive fervor, I stepped in to enjoy this magnificent colorful Holi Brunch.\\nAs soon as you stepped @courtyardmumbai you will see huge dessert counter. But today my eyes captured all authentic glossy, classy, looking desserts and I was so amazed. Everything was looking stunningly colorful.\\nI started my Brunch with Khow Suey and varieties of starters. I love the Ragda Patis Chaat, Chhole Kulche, specially Chhole was made up with nice Punjabi style. Litti Choka was absolutely delicious. The sourness, spiciness and hint gave the perfect tongue twister. Potato Cheese balls were crispy and went well with green chatni. Ditto with Paneer, mashroom and babycorn Satay.\\nIn main course I had various varieties amongst that Hyderabadi Biryani was delicious. Curd was not at all sour. The vegetables cooked with appropriate spices. Paneer Lababdar was definitely winner here.\\nNow my favorite part during the Brunch which, was Dessert. As I said I couldn't refrain myself from eating desserts at the earliest. I again selected Indian desserts and it was WOW!. Each and every dessert was made in uniquely. Different types of Gujiyas, Meetha Samosa were so delicious ditto with Jalebi and Laddu which was packed with lot of Ghee. The Coconut Rasgulla won my heart too. Meetha Paan was stuffed with dry fruits and had a Gulkand flavor to it. Very rare I see this unique dessert. I wish there couldn't have been any disease called Diabetes to repeat all those desserts multiple times. \\uD83D\\uDE05\\nTo accompany my meal I had Pina Colada (complimentary given) and Fresh Lime Soda. I had those to bring my taste buds back from the colorful food.\\nService was great and I never had any complaints about service here. Everyone is on the tows ensuring there shouldn't be any delay.\\nSo, I had a great Holi themed Brunch. Varieties of food but massive traditional dessert preparations bought more colors on my Brunch.\\n\\nDinner Time! I love dinner on weekend specially on Saturday that gives ample time to relax and eat everything on the table. And if I have such an amazing spread like this which offered @courtyardmumbai then it should be an elevating experience.\\nStarting from soup till the dessert I couldn't found even a single dish that was lacking spice.\\nStarting with soup and starter, this time Tomato Shorba was not thick but had spice to it. Chat platter was delicious and the curd used was not at all sour. Rest starters were good how ever I didn't eat Paneer Tikka more cos I had to save space for later course. \\uD83D\\uDE05\\nI loved Punjabi Kadhi though gave a perfect spice along with aloo palak dry sabji. I didn't ordered roti this time I finished everything with plain rice and Biryani.\\nHow can I miss desserts. I specially saved some space to grab those desserts. Balushai was so amazing ditto with Bengali sweet which topped with pomegranate and chocolate cream and dry fruits. Western desserts were good but I love the Indian desserts more.\\nAt last I had fresh lime water to wash it down again it was not sour and bitter. Was rightly made balancing sweetness.\\nAlright, I enjoyed the dinner but being honest what I enjoyed more was main course and Desserts.\\nService was excellent and I never waited so long to get the dish on the table. I never had service issues @courtyardmumbai which made my overall experience more delightful. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=I recently visited Something Fishy and absolutely loved the experience! I tried Surmai Malvani Masala , garlic butter prawns crispy , chicken tikka curry leaves , chicken Ghasi , Neer Dosa and mocktails so The food was incredibly fresh and flavorful — every bite had that perfect coastal touch. The seafood was cooked just right, juicy and well-seasoned, and the presentation made it even more tempting. The ambience was warm, cozy, and had a beautiful ocean-inspired vibe that made the whole dining experience even more relaxing. Soft music, elegant lighting, and a calm atmosphere added the perfect charm to my meal. Overall, it’s a lovely place to enjoy delicious seafood and unwind in a peaceful, beautiful setting. 🐠, name_person=sayama khan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Been to this iconic seafood place yesterday for lunch and we have to say that it was one of a kind experience. Cited on the second floor of legendary Tunga Hotel, Andheri. Something’s fishy is indeed a seafood paradise!
The ambience here is extremely sophisticated and has elegant corners to it.  Perfect for family dinners or even a date.

The food and drinks spread over here is absolutely fabulous! I’m drinks we tried wine (one red and one white) - served perfectly chilled at the right temperature. The wine went really well with the seafood offerings they have on the menu. For the food, in appetisers we tried Lobster chilli garlic which was wok tossed lobster in spicy chilli garlic sauce which were cooked to perfection retaining their juicy texture. The lobster was huge and the portion size was quite generous too. Next up we had butter garlic prawns which was by far one of the best butter garlic prawns we had tried. Absolutely no nonsense recipe and perfect way of making them wherein there was fine chopped onions and garlic sautéed in butter and later prawns tossed in that goodness. We also tried few chicken appetisers like the chicken Alisha kebab which was stuffed chicken kebab having minced chicken and cheese filling in it. The best part of this was that it was cooked perfectly with that dominant Smokey flavour of tandoor which made it even better! Upon our servers recommendation we tried peppery hunan chicken which was mildly spiced and the portion size was humongous! This would easily suffice 3-4 average eaters. It’s a must try if you are here. Lastly, for the mains we had Crab Gassi which was a classic coastal goodness simmered in coconut masala bursting with gold and rich flavours and when paired with neer dosa and appam it was pure heaven. The size of the crab served was big and the crab meat inside it was something out of this world! Loved every single bite of this.
To call it a day, in desserts we tried Rasmalai tres leches which is their signature dessert having layered vanilla cake soaked in rich milk and Rasmalai topped with whipped cream. Absolutely melt in mouth texture and lovely taste! We also tried banoffee tart which was really good. I’m not a fan of banoffee in general however this was nice as the flavour from the banana was not overpowering at all. It was quite subtle and it was delectable.

Hospitality at Something’s fishy is one big reason we would want to come here again and again. Such warm hospitality is super rare these days and here they have nailed it. Captain Bhaskar and steward Ram ensured that we have the best dining experience and recommended some incredible dishes to try as well., name_person=Arjika S}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Had an amazing experience at Something’s Clawy – the seafood festival at Something Fishy, Tunga International!
The festival runs from 20th November to 7th December, and it truly delivers on premium flavours and great hospitality.

We tried several dishes and every one of them stood out:
•	Surmai Slice Tawa Fry – perfectly crispy and super fresh.
•	Crispy Shell Stuffed – crunchy outside, creamy inside. Absolutely delicious.
•	Crab Gassi with Neer Dosa – rich coastal gravy paired with soft neer dosa… the best combo of the night.
•	Lobster Chilly Garlic with Appam, Lobster Cilantro Kalwan, Lobster Lemon Sabayon – each one packed with flavour and cooked perfectly.
•	Dessert: Hot Om-Ali with Malai Kulfi – warm, comforting, and the ideal sweet ending.

Loved the service, ambience, and the fact that every order comes with a complimentary glass of wine.

Overall, a fantastic seafood experience. Highly recommended — especially if you enjoy crabs, lobsters, and unique coastal dishes! 🦀🦞🍷, name_person=Rakesh Poojari}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=One of the best places in Mumbai to enjoy sea food. We had one of the best times till now for sea food here. We tried prawn, Crabs, Pomfret and Kingfish all were fresh and at Par. The staff was supportive and very helful specially  Mr Sunil Bhonsle and Mr Naresh who helped us throughout our dining experience, name_person=HARSH KANTHARIA}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=I recently visited Something’s Fishy in Andheri during their Crab Festival, and the experience was absolutely fantastic. The place attracts people from everywhere for its seafood, and now I know exactly why. I started my meal with their Crab Salad, which was incredibly fresh and full of flavour. The Crab Sweet Chilly Basil soup that followed was hot, comforting, and instantly soothing. Then came the highlight a huge crab that completely blew my taste buds away. Every crab or lobster dish also comes with a complimentary glass of Sula wine, which was a great addition to the meal. I tried both the red and white wines, and they were strong, smooth, and paired beautifully with the seafood.

The Lobster and Crab Hot Pot was rich, warm, and surprisingly addictive. The Lobster Lemon Sabayon was creamy and perfectly balanced. Their Chettinad Crab with Bhakri Tacos was unique, especially with the coconut oil aroma and the crab filling layered on top of the pita-style bread. The Lobster Alleppey Curry was outstanding and had an authentic South Indian flavour that went perfectly with the appam. I also tried their regular appam and neer dosa, both soft and freshly made. The wine by the glass was another nice touch to the overall dining experience.

To finish the meal, I ordered their Triple Chocolate Biscuette, which was absolutely delicious. I also tried their special Baklava, which was rich, sweet, and extremely satisfying. The portion sizes were generous, and the service was quick and attentive. The staff was friendly and helped guide me through their seafood recommendations. Overall, Something’s Fishy is an excellent spot for anyone who loves seafood. The Crab Festival makes it even more worth the visit, and I’m definitely coming back soon., name_person=Akshay Hatiskar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Other, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ ⭐️

reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"Aabhaas Walia\",\"time_line\":\"3 years ago\",\"review\":\"Located at lobby level of The Leela Hotel. It is a beautiful bar with splendid alcoholic drinks. The wine list is impressive. The complimentary snacks are served without a stop. The decor is excellent and so is the ambience.\\nPerfect for a cozy evening.\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"The Glocal Journal\",\"time_line\":\"7 years ago\",\"review\":\"Spanish Affair @TheLeela, Mumbai\\n\\nLeela at Bombay is near the airport road and known to host businessmen. The property's grandeur and usage of plantations to make it a destination for peace in this bustling city.\\n\\nWhen I first read, Spanish food caught my eyes and I thought I had to try it.\\n\\nWe had an evening of wine from Torres and Spanish food by the poolside at Six Degrees.\\n\\nHow was the ambience?\\nIt was a pretty evening with wines flowing, prawns cooking while the sound of fountains soothed & the sight of the poolside pleased\\n\\nWhat did you do?\\n\\nFor vegetarians, we had spinach croquet which was smooth and potato paella . Also, we had mushroom paella. Not to forget the Spanish tradition of having many olives in your meal.\\n\\nWould add, it was heavenly for non vegetarians with Serrano Ham and pequilo peppers and many others flowing. I didn't try it but my friends who had this said this.\\n\\nWe had a cold soup viz Ajio blanc shooters which was weirdly nice. It was really different but tasted good.\\n\\nComing to the wine,\\nTasted the Rose : De Caste which was good in its own way.\\n\\nThen next up, I have hogged onto the desserts.\\n\\nAroz con leche : This was served in a pretty looking jar but didn't taste great.\\nCreme catalana : This was delectable.\\n\\nPolvorones almond cookies : These cookies were soft and crunchy and just nice.\\nWe also tried the Churros. They were made at the time of serving. Chose chocolate and strawberries to go with as the strawberries balanced out the sweetness.\\nThere were pretzels and macaroons too. And not to forget the orange sponge cake which is again a Spanish authenticity.\\n\\nEnded it with,  the chocolate flan.\\n\\nMy Spanish affair ended on a sweet note.\\nIf you are fond of it, go and try it out!\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Everything On A Plate EOAP\",\"time_line\":\"7 years ago\",\"review\":\"The Leela Mumbai is taking its patrons on a culinary journey to Spain and is leaving no stone unturned. Celebrating the flavours of Spain, The Leela has collaborated with Chef Sergio Millet, Executive Chef of Mas Rabell restaurant at the famous Torres vineyards in Spain.\\n\\nTo add to the treat, The House of Torres is pairing with the menu some of its legendary wines ( Mas La Plana, Ibericos Rioja, Gran Coronas, Grans Muralles). What stuck with us the most about the wines, apart from the gorgeous flavours, was that each of them has a wonderful story to tell each explained to us passionately by Tushar.\\n\\nWe had the pleasure to attend one of their Tapas evenings and here\\nare some things that stood out :\\n\\nAjo Blanco\\nWe were quite happy to see this popular cold soup as a starter, especially served as shots! Ajo Blanco is typically made from a mix of bread, almonds, vinegar, olive oil, salt, water and garlic. The drink is very smooth & is quite refreshing, especially in the summer.\\n\\nGambas Pil Pil\\nThe Gambas ( Shrimp ) Pil Pil ( Sauce ) were flying off the stove like hot cakes! Almost everyone took seconds & thirds. Gambas Pil Pil Prawn tossed in a sizzling hot sauce of garlic, chilli & olive oil. Not only was it a delight to watch the chef toss them on the live counter but it was also plated adorably in these tiny little red pots.\\n\\nPan con Tomate with Spicy Tomato Sauce\\nMany say this dish is as humble as tapas can get. The tiny, bite-sized pieces of Spanish toast are a delicious, quick snack made with just five ingredients, namely, bread, tomato, olive oil, garlic, and salt.\\n\\nChicken and Mushroom Paella\\nWe kind of missed this but the others were raving about this dish!\\n\\nThese were just the tip of the iceberg, you must visit to learn more\\nabout the other delicacies on the menu.\\n\\nDesserts\\nFor the most part of the evening, we were hovering around the dessert counter drooling over the desserts on display.\\n\\nChurros\\nWe loved watching the churros being made and gulping them down nice and warm. To add to the delicious brown pastry, we had chocolate sauce, strawberry sauce & Ice cream made in the Leela Kitchen.\\n\\nCr\u00e8me Catalana\\nThe dessert draws parallels with the cr\u00e8me br\u00fbl\u00e9e, the difference being the latter doesn\u2019t contain fine cornflour. The custard was well set and was garnished with fresh fruit, we quite enjoyed it.\\n\\nArroz con Leche\\nPresentation-wise, this stood out the most as it was served in these tiny dessert jars with a dropper full of syrup. The Arroz ( Rice ) con Leche ( Milk ) is basically a Mexican rice pudding and can be a bit bland. Chef Rachna gave it a little extra flavour by adding in some fresh fruits.\\n\\nThere were also Alfajores, Polvorones Almond Cookies, Pretzel Pops, Macaroons, Orange Sponge Cake and more!\\n\\nOur brief visit to the Leela Mumbai Tapas Evening was definitely not enough for us. Crisp papadams, tangy pickles, and steaming hot appams completed the meal, while payasam and other Indian sweets brought the feast to a heavenly close.

Finally managed to get one thing of my bucket list of restaurants which I always wanted to visit. Located at Level 00 like most of the other restaurants at Sahara Star, Namak serves authentic Indian cuisine. Chic ambience, live kitchen, soothing music, lipsmacking food, prompt and courteous service; this sums up our experience at Namak. We preferred the Chef's recommended menu here since it is a three course meal, along with starters, main course and dessert.\\n\\nWe were welcomed with an inaugural drink - a refreshing mix of pineapple juice and mint leaves. Moving to the appetizers, it was a platter of 3 starters - Tandoori Malai Paneer Roll, Chenna Palak Ki Shami and Shimbi Paneer Ki Seekh. All three contain paneer but of all my absolute favourite is Chenna Palak Ki Shami. This Palak with cheese filling kebab literary melts in your mouth, the chef has done a fabulous job by preparing a veg version of this all time favourite kebab. Tandoori Malai Paneer Roll was also brilliant, again Paneer extremely soft and fresh marinated in pickling spices if onion and mint malai cheese grilled in tandoor to perfection. Shimbi Paneer Ki Seekh has a dominant mustard flavour with beans and paneer filing. Loved all the starters.\\n\\nTo go along with food - starters and mains, we called for couple of mocktails - Crimson Tide and Kala Khatta. Now moving to the mains there were three vegetables Khade Masale Ke Paneer, Tripoliya Subzi and Sua Dakhni Saag which is Namak's version of Sarson Da Saag. Of the three I would say Tripoliya Subzi - mix veggies was the best, one of the best I have had in a long time. Signature dish at Namak and a must have at Namak. Sua Dakhni - spinach based veggie gives this amazing smokey taste, which I personally love. This is due to roasted garlic. Again a must try for those who like Sarson Da Saag.\\n\\nAll these veggies were accompanied with the Thikri Dal Makhani, creamy and super yummy! For breads we called for Zaffrani Paratha which is a layered paratha along with tonnes of Saffron in it. Loved this paratha as well, another must try! Post this we ended the mains with Tarkari Biryani served with Raita. Biryani was superb had layers of rice with veggies and spices. Finally moving to dessert we had the signature one Shaad-e-Jamun which is mini jamuna baked and layered with rabdi. A must try dessert, don't miss this for anything.\\n\\nOne of the most memorable experience, one of the most memorable evening, all thanks to Namak Sahara Star. Special thank you to the chef Karan Singh who prepared this delicious meal for us. Also our server Saeed, for being extremely courteous and helpful. A must visit,  especially when celebrating any special occasions with your friends or family. Hope to come back here sooner than later!\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"Great service very tasty food and a soothing ambiance ..... must visit place\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"The biryani had a lovely flavour of spices and the chicken too was cooked well.\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"Nice ambience, polite staff and good quality food being served\",\"guided_block\":{}}"]

Location & ambience
•	Gallops is located inside the Mahalaxmi Race Course in Mumbai, which gives it a uniquely lush, open-green backdrop uncommon in the city’s dining scene.  ￼
•	The décor and setting combine colonial charm with upscale comfort: for example, walnut-floors, candle-light chandeliers, and equestrian-themed décor post-revamp.  ￼
•	Outdoor and al-fresco dining is one of its strong suits — especially nice in cooler months.  ￼

2. Food quality & menu variety
•	The menu successfully blends Indian and Continental dishes. From traditional kebabs and curries to refined European-style mains, there’s something for varied tastes.  ￼
•	Signature dishes that get strong mentions:
•	“Dori Kebab” (mutton or chicken) – minced, skewered and charcoal-cooked.  ￼
•	“Chicken Ala Kiev” with cheese/butter-filled centre, as a refined European choice.  ￼
•	Desserts are also strong: Baked Alaska and newer additions like Baileys Caramel Cloud.  ￼
•	Many reviewers emphasize the generous portions, good presentation and a sense of value for a fine-dining venue.  ￼

3. Service & experience
•	The service is frequently praised: attentive staff, good recommendations (e.g., for wine or pairings), smooth reservation experience when booked in advance.  ￼
•	The overall dining experience is described as memorable— especially when everything aligns (good table, nice view, well-timed service). For example:
“What a wonderful restaurant from the minute we arrived the staff were so efficient and helpful, the food was absolutely incredible.”  ￼

4. Ideal for special occasions / date nights
•	The ambience, décor and location make it ideal for anniversaries, special dinners or when you want to treat yourself. Many mentions of formative visits, nostalgic moments, photo-friendly setting.  ￼

If I were picking one restaurant for a refined Mumbai meal — especially if you’re after something more than just dinner but an experience — Gallops checks a lot of boxes:
•	A setting that feels premium yet relaxed.
•	A menu that offers both familiar Indian comfort and elevated Continental touches.
•	Good enough service to let you focus on the evening rather than logistics.
•	A chance to dine in one of Mumbai’s less-hustle zones (given the race-course setting) while still being accessible.

If you ask me: go for the outdoor or window-view table (book ahead), order one of the signature starters + a main you haven’t tried, and finish with one of the classic desserts. We ordered another starter even before we finished the first one. Same situation no one was taking care,  had to call out the manager. The food was served after waiting for more than 30 mins. And no one showed up with any courtesy to inform the delay.
They lacked professionalism in etiquette on how plates are placed. When food is over how the plates should be removed. The waiter who brought card swiping machine was also struggling to operate it. Overall extremely poor service and lack of professionalism.
FOOD : The Veg platter - was served with 8 pieces of potato, and other options too less. Sheikh kabab also wasn't good. Overall wasn't happy neither with portion nor taste. After this experience we didn't think twice to try for any main course.

I’d like to come here again!, name_person=Ecem Cirak}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=6 days ago, review=Baluchi is a very good restaurant which is inside The Lalit hotel, on the Mumbai airport road. It has a very good ambience. The staff is warm and courteous. We tried their Dal Baluchi, which is actually Dal Makhni which very delicious and had a very authentic taste., name_person=Abhijit JAVADEKAR}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=a year ago, review=I had gone to Baluchi at the Lalit Mumbai for NH 24 Rampur to Lucknow food festival.
The ambience is top class.
The service is just so perfect.
In NH4 Rampur to Lucknow festival there are special delicacies Curated by MasterChef Mohd Taj Qureshi.
The mocktail which I had were Kairi Panna which was just so authentic in taste.
Then had blueberry mint which tasted as required.
Starters were Rampuri Seekh Kebab which was so fantastic.
Also Athishi Suneri Jhinga was so wonderful.
In mains there was
Martaban ka Murgh which was so Flavoursome.
Then Rampuri Haleem which was so authentic.
Then came the Rampuri Gosht Biryani to add on to the amazingness.
The dessert Shahi Tukda ended the meal so well.
The festival is from 21st May to 31st May 2024 for both Lunch and Dinner.
For other details of festival and other menu at Baluchi , lalit Mumbai staff are best people to check with.
Had a wonderful time., name_person=Vaibhavi Shripad Marathe}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Kabab], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_PARKING_LOT], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=If you are looking for luxurious fine dining spot to intrigue some body, close to Mumbai International Airport, Baluchi at The LaLIT is one of the best available spot. 🌺

Baluchi offers signature pan Indian cuisines along with the finest cocktails and mocktails.
To their enticing la carte menu Baluchi has added range of Kebabs & Cocktails 🍹 . Here they offer best of curated veg / non veg traditional frontier kebabs along with the choicest of drinks. 🥂🥃

Walk in and the ambient lighting, wooden furniture, the copper utensils, the decor and artifacts reminds us the warmth of traditional hospitality of India. 🇮🇳
We visited Baluchi on rainy Thursday amidst unusually heavy traffic. However, the ambiance, the live combination of ghazal and tabla had a quick soothing effect uplifting our mood to begin our Kebabs & Cocktails experience.

The waiter started serving the different kebabs and chef kept on explaining the minute preparatory notes. The aroma was tempting and we started gobbling the kebabs. All were delicious, loaded with flavor and innovative in taste. Being a Konkani, I loved the Konkani tawa fish. 🐠

There are large options of mocktails and cocktails to choose from. We tried four and to our surprise all were unique in taste and presentation. Lazeez Sangria was the unanimous favorite among us.
The services is exceptionally better than the world standards. Staff were courteous, polite, respectful and professional.
An ideal date or business meeting venue. 🎯, name_person=Munawar Karbelkar}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=North Indian food lovers don’t miss out on this place
This is a Must try !! Though the prices are on a bit higher side but it’s worth.A special thanks to chef Qureshi for the amazing preparations.Will definitely visit again. The ambience is excellent as well. Do try it once. If you wish to have some special dish I would recommend you to preorder it as it is out of stock sometimes., name_person=saurav verma}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=a year ago, review=NH24 Rampur to Lucknow Food Festival at Baluchi, The Lalit Mumbai

What I Tried:
Drinks:
Kairi Panna (Mocktail) - Authentic and delicious!
Blueberry Mint (Mocktail) - Refreshing and perfectly balanced.

Starters:
Rampuri Seekh Kebab - Fantastic flavors, a must-try!
Atishi Suneri Jhinga - These prawns were absolutely wonderful.

Mains:
Martaban ka Murgh - Packed with flavor, a true delight.
Rampuri Haleem - Authentic and melt-in-your-mouth good.
Rampuri Gosht Biryani - Elevated the meal to another level!

Dessert:
Shahi Tukda - The perfect sweet ending to a phenomenal meal.

Ambience: Top-notch. Classy and elegant, perfect for a special occasion. ✨

Service: Impeccable. Attentive staff and interactions with Chef Mohd Taj Qureshi himself!  ‍

Must-Try:Absolutely everything! The menu curated by MasterChef Mohd Taj Qureshi is a flavor explosion. Don't miss the Rampuri Seekh Kebab and Rampuri Gosht Biryani!

This is a limited-time food festival running from May 21st to May 31st, 2024, for both lunch and dinner.
The Lalit Mumbai staff are incredibly knowledgeable about the festival menu and can answer any questions you have., name_person=shripad marathe}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=One-line headline – Drooling Goan Cuisine Comes Alive with Susegado Mumbai food festival at The Lalit.

Xacutti. Recheado. Xeque xeque. Ambot tik. Feijoada. Sorpotel. Never before would you have been so semantically food stumped. Amidst the whiff of coconut, the hiss of an oven and the sizzle in a wok, The Lalit Hotels prime restaurant Baluchi is faltering with inflexion and diphthong of typical Goan dishes. It’s time to feast with the array of the Goa’s culturally rich cuisine carefully curated by Executive Chef Tanmoy Majumdar (and his team). Believe me the visit will surely be etched out as a fond memory for a lifetime.
Minute detailing has been kept in mind. The ambiance has been revamped to get the Goan beach feel. Vintage wine bottles adorn the stacks to enhance the Goan backdrops. Famous Goan melodies play in the backdrop.
You are welcomed and garlanded with a beautiful creative sea-shell neckpiece (unlike a floral garland). And yes, this is a keep-sake memory from the stables the Lalit Hotels group for you. Such subtle gestures speak volumes of the Limitless Hospitality of The Lalit Suri Hospitality Group.
Kudos to Mr. Keshav Suri, Executive Director - The Lalit Suri Hospitality Group, to come up with this enticing brainwave / Concept of Executive Chef Pop-up to cross-promote Executive Chefs and bring to life the various flavours of India in their hotel properties. The buzz is strong that the group has an amazing line-up of never-done before food festivals. The Susegado Mumbai food festival at The Lalit will be on from 21st to 30th July 2018. Make sure you experience the true unmatched and scintillating flavours., name_person=Aryeman Raj}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Atmosphere of this cool and food, service of the staff are good}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Tasty food quality of food was nice , chicken panner tikka super yummy tasty....}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=I highly recommend this place for its taste and variety of dishes.}"]

Do visit., name_person=GVPIXELS}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=11 months ago, review=A Fusion of Flavors Across Italian, Chinese, and Indian Cuisines**

Located in the heart of the city, this restaurant brings together a surprising yet delightful blend of Italian, Chinese, and Indian dishes. From the first bite to the last, the meal was an exciting journey through diverse culinary traditions.

We started our meal with Orange Basil Mojito which was very refreshing.
Then in starters we had **Honey Chilli Potato** and **Mexican Gol Gappa**. The honey chilli potato was crispy and sweet, with a tangy kick that paired wonderfully with the lightness of the dish. The texture was spot-on, offering a satisfying crunch with each bite. The **Mexican Gol Gappa**, however, was an unexpected fusion—crispy puffs filled with zesty, spiced water and vibrant toppings that carried a perfect balance of heat and tang, bringing a fresh twist to the traditional Mexican snack.

For the main course, we opted for a **Pizza Quattro Staggioni and **Pesto Gnocchi**.
The pizza was generously topped with fresh vegetables and a rich tomato sauce, the crust perfectly thin and crispy. A classic done right, it was a comforting choice. The **Pesto Gnocchi**, on the other hand, was the real standout—pillowy-soft gnocchi coated in a fragrant, flavorful pesto sauce that wasn’t too overpowering. The dish struck the perfect balance of freshness and richness.

To finish the meal, we indulged in the **Lotus Biscoff Cheesecake** for dessert along with St.Patrick’s Irish coffee.
This was the highlight of the meal—smooth and creamy, with just the right amount of sweetness and that unmistakable caramelized crunch from the Biscoff biscuits. It was a decadent ending to a truly satisfying meal.

Overall,Whether you’re in the mood for something comforting like pizza, or looking to try something innovative like the fusion gol gappa, there’s no shortage of options to please your taste buds. Totally disappointed with the food quality, variety, and staff behavior. Except for the sushi, none of the dishes were good. Veg and non-veg starters, main course, and desserts were all below average. The desserts, especially cakes, were not fresh at all.

We decided to try the widespread buffet here that brings the streets of Asia to your plate!

Started off with a warm bowl of comfort — Manchow Veg Soup as well as the rich and hearty Eight Treasure Chicken Soup.

For dumplings there were two options, Chicken and Straw Mushroom Siu Mai Dumplings and Vegetable Basil dumpling with both steamed to perfection. We loved the non vegetarian option more and ended up ordering it twice.

The Prawns Tempura Sushi was also quite devouring and had the perfect balance.

There were two types in chilli appetizers, Jiang’s Chilli Cottage Cheese and Sriracha Chilli Chicken, bringing bold spices to every bite. We enjoyed the Cottage Cheese more here.

Crispy on the outside, tender within, the Salt & Pepper Turnip Cakes were also quite yum.

Fish in Soy Chilli Garlic, this was really delectable and enjoyable till the very last bite.

For mains, we had Chicken Hakka Noodles, Chicken Burnt Garlic Rice, Spicy Clay Pot Chicken, Fish in Hot Basil Sauce & Japanese Yellow Curry with shrimp. Both the rice and noodles were fine with spicy clay pot chicken being the pick.

For desserts, we had Daarsan with almond flakes, Hot Chocolate Rolls, Brownies and Ice Cream.

We also tried their add on mocktails such as Bali's Tropical, Peach Blossom and the classic Mojito.

So much flavour. So many favourites. This was a all in one buffet and we loved everything we had here. The staff was also quite courteous and helpful. The perfect place to hangout for your big family dinner or even with friends. Attended us very well and very professionally.
I recommend the Lvel special bang bang chicken, it’s an alternate for chicken popcorn, but much better infact.
Veg spring roll had 8 pieces in a plate, and we over ordered as whatever we ordered the quantity was much greater than expected.
The LIIT taste was very good.

The vibe was very good as well.
They have a beautiful rooftop, but since we went around 3pm, it was hot, so we didn’t sit upstairs.
Additionally, we made our booking on Swiggy Dineout where we got 50% off. And they made no issue out of it. The drinks were covered as well. And there was no separate over priced menu for Zomato or Swiggy booking.

Overall an amazing experience.
We were 5 people, bill was 6800, to which got 50% discount.

Note - 3 of us were vegetarian, and they too liked the food.

Totally worth it.
Am sure the vibe at night is even better.
Highly recommend, I myself will visit again., name_person=RUDRA PRATAP PRAMANIK}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Chicken_Crispy], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=This place is just a 10-minute walk from Sakinaka Metro. reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"anurag kasbe\",\"time_line\":\"a year ago\",\"review\":\"A Culinary Delight at Janata Lunch Home\\n\\nLast night, I had the pleasure of dining at Janata Lunch Home, and I must say, it was an experience to remember. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted with warmth and hospitality, setting the tone for a delightful evening ahead.\\n\\nThe standout dish of the night was the Squid, prepared in authentic South Indian style. The tender, succulent pieces were bursting with flavor, perfectly complemented by the aromatic spices. It was a true gastronomic delight.\\n\\nEqually impressive was the Surmai Tawa Fry, showcasing the freshest catch expertly cooked to crispy perfection. Each bite was a symphony of flavors, leaving me craving for more.\\n\\nThe Neer Dosa, a traditional coastal delicacy, was a revelation. Its delicate texture and subtle taste provided the ideal canvas for savoring the accompanying dishes.\\n\\nAnd who could forget the Prawns Gassi? This coconut-based curry was rich, creamy, and packed with the tantalizing flavors of the sea. It paired beautifully with steamed rice, creating a heavenly combination that left me utterly satisfied.\\n\\nNot only was the food exceptional, but the service was impeccable.
