["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner}, time_line=a month ago, review=⭐ 1/5
Extremely Disappointed with the Food Quality

I’m genuinely shocked by today’s experience at Malhaar Restaurant.

I had ordered from Zomato , the Veg Kofta was utterly bizarre and it had tutti frutti and cherries in it! Who puts dessert ingredients in a savoury kofta? It felt to me like the chef got confused between making a sweet dish and a main course. I paid ~₹450 for what tasted like a bland, uninspired dessert -definitely not a proper kofta!

The Hyderabadi Chicken too was devoid of flavour, lacking any authentic taste or spice balance. Overall, both dishes were pathetic and not worth the money.

What’s even more disappointing is that this isn’t the first time the quality has dropped. During our previous visit last month, the Manchow Soup we ordered was also far below expectations : watery, poorly seasoned, and lacking the usual flavour punch we associate with Malhaar. The soup wasn't simmered properly.

We’ve been regular customers and always appreciated the food before, but after today’s experience, I’m seriously skeptical about ever ordering from Malhaar again., name_person=Laxmi Patel}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=This place is heaven for South Indian seafood lovers! The fish was fresh and the marination was just perfect. We ordered the Tandoori Pomfret, Stuffed Bombil, Prawns Ghee Roast and Neer Dosa. All the items were damn good. The service was also good. They provide valet parking., name_person=Siddhali Dhuri}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=The food's great n the service is also amazing, but the owner's daughter is really mean to me 😞, name_person=Agnel Varghese}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=Nostalgia for the place and the love for sea food!
Ambience - The place has transformed from a shady bar to a classy place with great ambience. The new colors give a very happy feeling to the place.
Food - I have been going to the place for the past 10 years, even before writing reviews was not a thing. Frankly the restaurant was not that impressive but in the past year they have undergone a major reform and ohh boy they nailed it! Malhaar has entered the scene as a sea food specialist and with a bang. The food is simply great! We were served by the Shrimp Man, who has been working at the place for 16 years now. I would suggest to go with what he suggests as the menu is pretty diverse with a lot of cuisines.
Service - They have a good staff and service will be quick with the food. The bar service is slow for the cocktails so order well in advance for the next round.

Highly recommended for a casual night out., name_person=Yuvraj Modi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Potato_Wedges, Chicken_Wings], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=10 months ago, review=Gateway Taproom in Bandra BKC is an aesthetic spot, perfect for unwinding with loved ones or enjoying a vibrant atmosphere. It's a must-visit for beer enthusiasts, offering a variety of beers to try, especially after a hectic day. The “Gateway to Istanbul” menu is a standout, featuring refreshing cocktails like the Bitter Orange Cranberry Treat and Citrus Black, both unique in presentation and flavor. We loved the taste of these cocktails!

The food experience was also exceptional. The chicken doner was absolutely mind-blowing, and the spiced chicken wings hit the spot. But it was the roasted beetroot and kumpir (a baked potato dish) that really surprised us with their unique flavors. The overall vibe was cozy, and the staff was attentive, guiding us through the menu with excellent service. We ended our meal with a delightful pistachio and puff baklava dessert that was nothing short of mouthwatering.

Overall, a perfect spot to relax, enjoy good drinks, great food, and a chill ambiance. We give it a 10/10 for a fantastic dining experience. Highly recommend it for cocktail and beer lovers!, name_person=amin shaikh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=10 months ago, review=Located in Bandra Kurla Complex, this place has an exquisite ambience and some really tasty food. The staff was also quite courteous and their recommendations were pretty awesome. They are offering a special culinary experience with their Gateway to Istanbul menu, so don't forget to check that out.

Taking you through some of the dishes we had:

Crispy Chickpeas Over Hummus (Recommended)

The all-time favorite hummus with crispy chickpeas placed over it and served with pita bread. The combination was absolutely yum.

Chicken Doner (Recommended)

Pita pocket filled with Turkish chicken and salad in garlic sause. This was really devouring and we relished every bite. It was served with fries that were too good as well.

MaC n Cheese Balls

Crispy coated crunchy balls filled with mac n cheese that has a rich and creamy flavour. Quite satisfying and a more comfort food.

Fish N Chips

Golden battered fish perfectly fried and served with tangy tartar sauce. The quantity is amazing for a small plate and it's served with really delicious fries.

Pistachio & Puff Baklava

Puff Baklava filled with crushed pistachio that is really sweet and served with whipped cream on top. Have your sugar tooth activated for this one.

For mocktails, we had Cold Coffee & Summer Cosmopolitan which was a mixture of apple, rasberry and cranberry.

Overall, we had a spectacular experience and loved everything about Gateway Taproom. It's a wonderful place to come for a date night or even have a meeting over lunch. We made a special request for the Hummus & Chicken Doner to be a part of their permanent menu, hopefully they oblige. Mojito was nice. Crispy Sichuan chicken, fried prawns, chilly paneer, peanut chaat, nachos, chicken wings were delicious!!
Butter chicken was yum!
The chocolate cake with gajar halwa and icecream was soo good!!
Great place, definitely coming back here!, name_person=Nishad lad}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Craftbar is located off BKC in Bandra East and it is accurately available on Google Maps hence easy to find. Their other outlet is in Andheri East.

The restaurant is spacious with nice sound system, a projector screen, a finely lit bar and multiple seatings for all type of groups. They have not invested much in the ambiance however the feel is nice.

They specialise in a multi cuisine menu and the options are great. Dishes are nicely balanced for both vegetarians and non vegetarians. Prices are at par with similar type of brands amd the best part is the offers on drinks. On a daily basis they have kept different offers so do check those before visiting.

I went here for dinner and the kitchen service was quick and the table service by staff Jeevan was good.

What We Had -
APPETIZERS~
Kashmiri Paneer Tikka -
Fresh paneer with coriander and green base tasted decent. The spice rub lacked the zing and I felt less time was given to tandoor. Hence minor improvements needed.

Devil's Chicken Chilli -
Looked fiery but tasted great. Juicy chiken chunks with bell peppers and onions with garlic and red chilli base tasted delicious. Loved the bold flavours which were not too strong.

Butter Garlic Prawns -
One word perfect. Fresh prawns with bell peppers and onions and base as butter garlic tasted outstanding. Loved the juicy prawns and the butter didn't left any sweet after taste plus flavours from the garlic was spot on.

MAINS~
Desi Style Triple Rice (Chicken)-
A perfect craving buster for a Chinese lover like me. Loved the rice, gravy and the egg on the top. Deliciously tasty as everything about this dish was amazing.

DESSERTS~
English Vinglish -
A fusion of chocolate brownie with gajar ka halwa. Looked stunning tasted great. Loved eating every bit of this.

MOCKTAILS~
Fruit Punch.
Citrus Cooler.
Both the mocktails were refreshing with perfect flavours.

So our dinner at Craftbar BKC was a great meal as everything from food, service to music was amazing. Therefore a must visit but do check their offers., name_person=Shaikh Khalid Sarfaraz}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=Craftbar BKC delivers an exceptional dining experience, deserving a solid 5-star review. The Beetroot Tikki was a standout, with its earthy flavors beautifully complemented by just the right amount of spice.

The Devil’s Chicken Chilli lived up to its name, delivering a fiery kick that left us craving more. Chicken Kulfi was a surprising highlight, with tender, juicy chicken infused with aromatic spices, creating a dish that melted in the mouth. Finally, the English Winglish dessert was the perfect end to the meal—a sweet, indulgent treat that balanced the savory dishes perfectly. Each dish was presented with care, and the flavors were spot on, making Craftbar BKC a must-visit for any food lover., name_person=Prathmesh Todkar}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Saturdays only The live music band is just amazing. 8/12 is my parents anniversary and exactly a year ago we arrived at Nara only to be turned away due to a staff party. One more attempt in between and it was fully booked.

This time i had booked the table only to be sure to have a table. There is outdoor seating too.

The hostess quick in finding our reservation and within seconds we were ushered into the restaurant and offered to choose our table which was a big plus as some places designate tables. The ambience was welcoming and elegant.

Our server Leishi arrived at our table with greetings and a smile to ask if we were comfortable. Within minutes, we had the menus in our hands and as usual i turned to our server, Leishi for recommendations. I never thought we’d end up having a five course dinner here. The recommendations offered by her were all worth a try. Although, the crispy lotus root starter that we wanted was sold out, we were happy choosing the crispy tofu dish instead. The thai ice tea was also unavailable. We chose a thai bubble tea instead. Do ask them to make a dish less spicy, not everyone can handle that kinda thai heat. Our soup, salad and starters arrived fairly quickly and were served well by Leishi. The chicken starter was a fantastic recommendation. The smoky flavour was also a bit like parmesan somehow and it was perfectly cooked.

For the mains, as recommended, we went for the house speciality, green curry with jasmine rice. For me, i got a chicken side dish to go with an extra portion of jasmine rice. I was full but something about the dish made me finish it to the last bit. It was delicious to say the least.

Time for dessert and we thought of skipping it because we were so full! But no! Lets get the sweet potato icecream with sticky rice. 2 scoops resting on sticky rice with some garnish. All gone in minutes. Well recommended by another server.

All in all, we had 5 courses we never thought we’d have. The food was truly authentic with great presentation elevated by some great service. I was very happy at the end.

I will return to try out the unavailable items and many more. Though, I would be on the lookout for some dine-out discounts on swiggy/zomato.

A big thanks to Leishi and other staff that interacted with us. Your warmth and smiles truly made our (parent’s) anniversary dinner exxtra special.

This one will be remembered.
We will return., name_person=Darsh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Went here to get lunch with a friend. ["{guided_block={}, time_line=Edited 7 years ago, review=Sofitel Wine Days are back! This is held on a monthly basis at The Sofitel Mumbai BKC and I was lucky to be a part of one at Le Bar Diamantaire, located at lobbey level next to Pondicherry Cafe!

A sit down multi course Italian meal with Italian wine is what you witness! An experience unparalleled. Sofitel has always been my one of the most favourite places in Mumbai because of the numerous festivals they do. But the food tried at this event was one of the best that I have ever had!

Every course had its own wine, started with couple of white and finishing with couple of red! All the wines had been specially curated and imported and the food also complemented really well. You have Veg as well as Non Veg options, so one can choose accordingly. Talking about what all I tried at Sofitel Wine Days -

We began with Almond and Goat Cheese as Starters, had Zucchini, Avocado and Mustard Sauce. The non veg equivalent to this was Amaranth Prawns. This was served with the first wine of the evening - Villa Antinori Bianco - white wine. A perfect way to begin your meal! The wine aims at maximizing the Tuscan character of the wine and is straw yellow in colour with greenish highlights. It is still wine with approx 12% alcohol by volume.

Next in line we tried the Forest Mushroom Veloute which was Truffle Mousse, Pine nuts and brioche. Absolutely awesome and I loved the taste! Texture was thick and rich in flavour and aroma. This was served with the second white wine of the evening - Antinori Santa Cristina Pinot Grigio. The wine is straw yellow in colour, the wine offers fruity and delicate aromas of pineapple, green apples and lemon. The wine is refreshing and has approx 12% alcohol by volume.

Moving to the mains - we first had the Baked Courgette which was Duxelle, Edamame and Parmesan Risotto! Again an awesome dish for Mushroom lovers. This was served along with the first red wine of the evening - Antinori Santa Cristina Toscana. For non vegetarians there was Grilled Seabass (Risotto). Wine is a red wine from Toscana, Italy and has approx 12.5% alcohol by volume.

Next main dish was Grilled Polenta which had red lentil ragout, charred leek, fondant potato and caramlised onion straw! A filling dish and really good! I preferred Polenta more than Baked Courgette! This one was served along with Antinori Peppoli Chianti Classico, the last wine / 2nd red wine of the evening. Non veg equivalent was Braised Lamb Shank with same ingredients. The wine represents the Chianti Classico territory and it's historic grape variety with typical floral and fruity aromas. Wine has approx 13% alcohol by volume.

We ended our meal with one of the most amazing desserts - Berry Trail. It had Raspberry Parfait, Blueberry Jelly, Blackberry Chantilly, Oats Crumble and Berry Chocolate Crisps. One of the best dessert that I have had till date! Simply awesome.

In complete awe of the experience at Sofitel Mumbai BKC! As mentioned earlier, they keep doing #sofitelwinedays often, almost every month and I would highly recommend everyone including all wine connoisseurs!, name_person=Jatin Shah}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=Sofitel BKC  has been our favourite hub to enjoy some family times , thanks to their Festivals which they organise with great enthusiasm .

Lastly Not to Forget the Red Beauty ie Ferrari standing at the door step of the Sofitel.

Let's straight move on to what all we savoured out here during our visit .

Appetizers :

Bruschetta :
An amazing start to a classy evening . Crisp bread with luscious Topping ....

Hot balls having a Scrummy peas based stuffing .

Boiled Cornmeal served with a tasty mushrooms preparation served along side .

Lasagna :
Again a super delicious dish straight from the treasure box of chef special delicacy of the outlet .

We went for our all time favourite classic Mocktails during our visit . Mojito ,  Shikanji and Blue Curacao were amongst the Favourites .

Tiramisu :

Highly recommended, name_person=Rei Kudukar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Hitchki in BKC is hands down one of the best and most vibrant places we’ve visited recently. Coming to the food and drinks—we had a delightful experience trying their curated menu:

🍸 Cocktails:

Dum Maro Dum – This drink is an absolute showstopper! The combination of vodka, cranberry, and pineapple juice, blended with that signature smoky dhuaan, makes it not only taste divine but also look dramatic when served. Refreshing, tangy, and smooth—it’s perfect for setting the evening mood.

Hara Bhara Karo – A creative take on the classic hara bhara kebab! Served with a green pea mush and crisp tikki topped with wasabi mitti mayo, every bite felt wholesome yet innovative. The hint of wasabi gave it a refreshing punch.

Dabeli Kachori – An absolute treat! This fusion snack is stuffed with dabeli masala and served with a tangy kala khatta salsa. The crisp outer shell with the spicy, tangy filling inside is comfort food with a twist—something you rarely find elsewhere.

Paneer Lazeez – Creamy malai paneer cooked with bell peppers and onions in a rich, aromatic curry. The paneer was soft and melt-in-mouth, perfectly paired with the cheese garlic naan which added that extra indulgence.

Veg Kolhapuri – A fiery and flavorful dish with perfectly cooked mixed vegetables in traditional Kolhapuri masala. This was a perfect balance to the Paneer Lazezz, bringing spice and zest to the table. We enjoyed it with butter naan, which complemented the richness of the curry beautifully.

Black Friday – The grand finale! A heavenly dessert crafted with Black Forest pastry, layers of dark and white chocolate mousse, and topped with cherry gel. Every spoonful was rich, smooth, and indulgent, leaving us with the sweetest memory of the evening.

Unfortunately, this turned out to be one of the most underwhelming buffet dinners we’ve had in a long time.

To begin with, the vegetarian selection was extremely limited, which itself was disappointing for a premium luxury hotel. What made it worse was that several items had already run out by around 9:30–10 PM, which is surprisingly early for a dinner buffet. The veg sushi, in particular, was tucked away inside the refrigerator with no proper labelling or indication—it genuinely felt like a game of hide-and-seek unless you already knew where to look.

We were excited to try the chaat and gol gappas (puchkas), but this was hands down the worst part of the experience. The chaat was served cold, soggy, and overly sweet, even after we specifically requested mild spice. The gol gappas were shockingly plain—filled only with boondi and nothing else, completely missing the usual exciting mix of chutneys, potatoes, or flavours.

The Indian vegetarian main course was mediocre at best, lacking both variety and flavour. The only true highlight from the Indian section was the freshly made garlic naan, which was genuinely good. The hot dim sum station was another pleasant surprise, as those were freshly cooked and nicely done.

A special mention must be made of the pancake counter—the lady handling it was warm and sweet, and the fact that the pancakes were eggless won us over completely. Though pancakes aren’t a typical dinner or dessert item, this ended up being the most enjoyable part of our meal.

Service suffered due to severe understaffing. The staff, though polite, seemed unsure of menu details themselves, and the small dining arena with closly sat tables, which further affected the overall experience.

Overall, this dinner experience was a 5/10 at best. As Accor Gold members who genuinely love Accor properties, this was by far one of the most disappointing dining experiences we’ve had in recent times. Sadly, we wouldn’t recommend Pondicherry Café for vegetarian diners and do not see ourselves returning anytime soon.

P.S: Not adding any photos as the experience was not as exciting to capture into images!, name_person=Kunal Shah}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Would not recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Paid_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_PAID_PARKING_LOT], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION, Clearly_labelled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=Edited a year ago, review=Restaurant Review: Pondicherry Café - Sofitel, Mumbai

I recently visited Pondicherry Café at Sofitel in Mumbai, and unfortunately, the experience fell far below expectations. Here’s a detailed breakdown of my visit:

Parking Hassle

As someone who arrived on a motorbike, the experience began with a significant disappointment. The hotel does not provide motorbike parking within its premises. Instead, I was directed to a pay-and-park lot 300 meters away, located on an open ground opposite Jio International School. This parking area was poorly maintained and inconvenient, especially for those with huge bikes like mine. I had to leave my bike without a handle locked, which was unsettling.

Walking from the parking lot to the hotel in the scorching sun further diminished the experience. For a luxury hotel, this lack of accommodation for bikers is surprising and disheartening.

Ambience and Atmosphere

Once inside, the ambience of Pondicherry Café was pleasant but lacked any accompanying music, which made it feel somewhat lifeless. The décor was appealing, but the overall atmosphere could use some warmth and vibrance to match the expectations of a premium dining experience.

Buffet Experience

We opted for the buffet based on its promising menu, but the food did not deliver in terms of taste. While there was a variety of options available, very few stood out. Here’s a breakdown of the meal:
•	Soup: 2/5 – Bland and unremarkable.
•	Starters: 3/5 – Only two items were decent; the rest were forgettable.
•	Main Course: 2/5 – A disappointing selection with subpar flavors.
•	Desserts: 2/5 – Average at best. The pista kulfi had an odd paan flavor, which didn’t appeal to me.
•	Pizza & Pasta: Possibly the worst I’ve ever had.

Overall, the food lacked flavor and quality, especially considering the premium pricing.

Service

The service was another letdown. Staff were hard to find when needed, whether it was for cutlery or water. This lack of attentiveness added to the frustration and further detracted from the overall dining experience.

Final Thoughts

For a restaurant within a luxury hotel, Pondicherry Café failed to meet expectations on multiple fronts. The motorbike parking issue, coupled with an underwhelming dining experience, made this visit quite disappointing. Considering the high ratings this restaurant holds on platforms like Zomato and Google, I feel it is overrated.

Recommendation:
•	For Bikers: Avoid this place if you value convenience and proper parking facilities.
•	For Food Lovers: There are far better dining options in the BKC area offering superior taste, service, and overall experience at similar or lower price points.

Overall Rating:
•	Ambience: 3/5
•	Food Taste: 2/5
•	Service: 2/5
•	Value for Money: 1/5

I highly recommend Maya for anyone looking to indulge in an exceptional dining experience!\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":4}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Madhur Gupta\",\"time_line\":\"Edited 4 years ago\",\"review\":\"Extremely expensive food which is overly spicy and all this served by a seemingly inexperienced staff.\\nWent there as a party of 24 for a very special occasion.\\nThe hotel looks great with a huge chandelier and fresh lilies in the middle of the lobby.\\nThe restaurant looked promising but we were in for a letdown.\\nStarted with tomato shorba which was good and everything went downhill after that.\\nHad chicken and prawns in appetizers which were okay but the main course was a HUGE disappointment.\\nThe dessert are also very mediocre.\\nWe wanted to talk to the chef who instead of accepting his fault started defending himself.\\nWill not miss going there.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\"}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Chandra Sekhar Deepala\",\"time_line\":\"3 years ago\",\"review\":\"A little expensive restaurant for the quality quantity and ambience. The reception and waiters were so respectful and the hospitality was more than expected. I ordered from the menu and changed my mind. They did not mind the change of decision and immediately communicated with the chef. Complimentary Papad (Snacks) looks amazing. Papad tasted okay. I ordered Butter Garlic Naan (Bread) and Gongura Mamsam (Tender Goat with Sour Greens). Garlic bread looks amazing and tastes buttery and the texture was perfect. Gongura Mamsam looked good/okay but the taste was perfectly amazing (Gongura tastes little sour) Goat was tender and delicate. It tastes perfect with the exact flavour. Food was good but not 5 star hotel level great especially given the price. \u20b95000 for two people with no alcohol, 1 appetizer, 1 main course, couple of breads and mocktails\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\"}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Moumita S\",\"time_line\":\"6 years ago\",\"review\":\"Maya  is elegant with excellence in true sense\\nBeautiful Indian cuisine restaurant in Trident BKC, means luxury & best in the hospitality industry ..\\n\\nSpacious restaurant with beautiful sculptures displayed, a beautifully beaded curtain in the entrance..\\nThe restaurant Interior is dominated by three basic classic colours - Red Black White\\n\\nMaya, Trident BKC\\nOne of the most renowned Award winning restaurant of Trident, Bandra Kurla, Mumbai\\nFamous 5 star hotel in BKC\\nMe & My Parsi family attended\\nNavroz Food Festival (7th-18th of Aug)\\nChef & his team\\nManagement Team of the prestigious Luxury property\\nWe're thankful for your warm welcome\\uD83D\\uDE4F\\nAmazing cocktails mocktails wines\\n3 course lovely authentic Parsi meal..\\nThe best feeling is, of having good tasty authentic Parsi food in a lovely place called Maya\\n\\nMuktads started on 7th of August\\n\\nMuktads are of 10 days duration.\\nAccording to Zoroastrian tradition, it's a special religious part of their culture..\\n\\nThe Muktad days are also known Farvardegan, which means \\\"days of remembering the Fravashis.\u201d\\n\\nEvery creation \u2013 spiritual or material \u2013 has a Fravashi. Human beings have individual Fravashis as their Guardian spirits.\\n\\nMuktad is a joyous and festive occasion to welcome and be hospitable to the Fravashis.\\n\\nMuktad are the days of enhancing communication between the physical and spiritual worlds.\\n\\nThe simple ritual would be to light a divo/candle, place a bunch of flowers & some sweets\\n\\nAfter this period Navroz, The Parsi New Year is celebrated..\\n\\nMaya\u2014the Indian speciality restaurant at Trident Bandra Kurla, is celebrating the auspicious Parsi New Year with a specially curated festive \u2018Parsi Bhonu\u2019 menu over lunch and dinner daily.\\n\\nYes, lavish traditional menu prepared with an experienced team of Chefs of Maya, in the guidance of Chef Angad\\n\\nI should mention, food is cooked so well, with acute amount of spices, nothing is too much used while preparing, easy to digest..\\n\\nTo preserve the cultural and culinary specialities of the Parsis, the Navroz Special \u2018Parsi Bhuno\u2019 features delicacies like Chicken Farcha, Kolmino Patia, Mutton Berry Pulav, Saas Ni Macchi, Papetay Ma Gosht, Parsi Mutton Kebabs, Patra Ni Macchi, Khaman Pattie Main, Salli Boti, Dhansak, Lagan Nu Custard and much more\u2026\\n\\nIn this Chef's curated a la carte menu, the best & popular Parsi delicacies are included ..\\n\\nVery organised & helpful staffs.\\nWheel chair accessible..\\nClean & hygienic..\\nAll the 5 star facilities are available here..\\n\\nEnjoy Navroz with good food in a good place..\\nINR 2000+ taxes per person (drinks are extra)\\n\\nFood Presentation Service Ambiance Satisfaction - all get 10/10\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Mayank Ajay\",\"time_line\":\"a year ago\",\"review\":\"Maya Restaurant in Trident BKC Mumbai  truly excels in delivering exceptional food quality that tantalizes the taste buds with every bite. Chef Swanand Thipsay's meticulous attention to detail and Manager Yash's impeccable service instructions truly elevated our dining experience at Maya Restaurant. Let’s begin with what truly matters: the experience.

From the moment we walked in, there was a sense of genuine hospitality. The chef personally interacted with guests, and the team was attentive without being intrusive—hallmarks of a well-trained hospitality crew that truly understands service. There was care in every detail, from the way the dishes were plated to how staff ensured dietary preferences were catered to proactively.

Located in an industrial lane, this restaurant has amazing vibrant vibes. They curate unique and innovative cocktails by their excellent skilled bartenders. The food is no doubt, Delicious !!! You get to choose on Indian, Regional, Italian, Mexican, Middle Eastern & more such cuisines. My personal favourite was the mango menu and from that was the mango cheese cake. The food is really too good and absolutely yummy. Loved this place and the vibe., name_person=Jayesh Tiwari}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=7 months ago, review=What’s Your Plan is located in Sakinaka and it is behind the famous McDonalds and you have ample parking space available.

It might sound cliché, but this is the first time I’m genuinely using the term hidden gem — this place truly surprised me with how good it was in every aspect.

The restaurant is spacious with two different sections being available. One is AC with high chair seatings and a bar plus DJ space too and the other is Non AC causal seatings with pool table in the center and a nice bar. Loved the use of the space and the wall designs as it looked really happening. Currently as IPL is going on they have decorated the Non AC section with team flags and have kept a big screen too.

The menu here is vast and they have options available in Indian, Asian, Italian and some more cuisines. Right now they have added a limited edition mango menu too. Apart from this they have various offers in food and drinks specially for big groups for IPL season. Prices are at par with similar type of brands and the quantity served is good.

Went here on a Monday dinner and the kitchen service was on time and table service by staff Mantu was great as he was polite and knew the menu well.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Jamaican Jerk Spice Chicken Tikka -
Served in a unique way as hanging skewers in the Dubai frame. Served with buttery naan, onion and green chutney this was juicy chicken tikkas done in green Jamaican spices. Loved the taste of this as it was not the regular tikka and the spices had nice hint of hotness to it.

Genkai Prawns Maki Roll -
Surprisingly a very nice and tasty sushi served. Fresh prawns rolled nicely with rice and the crunchy tempura coating with spicy sauce tasted excellent. Loved everything about this sushi as it was bang on tasty.

MAINS~
Mushroom & Truffle Cream Cheese Flatbread -
Thin base topped with generous amount of cheese, mushrooms, red chillies, cream cheese and sprayed with aromatic and earthy truffle oil looked perfect and tasted delicious. Loved the juicy mushrooms and the cream cheese and they were honest in using the truffle oil hence a perfect dish again.

Nasi Goreng -
This was a complete miss for me as it was way different from the Nasi Goreng that I have been eating for years. Maybe it is their way as I felt it was a plain normal fried rice however being fried rice it tasted nice but for Nasi Goreng they need to check the recipe.

DESSERT~
Mango Cheesecake -
Again a very different version of cheesecake as this was more closer to a baked layered malai cake with mango flavour and topped with Alphonse mango. Taste wise it was really good as the mango was sweet and it was not extra sweet.

MOCKTAILS~
Tropical Bliss.
Sunset Bloom.
Both the mocktails tasted refreshing as the ingredients tasted nice with each other.

So our meal at What’s Your Plan was really good as the food tasted perfect, the ambiance plus vibe of the restaurant is great and the service was excellent. Therefore a must visit., name_person=Shaikh Khalid Sarfaraz}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=6 months ago, review=*New Place Alert*

Recently visited this place with some friends of mine!
It is located in Vile Parle East!
It is good hangout spot for Sathaye & Dahanukar College students as it’s very near by!
The ambience is very pretty with amazing lights & they have indoor and outdoor seating as well.
I visited this place for lunch.

So we had ordered-
Cocktails:
Caprioska, it was very nice. It had mint leaves and lemon in it

Mocktails:
Cinderella, it was a pomegranate based juice, it was sweet and very refreshing.

Appetizers:
Afro chicken, stir fried chicken with fried veggies which were onion, bell peppers & garlic! It was saucy

Afghani chicken tandoor, it was so nice, was served with green chutney and salad.

In the main course we tried,
Chicken steak sizzler, I always wanted to try chicken steak so I chose it. The chicken was very juicy and it was served with stir fried veggies, potato fries and rice/noodles.

In desserts:
We had Sizzling brownie with Vanilla ice cream! The classic. The brownie was so good!

My experience at this place was amazing and would definitely recommend this place., name_person=Sanika Angwalkar}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=3 years ago, review=If you are looking for the perfect place for get together, family function or wonderful food experience then  Spice 57 is the one of the best Restaurant in Vile parle  which is Situated at Ground Floor of Sangita Nest Building. This place near from Vile parle railway station which is around 1.2 km. This is One of the best place which known for  their sizzlers, BBQ food and Seafood.  Yesterday I've visited this beautiful place for lunch with my friend. Ambiance of this place is beautiful and colorful which perfectly decorated with lots of lights and colorful ambiance. They Maintain Perfect Ambiance. The seating arrangement of this is perfectly managed and organised. They have perfect combination of attractive wooden table and comfortable colorful chairs which gives a great look to this place. Liked this place a lot.
Talking about staff and food..
Staff are professional and Attentive. Management has maintained good hygiene and  take all safety precautions and sanitation.
Food was so delicious. Quality , Quantity and presentation of food was awesome. We've tried many dishes here. Liked each and every Dish.
We've Tried and Blue Lit and Whisky Sar in cocktail.  In Staters Fish Chilly  tastes superb. Liked it very much. In Main Course Prawns Chilly Sizzlers was awesome one of the best sizzler i ever had. Highly recommended sizzler.
In Dessert Choco Delight was fantastic. Love the dessert. Overall my experience at Spice 57 was Great. Liked each and everything.
Highly recommended 👍👍👍, name_person=yogesh gaikwad}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=3 years ago, review=NEW PLACE ALERT*

Located in Vile Parle East, this restaurant and bar serves some amazingly fresh and quality dishes. The primary cuisine served is North Indian and Chinese. They also have Mangalorean dishes on the menu which are a must try. They have a nice bar with a wide variety of drinks to choose from.
The ambience is nice with dim lights and a wall full of quotes. The seating is comfortable. The overall look and feel is like a family restaurant and bar. The service was prompt to start with Mahesh taking down the orders. However they took a reasonable amount of time to get all the dishes.

The mocktails we had were Cinderella and Berry Blast. Both these were juice based drinks. Berry blast has Cranberry and Apple juice with a touch of honey.
Cindrella has orange juice and fresh lime which makes it very refreshing.

The food we had was all very good in terms of quality and quantity. I would rate it a value for money place.

We had Murg Toorki which was Chicken Tikka marinated with Cheese and this was delicious. The chicken was cooked to perfection, juicy and charred perfectly. This tasted even better with the mint coriander chutney.

Coriander Chicken Dry was a Chinese appetizer, this was again very good. Herbaceous flavour with garlic and spring onions. Again well cooked Chicken. Very satisfying.

For the main course we had Chicken Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa. My favourite and everything was perfect. Must have when here. Highly recommended.

The Cheese Garlic Naan here is not the usual Naan with the Garlic and Cheese outside. Here it's stuffed inside and is very wholesome.
We had Chicken Betabi which is a red gravy similar to Butter Chicken in many ways with shredded chicken in a luscious velvety gravy.

For dessert we had a sizzling walnut brownie with ice cream. This was fresh and well made.

This place even has outdoor seating which is accessible only post rains. I am totally in awe of the simplicity and the no nonsense kind of approach to serving good quality food.

I am totally coming back here again with my gang for a great meal.

Till next time Bon Appetit!, name_person=Varun Poduval}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good Ambience, Good Service, quality and tasty Food ,}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=They serve Chinese, BBQ,North Indian, seafood, biriyani, deserts and beverages.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Tasted really well with the mild flavours of the butter garlic chicken.}"]

The restaurant is located on the 4th floor and on top of the evergreen building near the Khar railway station. The restaurant is not too big, but the layout is elegant, with a sofa-like seating arrangement at one end with a table in between. The restaurant also serves hookah for people who want to do it.

Coming to the food, we started with many sides and starters, including cheese corn balls, chilly cheese toast, bruschetta, cheese garlic bread, etc. Every item that I have tasted was one of the best I have ever tasted after visiting so many restaurants. But the chilly cheese toast and the cheese garlic bread were supremely tasty. The perfect cooking and the tons of loaded cheese on top made it delicious to delve into those.

For the main course, we ordered garlic naan, paratha, butter kulcha, and two portions of Veg. Kolhapuri and Butter paneer masala each. The Indian bread, all of them tasted excellent and were made really well. All of them were absolutely soft, and the amount of Butter on them improved the taste significantly. Each of the main course vegetables was delicious too. The butter paneer masala, one of my favorite main courses to try, was delicious. The paneer was fresh and soft, and the gravy was also not very spicy. On the other hand, the Veg. Kolhapuri was on the spicier side with a rich combination of delectable vegetables such as french beans, carrots, peas, etc.

We also tried out a few platters. I loved one Veg. platter particularly. It was a combination of veggies stuffed together, including Veg. lollipop and grilled potatoes, flame-grilled baby corns, bell peppers, etc. While the other was a Veg. starter platter that included two types of paneer tikkas (red and green), Veg and paneer Manchurian, and other starters.

Tucked away in the opulent ITC Maratha, Peshawari is a culinary institution that has been regaling palates for over three decades. This iconic restaurant has been a testament to the rich culinary heritage of the Northwest Frontier Province, now known as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

As I stepped into the majestic ITC Maratha, I was struck by its grandeur. This 5-star hotel, located in the heart of Mumbai, is a masterclass in luxury and elegance. With its intricate architecture and impeccable service, it's no wonder that ITC Maratha has been a favorite among discerning travelers and gourmands alike.

Now, let's delve into the culinary prowess of Peshawari. This award-winning restaurant is renowned for its authentic North Indian cuisine, particularly its non-vegetarian delicacies. The Sikandri Raan, a signature dish, is a masterclass in slow-cooked perfection. The tender, fall-off-the-bone mutton is infused with a rich, aromatic spice blend that will leave you craving for more.

Another standout dish is the Chicken Tikka, marinated to perfection in a blend of yogurt, spices, and herbs. The chicken is cooked to a succulent, smoky tenderness that's simply irresistible.

The service at Peshawari is impeccable, with attentive staff who are knowledgeable about the menu and happy to make recommendations.

Verdict
Peshawari is a culinary gem that shines brightly in the heart of ITC Maratha. With its rich history, impeccable service, and outstanding cuisine, it's a must-visit destination for any food connoisseur.

Price: Upscale (around ₹1,500-₹2,500 per person)

The place has a very relaxed yet elegant vibe. As soon as you walk in, you notice the clean, modern interiors with a warm touch — not too fancy, not too casual — just the right atmosphere to enjoy a good Italian meal. The service was polite and attentive without being overbearing, which made the whole experience even better.

We ordered two dishes: the Arrabiatta Pasta and the Vegetariana Pizza.

The Arrabiatta Pasta was absolutely spot on. It had the perfect balance of flavors — the tomato sauce was rich and vibrant, with just the right amount of spice that hits you pleasantly at the back of your throat without overwhelming the dish. The pasta was cooked al dente, which gave it that slight bite that’s so essential but often missed. Every forkful felt hearty and comforting, exactly how a good pasta should.

The Vegetariana Pizza was equally impressive. Made in a true Neapolitan style with a thin, airy, and slightly charred crust, it came loaded with colorful fresh vegetables — bell peppers, zucchini, mushrooms, and more. The mozzarella was creamy, and the vegetables were cooked just right, still holding a bit of crunch and freshness. What stood out the most was how light the pizza felt — unlike the heavy, greasy ones you often find — yet it was packed with flavor in every bite.

Both dishes were served piping hot, and the portions were generous without going overboard. It really felt like the kitchen team cared about every plate they sent out.

Overall, Gustoso completely delivered on what we were hoping for. If you’re craving truly authentic Italian food, especially pizza or pasta done the traditional way, this place should be very high on your list. It’s a little slice of Naples right here in Mumbai., name_person=Kartikeya Pathak}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=The pizza is truly impeccable, with a saucy base unlike any other you’ll ever taste. Try the fish curry and rice!, name_person=Erica}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Bombil_Fry, Pork_Sausage_Chilli], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=9 months ago, review=I usually visit Mumbai for music concerts and every time I go for one, despite it ending over the weekend, I book my flights a day later just so I can visit Soul Fry on a Monday night for the karaoke. This place was suggested by my Goan friend who stumbled upon it for it’s authentic Goan cuisine and great vibe. And for the past couple of years I’ve made it a ritual to go here with my friends every time we visit Mumbai.

Every visit I had here has been nothing short of a fantastic experience. From the excellent service by the waiters, the yummy taste of well-made Goan food to the fun vibe the place and it’s people exuberate, it’s become my goto place in Mumbai for a fun night of singing. Eddie’s Bistro has long been on my radar, and I finally decided to give their Iftaar menu a whirl, expecting nothing less than a feast for the senses. Right from the get-go, the presentation scored high marks; the food arrived in pristine packaging that promised good things within.

Carnivorous Delights Unleashed:
The evening kicked off with Lamb Sliders, a real treat for the palate. These little delights were packed with tender, juicy lamb that melted in the mouth—clearly the star of the evening. Each bite was a perfect symphony of flavors, making it hard not to crave more.

Vegetarian Surprise:
Next up, the Paneer Chilly. Soft, succulent cubes of paneer tossed in a spicy sauce that had a kick but was incredibly flavorful. It was a bit on the spicy side for my taste, but it seemed to hit the right note with everyone else at the table, proving that spice is indeed the variety of life.

Kebab Corner:
The Chicken Seekh Kebab lived up to its reputation. Perfectly cooked with spices that sang through each bite, it was a testament to the careful preparation and love that went into its creation. It’s always a pleasure when a dish meets your high expectations, and these kebabs did just that.

A Chinese Twist:
Rounding off the meal was a Chicken dish with a Chinese twist that was intriguingly different. It was a refreshing change, adding a unique flare to the meal and showcasing the versatility of Eddie’s kitchen.

Overall Experience:
Eddie’s Bistro delivered an Iftaar that was both delightful and memorable, scoring a solid 5/5 on the food front. It’s clear that their culinary prowess isn’t just about good food, but about creating experiences that linger long after the meal is over.

Whether you’re in it for the love of meat or the joy of well-crafted vegetarian options, Eddie’s is a bistro that caters with heart and substance. I recently visited with friends, and the experience reminded me exactly why this place is considered a classic. The moment you enter, the quirky garage-themed decor pulls you in—number plates, car parts, the iconic Beetle overhead, dim lights, and a vibe that instantly makes you feel like you’ve stepped into an old-school rock pub.

The music is easily the best part of Toto’s. Their playlist is always on point, with rock classics, indie hits, and the kind of tracks that make conversations flow and the mood lift automatically. It’s loud enough to create energy but not overwhelming, and the crowd is always a great mix of regulars, college kids, and working professionals just looking to unwind.

The food and drinks are fairly priced for Bandra, and everything we ordered tasted fresh. The chicken wings, nachos, and their signature cocktails are must-tries. Service is quick, friendly, and no-nonsense—exactly what you expect from a legendary neighbourhood pub.

What I appreciate most is the consistency. Even after all these years, Toto’s still feels authentic, cozy, and full of character. It’s one of those places where you can go with friends, have a good laugh, enjoy great music, and genuinely feel at ease.

Yesterday, my friend and I checked out the new outlet. It’s nice, with comfy seating and a decent vibe 😊✨ But honestly, nothing compares to their Oshiwara outlet. That was until I discovered Chef James — a true culinary virtuoso.

At his restaurant, every dish reflects authenticity, artistry, and passion. Using genuine ingredients and presenting a thoughtfully curated “James Special” menu, he has redefined the Japanese–Korean dining experience in Mumbai.

I’m still savoring memories of the exquisite Sushi, Makgeolli rice beer, Kimbap, Galbisal, Ramen, Prawn Tempura, and the irresistibly delicate Mochi sticky rice ice cream. Each bite was a perfect balance of flavor and finesse.

I can’t wait to return to explore more — the Hot Pots, live barbecue, sizzlers, Donburi, a wide selection of appetizers, Sashimi (fresh raw fish), and Aburi Nigiri, gently seared with a blowtorch for that smoky finish.

Mumbai finally has a place that captures the true spirit of Japanese and Korean gastronomy — thanks to Chef James., name_person=Lamka Matters}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=6 days ago, review=Chef James Kitchen in Andheri is truly a hidden gem. Recently shifted from Adarsh Nagar, the restaurant offers a calm, intimate, and very chef-driven dining experience.

What makes this place special is the variety and thought behind the menu — Japanese and Korean favourites paired with Peruvian flavours, which is something you rarely find in Mumbai. Every dish felt well-balanced and carefully executed.

From the freshness of the crab salad to the melt-in-the-mouth Buta No Kakuni pork, the smoky sumi biyaki prawns, and the beautifully done Salmon Crello, each plate had its own personality. The chef’s special sushi roll and ramen were comforting yet refined, and the mushroom rice tied everything together perfectly.

The Mount Fuji cocktail was refreshing and well-crafted, and ending the meal with mochi ice cream was a lovely touch.

Overall, Chef James Kitchen isn’t just about food — it’s about the experience. No signs, no directions, no hint of welcome—just confusion in a remote location. What was meant to be an adventure felt more like a poorly planned scavenger hunt. By the time we found the entrance, the charm had worn off. A little signage goes a long way. Sadly, this place missed the mark.

Unfortunately, the service fell short of expectations. We waited quite a while without being checked on, and no one asked if we needed help serving ourselves. The food quality was mixed. The hotpot recommended by the waiter fell below expectations—it tasted like watered-down broth with no spice or depth, and no banchan were served alongside it. The fried tofu/paneer in it felt very off... My friend received only kimchi with her cold noodles, which felt sparse and incomplete.

The takoyaki was flavourful and rich in umami, and the vegetable gimmari was well cooked and enjoyable. However, there was a noticeable absence of a dessert menu—just one option offered, with no details or presentation. A single option without context misses the chance to end the meal on a memorable note., name_person=Melissa “Flavia” Pereira}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Even though this restaurant is hidden away, everything was just awesome. As you enter, the ambience is top-level. Cozy, good music, quiet, chill atmosphere. Staff is extremely polite and kind! I recommend reserving a booth before visiting. 🤎
Service was quick. The food was really good. It was my 1st time trying this cuisine and the experience was wonderful. There's a huge variety in Ramen, Kimbap, Sushi flavors and at an affordable price. 🍜
Ask them for in-house beverages! ;)🍶
I tried two desserts matcha ice cream, and the vanilla mochi was recommended by our server- it tasted pretty good!!
I'm a huge fan of Anime and Kdramas, so I felt literally at-home here! The booth area is especially my favorite. 🎀
Hats off to the owner of the restaurant! Great idea, great execution.
Will definitely visit again!
The dishes I tried :
Prawns Tempura Sushi roll 5/5🍤
Pork Kimbap 3/5
Chefs Special Ramen 5/5
Squid BBQ 4/5
Chicken Mandu 5/5
Matcha Iced Tea 5/5
Green Apple Mojito 5/5
Match ice cream 5/5
Vanilla Mochi Ice cream 5/5, name_person=Melanie}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=5 months ago, review=I’ve visited both the Malad and Oshiwara branches of Chef James' Kitchen, and I have to say, the Oshiwara branch stands out—especially when it comes to portion size and slightly better quality overall.

Here’s what we tried:
- Spicy Chicken Korean Carbonara
- Chicken Spicy Chef James’ Special Ramen
- Chicken and Pork Katsu Rice Bowl
- Prawn Tempura Sushi Roll
- Strawberry Mochi Ice Cream

The Spicy Carbonara and the Chef James’ Ramen were absolute winners—flavorful, comforting, and totally worth the price.

If you’re craving a hearty rice bowl, don’t think twice—go for the Chicken Katsu. It’s packed with flavor and super satisfying. The pork version didn’t quite hit the mark for me, especially the katsu fry, which lacked the crispiness and taste I was expecting.

I’m not usually a sushi fan, but the prawn tempura roll but it is worth a try.

And finally, the strawberry mochi ice cream was the perfect sweet ending—light, chewy, and refreshing., name_person=Ancia Dias}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 months ago, review=I've never had a worse tonkatsu ramen in my life. It's supposed to be comforting and flavorful even if mild, but this just tasted like hot water. A complete waste of money.
The staff were super sweet to at least give me a side small serving of pork that would add some flavour to the flavorless broth water, but it was too late by then. Even objectively speaking, nobody would like this, it was just plain water with noodles, i just left most of it. The pork pieces were the only redeemable thing in ramen. They dropped the ball on this one. We waited a long time for all 3 of our orders.

The chefs special ramen on the other hand was top class, incredibly tasty and enriching. I couldn't believe how good it was compared to the tonkatsu.

Even the snow moutain maki roll was really good. It's served with a mountain of crab. Damn tasty.
Any star they get is for the wonderful staff and the other 2 items we tried., name_person=Anish Karkera}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=It is a quaint little japanese and korean restaurant serving lovely food}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=For starters we ordered spicy crab gimbap and pork katsu.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Huge juicy chunks of chicken batter fried perfectly as not oily tasted good.}"]

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=5 months ago, review=“An Asian food lover’s paradise with a bold twist!

Only went for the Bao, and they were good., name_person=kevin saji}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Salad], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=a year ago, review=Linking Road in Bandra is home to some of the best food in the city, and one of the best asian joints in the place is The fatty Bao. It has a modern, chic vibe crossed with a vibrant and sassy decor, perfect for a date night, or for a hangout sesh with friends.

The decor feels inspired by Malay/Singaporean cafes, with a lot of the artwork depicting the same, and it comes off pretty well. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, though the indoor seating is a bit cramped, but that's mostly fine. They do have a small bar serving the usual suspects, as well as some of their own stuff.

While I didn't get to order a large chunk of their menu, whatever I had was pretty great. Their name is definitely apt, as the baos I got were plump and pillowy, and the filling was perfect. I got the pork char siu baos, and the pork was fatty and melt in your mouth, complimented nicely by a slice of raw apple, giving it a fruity kick. Every Bao order comes with two, making it perfect for date night.

I also got their raw papaya salad, which was one of the best renditions of the dish I've eaten in Mumbai. It was tangy, sweet and spicy in just the right amounts, and wasn't just a refreshing palate cleanser, but a great meal by itself. It's also a very generous portion making it great for sharing.

The last thing I got were Chicken and asparagus dumplings, which didn't impress me as much, as I've had better dumplings in the same price range. They weren't bad but not particularly great either. The filling was generous, but it lacked in flavor. For 6 pieces, it was not the best value, and I recommend trying other dumplings, or avoiding dumplings all together.

Overall, I would rate both the Char Siu Bao and the Papaya Salad a solid 9/10, and the dumplings about a 6.5/10. Definitely go for their baos( pretty obvious given their name).

The service was fine, but they do tend to ignore the smaller tables and focus on the bigger groups, and it was also pretty busy on the day I visited. But I did see other tables also not receiving food at the proper times, so I'd rate the service a little lower, like a 6/10. Definitely could do with some improvement.

The Fatty Bao definitely ticks a lot of the boxes, though they do miss a little bit in their service, and cocktail variety, though I did not have the opportunity to try it. However, they more than make up for it with their snazzy decor and contemporary vibe, along with some pretty great food. I highly recommend checking the place out if you're out shopping in Linking Road and need to grab some lunch or dinner. You're definitely gonna be leaving a happy and fatty bao when you're done.

Final rating- 8.5/10, definitely recommend., name_person=Riddhiman Chanda}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Firecracker_Cottage_Cheese_Bao, Prawn_Tempura], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=2 years ago, review=The tempura sushi, mushroom dumplings, cottage cheese bao and avocado cheese sushi all tasted amazing. Cocktails could have been better since they were expensive. The mushroom and chicken Ramen weren't very authentic since I have had better ones. Overall it was good, would go again and order more of their appetizers., name_person=Priyanka Saravanan}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=4 years ago, review=I am not very big on Asian food but i decided to try it anyway and a friend recommended this place so, here we go. The ambience is very pleasant. very hospitable staff.
Started with drinks and a few appetizers.

The drinks were great and so were the appetizers.

Tried the char siu bao, the meat was seriously overcooked and very dry. A little disappointed because of that.

Also, when taking the last round of order, nobody asked around whether we wanted to order more. They need to work more of customers.

Overall this place is amazing but they could've done better in terms of food and customer satisfaction.

Cheers!, name_person=Dipak Vishwakarma}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=2 years ago, review=We went here because we hadn't made a reservation anywhere and most of the good restaurants were full.

Scrumptious dumplings, soups, salads. We had the 8 course lunch menu, everything from soup, salad, dimsums, chicken starters, rice, noodles and curry was amazing. The sichuan chilli oil dimsum and the pork Chinese cabbage was to die for., name_person=Snehal Richter}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=Edited 3 years ago, review=Just beside the Monkey Bar.......An authentic Asian restaurant.

Tried their veg and non-veg dishes. Both were good. Stir fry chicken and chicken spicy dumplings were the best. Try their 5 rice chilli combo, superb! That too veg. Place is great for a small group. Do book in advance., name_person=Navin Nathani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=We dined at Hakkasan Mumbai tonight and, while the space is beautiful and the service was polite, the overall experience did not live up to the premium pricing or the reputation of the brand.

The biggest disappointment was the cocktail pricing. We ordered very standard drinks — a Negroni and a Paloma — and were charged approximately $40 per cocktail. At that price point, you expect truly exceptional creativity, presentation, or ingredients, but these were simply average. If a restaurant chooses to price cocktails at this level, they really need to deliver something ultra high-end to justify it. Otherwise, it feels excessive and out of proportion to what you’re actually getting.

We had dined the night before at Bastian at the Top, and the contrast was striking. Bastian was on another level entirely — the views from the 47th floor, the energy, the food, the drinks, and even the value for money were all significantly better. Their cocktails were roughly 50% less expensive, yet far more impressive in both taste and presentation. That experience absolutely set a high benchmark, and unfortunately Hakkasan did not meet it.

Overall, Hakkasan is not bad by any means, but it feels overpriced for what it offers. With so many outstanding dining options in Mumbai, I expected more in terms of both value and wow factor. For us, it ended up being a 3 out of 5 — decent, but not memorable, and not somewhere I would rush back to given the pricing., name_person=Aman B}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=It was my first time to visit this restaurant.Over all everything was nice and place is very beautiful. We had great interaction with Hardik who is working as restaurant manager and Mathotmi was our server. Hardik introduced us about restaurant and Mathotmi explained us about drinks and food. Also they suggested us food and drinks too. Food was authentic and well presented and explained by the server.We had great time and I hope to visit again soon. Thanks., name_person=pooja gaonkar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Dark_Chocolate_Mousse_with_Mandarin_Sorbet, Classic_Hakka_Steam_Dimsum_Platter, Braised_Pork_Belly_with_Truffle_Sauce_and_Mantou, Dumpling, Dark_Chocolate_Mousse, Mocktail, Half_Peking_Duck], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=Edited 5 months ago, review=This is my second visit to Hakkasan. As always, brilliant food and even better service. The staff were pleasant in particular, Apam, which lifted the overall experience. Had the pleasure of meeting the man behind the scene Chef Raymond. Special thanks to Dhananjay Gowda for making the experience even more memorable with his recommendations to suit all our fussy palettes., name_person=Demetrius Errol Cordeiro D'Souza}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=a year ago, review=I recently revisited this upscale Chinese restaurant for brunch, despite previous underwhelming experiences. Unfortunately, the lack of natural light and overuse of tacky blue lights remained a major turnoff. The ambiance, while appealing to some, doesn’t  resonate with me.
The food, while reasonably priced during brunch, didn't change my opinion about Chinese cuisine in Bombay. It still feels like a generic Chinese restaurant in a five-star hotel.

On a positive note, the staff was attentive and well-trained, with noticeably more staff members on deck. The addition of a smoking cabin upstairs was convenient, and the toned-down music was a welcome change. The unlimited flow of good brand cocktails was a great value.

While this restaurant still isn't my favorite, I appreciate the positive changes in price, smoking area, and music volume., name_person=Chirag Patel}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Soup, Dumpling], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Not sure, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=a year ago, review="Hakkasan, Bandra West, is a stylish and sophisticated spot, but the food doesn't quite live up to the hype. Some dishes feel overpriced and lacking in flavor. Must-try dishes include the Peking Duck, but other options are hit-or-miss. Cocktails: 5/5 - Innovative and expertly crafted. Overall, Hakkasan is a great spot for a night out, but foodies might find it just average. Rating: 3.5/5 stars", name_person=Lakshita Agarwal}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Breakfast, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Classic_Hakka_Steam_Dimsum_Platter, Dark_Chocolate_Mousse_with_Mandarin_Sorbet, Soup, Half_Peking_Duck], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=11 months ago, review=Had the pleasure of dining at Hakkasan in Mumbai, and I have to say, the atmosphere is fantastic. The setting is modern and sleek, with comfortable seating and a stylish bar that creates a welcoming vibe. It’s definitely one of the top Chinese restaurants in Mumbai, but while the ambiance is spot on, it doesn’t quite deliver in terms of traditional Chinese authenticity.

The staff were friendly and attentive, always ready to assist. We ordered the Peking duck, which was, unfortunately, underwhelming. The preparation was just okay—the skin wasn’t crispy, and the duck itself was on the smaller side but came from Thailand. Traditionally, the creases would be used for a soup or stir-fry, but they were left unused here. A bit disappointing considering the cost and overall taste.

On a positive note, the dim sum was quite good, and I was impressed by how they cater to a wide range of dietary preferences, with no lard used in their offerings. We also tried the stir-fried buffalo, which was surprisingly delicious—tender, not too gamey, and packed with flavor.

The drinks were excellent, and it would’ve been nice to see the tea served personally as needed, perhaps with a selection of puer on the menu for added depth?

As for dessert, I think they could elevate the experience by adding some authentic Chinese options instead of just only the Western-style desserts.

The desserts, while good, leaned more towards Western-style offerings. I would love to see some traditional Chinese desserts added to the menu for an authentic touch.

All in all, it was a very enjoyable experience. The service was excellent, and the atmosphere was top-notch, though there’s room for improvement in the authenticity and food preparation. Hopefully they will be more responsible to the society and other customers going forward., name_person=Sonali Shivlani}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=I was looking for a venue for a lazy brunch, and Zomato suggested Bora Bora. I had been there before, quite a while ago, and with a review pending I thought why not, so here goes. I reached to find out that the AC section was closed for renovation, and was given a table outside. I chose the alcoholic menu for their Sunday brunch, and started off with Long Island Iced Tea, Tempura Prawns and Mini Angry Bird. My next order was Chicken Chilly Tacos and Top Secret Malai Kebab, and my next drink was Blenders Pride. The tacos were particularly impressive, spicy meat on toasted bread with cheese, they were an absolute winner. The kebabs weren't too bad either, the meat was tender and though the name said Malai, there was some spice to it, which I didn't mind at all. This was followed by Wild Fish Fingers, strips of basa with a crunchy crust, I found it to be average, have had better elsewhere. With my tummy filling up, I drained my final round of whiskey, and ordered desserts. First up was a platter of pastries, in 3 flavours. The orange pastries were nothing to write about, the red velvet was a little above average, while the kiwi was the by far the best. Next I had some icecream, Vanilla and Strawberry scoops put together and it was delicious, I was tempted to go for another round, but then I was suggested Gulab Jamun by the staff so I opted for that, and what a suggestion it was. The gulab jamuns were soft, sweet and simply superb, a must-have here. Speaking of the staff, I must mention the attendant to my table, Angam. He was most polite, helpful, always with a smile, a big shoutout to his stellar service. With the desserts done, I asked for the cheque to conclude what had been a truly fulfilling meal. The decor was among the stronger points of the place, it has a beautiful interior with some funky looking seats as well with swings inbuilt to it.

The menu was very extensive, covering a very large number of cuisines. Normally places that say , wow, we can make all of this stuff in our kitchens, normally they're being a bit too ambitious.

We got tofu based dumplings, parmesan garlic fries, a veg sushi, the blah! special pasta, smores based pancakes and also a couple of Vietnamese coffees and a lemon based tea.

I suppose the best part of the order was dumplings, fries and the sushi, probably in that order... The tofu dumplings were delectable and perfectly well done.... The pasta was kind of average at best and the smores pancakes were ok but we've had better ones.

The Vietnamese coffees were actually among the best I've ever had and quite authentic in its preparation in that it has a VERY dense layer of thick condensed milk at the bottom and has the espresso above it. You have to mix it to get the final beverage and that's how Vietnamese coffee is supposed to be.

My friend had the tea and it could be best summarised as "tea without tea in it", which is kind of odd because tea leaves are usually a big deal in making tea, well, tea....

Service was ok but the ladies restroom had some issues which took considerable amount of time to resolve.

The price point was ok by BKC standards I suppose, but not fabulous on the value for money scale.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservation required, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=I spent the afternoon at Cecconi’s, settling in from noon until sunset and honestly, there’s no better place in the city to watch the sky melt into the sea. The ambiance is effortlessly chic, exactly what you’d expect from Soho House: understated, elegant, and always buzzing with the right kind of energy.

I tried the Margherita pizza, which was absolutely delightful,simple, perfectly done, and full of flavor. The penne pasta with veggies was decent, but the real star for me was the salad with rocket leaves and pear. Fresh, bright, and beautifully balanced… easily my favorite dish of the day.

The cappuccino was smooth and well-made, and the tomato basil soup hit all the right comforting notes.

Overall, Cecconi’s continues to be one of those places where the food, the vibe, and the view come together effortlessly. The perfect spot to linger, unwind, and watch the sunset paint the Arabian Sea., name_person=Padmini Dixit}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, 3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Cecconi’s at The Soho House, Mumbai, is truly one of the city’s most iconic dining spots — and for good reason. Nestled by Juhu Beach, it offers a breathtaking view of the sea that instantly elevates the entire experience. It’s also known as a celebrity hotspot, and you can easily see why — the ambiance perfectly balances elegance, warmth, and that distinct Soho charm.

We tried the Marinara Pizza, topped with cherry tomatoes, sun-dried tomatoes, paprika, and garlic. Despite being a cheese-free pizza, it was bursting with rich flavors — fresh, tangy, and perfectly balanced with just the right hint of spice. Every bite tasted authentic and full of character, truly a standout dish.

Whether you’re here for the food, the view, or a bit of star-spotting, Cecconi’s promises a dining experience that’s hard to match in Mumbai. A must-visit if you’re looking to indulge in great Italian food by the sea., name_person=Kartikeya Pathak}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Not sure, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=Cecconi’s, an absolute treat for the taste buds and ambience which is just an excellent match soft music, open ocean view and light breeze

That said when it came to service there were a few highs and lows which I believe alters the overall experience but more on that later.

The food was our highlight for this place;
Arancini, crispy fried and served on a base of really great sauce which balanced the richness of arancini with just enough tart flavour.

The Vegetable Lasagne, well this was like the star and quite literally, the cook of the pasta the tomato sauce n the healthy topping of melted cheese all of it made this one dish feel like literal comfort simply, difficult to quite explain in words but anyone who visits here should give this dish a try, you won’t regret it😁.

Spinach and Ricotta Ravioli has always been like my go to a safe dish for a new place and they nailed it right, light sauce with cherry tomatoes fried basil leaves and properly seasoned filling of ravioli.
