After a few deliberations we zeroed in on 90ML Bar and Kitchen at Bandra, not far from Chetna college. It took us a couple of minutes to find the place even though Maps indicated that we had arrived, as the outlet is placed in a pretty non-descript row of low-rise buildings. We entered to find a small outdoor seating area, and chose to dine inside, away from the heat. Activating our Zomato Gold, we went along with the suggestion of our attendant and ordered the Classic variant of Long Island Iced Tea along with Peri Peri Peanuts. For starters we opted for Paneer Dragon Dry and Roast Chicken Chilly. The cocktail arrived first, and it was made to perfection. I highly recommend it, being one of the best LIIT's I have had in a long time. The peanuts were quite spicy as well as tangy, making for some great chakna. The starters then were served simultaneously, the vegetarian being, as expected, the milder of the two. Neither the paneer nor the chicken left any room for disappointment, being tender and appropriately chewy. Our second drink was Sex On The Beach, a concoction of vodka, schnapps, orange and cranberry juices. Not that I didn't like it, but I found it to be a bit fruity, would have preferred it to have some more punch. Continuing our Oriental theme for the food, we inquired about the rice preparations on offer, and Mongolian Rice appealed to us the most. Fried rice with finely chopped chillies and green gravy full of veggies like broccoli, capsicum, onion etc, it made for a very fulfilling main course. The desserts menu was rather limited, and our choice, Brownie with Ice Cream, wasn't available so we settled for Caramel Custard. It had a lovely jelly-like texture, but was not as sweet as expected nor did the chocolate sauce enhance the dessert, not a must have in my opinion. To sum up then, 90ML Bar and Kitchen ticks most of the boxes and does a good job without being exceptional. The only criticism I have is the service, which was a little lethargic at times. Basics like providing water and cleaning the table had considerable delays even though most of the tables were unoccupied. Overall, the drinks are nice, the food is on the spicier side and they seem to use chillies instead of masala to spice things up, I like that. Quantity wise there are no complaints, and the booze is not exorbitant, plus they have Zomato Gold, making this place excellent value for money., name_person=Rohan Bidi}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Food, ambience, price, staff everything is great of this place as of now.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Service is good also quantity of dish is enough for 2 people.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=▶️ Roasted Veg pizza ⭐⭐⭐ 1/2 Thin crust pizza with loads of veggies.}"]

Food — Bold Flavours, Beautiful Presentation
Here’s where Papaya truly shines. The menu is curated — not overwhelming, but packed with dishes that bring flavour, texture, and colour.

Dim Sums: Soft, delicate, and generously filled. The truffle edamame or prawn har gow are favourites for good reason — silky, aromatic, and full of umami.

Crispy Lotus Stem: Thin, crunchy, sweet-spicy, and addictive. A signature dish that sets the tone.

Thai Curries: Creamy, fragrant, and comforting. The green curry especially has the perfect balance of heat and herbal notes.

Sushi & Rolls: Fresh, neatly rolled, never overpowered with sauces. The fusion rolls are visually stunning and flavour-rich.

Baos: Pillow-soft and packed with flavour. restaurant_name: Fresh Catch By Francis - Coastal and Seafood Restaurant
reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Did you know that this family run seafood restaurant in Bandra has been a celebrity favourite since 1998? Fresh Catch by Francis serves some fabulous Goan and Mangalorean seafood. Fun fact - they only serve the freshest catch of the day and that is where their name comes from. I had their Prawns Rechado and Rawa Surmai Fry first and both were delicious. I loved the Prawns Konkan Curry with Neer Dosa, it also went well with rice. I tried the Goan Bebinca here for the first time and I’m a fan. If you love seafood, you can’t miss this spot., name_person=Ramsha Tausalkar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=2 months ago, review=This place was as good as I expected, and the food tasted nice, but the quantity and portion size were quite small for the price. The staff was really nice and welcoming, and the crab dish was definitely good — just not worth the amount charged. Overall, it’s a decent spot, but I think they should consider making some changes to the menu and portion sizes to make it feel more worth it., name_person=Zikra Shaikh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=I got to know about this place through YouTube channel Curly Tales, that discusses the favourite food of various celebrities around the country. This place was heavily recommended over the channel by Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, hence making it easier in terms of choosing the place.

It's a restaurant that serves a vast array of seafood items and some standout dishes that are worthy of being called Legendary.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.
Add to that, 2 mugs of kingfisher beer to help in aiding the food down the stomach correctly.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

Keep up the good work., name_person=Siddharth Bose}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a week ago, review=⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Fantastic Seafood Experience!

I visited fresh catch seafood restaurant on 11.12.24 @ 2.00 pm. This restaurant delivers an outstanding seafood feast from start to finish. The prawns were exceptionally fresh and perfectly seasoned, and every fish dish—fried, grilled, or in curry—was full of authentic coastal flavor. I especially loved the refreshing solkadhi, which balanced the spices beautifully. To end the meal, the traditional Goan dessert bebinca was absolutely divine—soft, layered, and rich without being overly sweet.
The service was impeccable throughout; the staff was warm, attentive, and quick to offer recommendations. Overall, an excellent dining experience that captures the true essence of coastal cuisine. Highly recommended!, name_person=SWATANTRA PRAGATI}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Bombil_Fry, Surmai_Masala_Fry], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_STREET_PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Somewhat difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Fresh Catch is a seafood restaurant that has a mix of goan and mangalorean style fare. Located on the second floor they have a lift that makes it accessible. The interiors make the restaurant look like a fine dining place but the servers floral shirts make it seem like the opposite. For starters we ordered the bombil rava fry which was crispy and tasty. Next we got the prawns butter garlic which was again done very well but the quantity could have been more. We got the surmai masala fry which was delicious and the masala was spot on. For the mains we got the ravas rechado gravy with some neer dosa and it was an absolutely delightful combo. We also got the prawns pulao which was less flavourful and dry. We ordered some squids sukkem to go along with the pulao. The squids were well cooked. In the drinks we got the mango mule and the spiced guava which tasted like any other tetra pack juice and was too expensive. Overally the food is good but the ambiance and certain aspects of the food should be looked into., name_person=Patricia}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=7 months ago, review=One of the biggest hype bubbles, Fresh Catch finally burst! Never expected it to be so so so bad! Lol! 🤣 All those pictures of Sachin notwithstanding, this place is a DUD!

Our meal happened on a weekday, and early in the evening when only two other tables were occupied. It was hot and all of us were sweating, profusely. The staff just said, multiple times, that all the air conditioners were on full blast. We even politely asked for a table/pedestal fan and it was promptly denied, though one pedestal fan was sitting idle in the corner with the TV. Allowing paying customers to keep sweating is unpardonable IMO. Staff should ideally do everything in their power to make customers comfortable. I guess  with so many pictures of Sachin on the wall, why bother with idiot sweaty customers. 🤷

The best part is the food - most of the things we ordered (many recommended by the staff) tasted the same - bland, characterless, papery. Only the Surmai was exceptional - really fresh with the most heavenly rachead masala. I think I tasted/munched on sand in the Crab Butter Garlic, which is ridiculous!

We didn't want to order mains because it was unbearably hot and all the food we had already ordered didn't inspire much confidence. Delicious food and good quality for 2 people, name_person=Avinash D'Souza}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=I travelled 17,000 km from Canada to Mumbai, excited to experience the warmth and hospitality of my home country, but my visit to Fresh Catch was nothing short of disheartening.

I genuinely cannot understand this level of arrogance and indifference in the service. It completely ruined what was meant to be a special meal after a long journey.

I will never visit again, nor would I recommend this place to anyone who respects their time and their dining experience., name_person=Devesh Gavankar}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Must try the chicken Rossa curry and crab meat butter garlic}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Very small portions for the prices.. very lazy and snobish staff}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Fantastic music, ambience and service combine for a home like feel.}"]

Donna Deli – Bandra West | Saturday Dinner Review

📍 Location & First Impressions
Donna Deli sits right on SV Road, Bandra, a short stroll from Khar Road Station so if you’re planning to drive, God be with you. If you're walking in, the white-washed European façade welcomes you like you’ve entered a Pinterest board.
Pro Tip: If it’s a weekend, reservation is non-negotiable. This place fills up quicker than your WhatsApp family group on Diwali morning.

🍽️ What We Tried

1. Truffle Pizza

Creamy, crispy, indulgent basically everything you want from a pizza that wears truffle like a crown. If royalty had a flavor, this would be it.

2. Truffle Fries

Yes, more truffle. Don’t judge.
We inhaled these while waiting for our drinks. Perfectly crisp, generously tossed, and honestly… finished too soon.

3. Donna’s Signature Drinks

We tried a bunch of their mocktails (let’s just say the menu has more Donnas than a Bollywood family tree). Refreshing, quirky, and worth experimenting with.

4. Hungover Noodles (⭐ The Star of the Night)

Do not go by the looks.
These noodles pack flavour, comfort, and a bit of drama. Easily the winner and something you’ll crave again.

🛎️ Service

Shockingly fast.
I mean the food arrived before our mocktails.
They take the “fast” in fast-casual seriously.

🌿 Ambience & Vibe

Donna Deli scores big here white décor, leafy corners, soft lighting, aesthetic touches everywhere. Instagram would approve. So would your date.

🚗 Parking & Access

Located right on SV Road

Walking distance from Khar station (recommended)

If coming by car, patience is a mandatory side dish

📌 Final Verdict – SGT Meter

Ambience: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

You can order House nachos, House peri peri wedges, Paneer lababdar with Naan and Daal Khichdi was tastyyyy, name_person=Hiya Bhanushali}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 months ago, review=Toss & Sipp is the perfect spot if you're in the mood for good vibes, great music, and even better cocktails. The energy of the place is upbeat and fun—ideal for a lively evening with friends. The décor is stylish and modern, adding to the vibrant atmosphere.

Huge shoutout to our steward, JP, who was super attentive and helped us pick the best from the menu based on our mood—his cocktail suggestions were on point! The Spark with Beefeater, raspberry, and sparkling wine was a bubbly delight, while the Sipp Me Up was super refreshing with elderflower, basil, and cucumber.

The Smoked Chicken Taquitos were packed with flavor, and the Sesame Chilli Prawns had the perfect kick. The Kerala Mutton Pepper Fry with Malabar Parota was a spicy, satisfying bite. We also loved the vibrant Assorted Hummus Platter. And to top it all off, the Strawberry Cheesecake was the perfect sweet ending.

Definitely a must-visit if you're looking for a fun night out with amazing food, drinks, and a buzzing crowd!, name_person=Tanishka Chavan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=7 months ago, review=Visited **TOSS & SIPP** during lunch hours, and I must say, it was a delightful experience from start to finish. The ambiance is stunning—beautifully designed interiors with a cozy yet vibrant vibe that instantly makes you feel at ease.

We started with the drinks, and they were an absolute hit. The **Cranberry Spice** mocktail was refreshing with just the right balance of sweet and tart, while the **Affair** cocktail had a bold, smooth flavor profile that set the tone for the rest of the meal.

The starters were a burst of flavor. The **Ghost Chilli BBQ Paneer Tikka** brought the perfect amount of heat and smokiness, and the **Smoked Mozzarella Coriander Chicken Tikka** was incredibly tender and packed with flavor.

For the mains, the **Grilled Cottage Cheese Burrito Bowl** was hearty and satisfying—perfectly grilled and loaded with textures. The **Grilled Chicken Herb Rice Bowl** was light yet filling, with beautifully seasoned chicken and herbed rice that was full of fresh flavors.

We ended on a sweet note with the **Caramel Tres Leches**—soft, creamy, and indulgent. An absolute must-try!

Great food, amazing drinks, and a lovely ambiance make it perfect for lunch dates or casual hangouts., name_person=Rahul Gupta}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Toss and Sip, Sakinaka, Mumbai is one of my favourite eating place. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=a month ago, review=It was not worth the hype, for a restaurant this famous with the kind of price they charge per person there was nothing unique, I'd ordered for a pizza but that did not end up coming to my table (the chef probably forgot it), the pasta was very basic, soups okok, the chatt counter was nice but that's something i can have anywhere, the inky love highlight for me was the cheese section nd Salads including the salami, main course as well was very okok (the goan prawns curry nd mutton was good) and lastly the dessert there were too many cake options and indian sweets which again I think I'd get at any other decent buffet (I grabbed the chocolate mouse, blueberry pie, cheesecake nd dark chocolate dessert), name_person=Michelle D'Souza}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=Edited 11 months ago, review=The ambience here is truly great and has always been a highlight 🌟. I’ve been visiting this restaurant 2-3 times a year for the last 5-7 years, and earlier, the taste they delivered was gold. Back then, they really tried to include everything in their buffet, and the dessert section used to be huge and impressive 🍰🍮.

Now, let’s talk about the breakfast buffet—it’s pretty standard, similar to what you’d find at any 5-star continental breakfast 🍳🥐. They do include a few Indian dishes, but honestly, breakfast here has never excited me since the beginning.

As for dinner, it used to be something I truly looked forward to because of how flavourful and varied the food was 🍽️. However, over the last 2-3 visits, it feels like something is always off—sometimes it’s the salt, sometimes it’s the flavours. The food feels same-same now, and perhaps I’ve become fed up of eating the same dishes repeatedly. There’s nothing new or exciting anymore, and the taste is not extraordinary enough to crave anything specific. I used to love the pizza here; it was one of my favorites. But lately, the taste has literally deteriorated 😞. It’s just not the same anymore, and it’s disappointing to see the quality drop. Hope they bring back the original flavors they were known for.

That said, this place still shines for its ambience ✨, and for newcomers, it might still feel impressive and worth the visit. But for me, my interest in visiting Lotus Cafe is slowly fading away 😕. I guess it’s a matter of having it too many times.

Still, for the overall experience, I’d rate it 4 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐., name_person=Ameen Shaikh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=6 months ago, review=I visited this cafe a few weeks ago, for their famous Sunday brunch. I was spoilt for choice. They have a wide array of dishes to choose from.

I started off with their Asian dumplings and they were good. I absolutely loved chicken Sumai.

Next up, I tried a cheese platter with Gouda, Brie, burrata, cheddar, caramelised figs and crackers. Everything paired so well.

They had a wide range of cured meats, smoked tuna, smoked salmon and lots and lots of grilled veggies.

The lobster and oysters and tiger prawns were outstanding. Their mutton chops were delicious too.

But their pizza and drinks stole the show for me. The pizza base was perfectly chewy and charred while the cheese was melty and gooey. Their pineapple Pina colada was sweet and creamy.

The pasta was okayish. And some dish were just average.

They also had a wide range of dessert to choose from. But their Gulab Jamun and chocolate caramel dessert was overly sweet. But I loved their blueberry cupcake and chia seed pudding.

Overall it’s worth visiting. The service is quick and the staff is amicable., name_person=Zoya Khan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=10 months ago, review=A premium restaurant with a large variety of good quality and delicious food. There were several options for starters, mains and desserts, which included a good selection of food for both vegetarians and non-vegetarians alike.

Service was very good with table service available for the buffet which makes things very convenient.

It is quite expensive but this premium is expected from a restaurant in a 5 star hotel where quality is assured., name_person=Karan Samani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=9 months ago, review=Lotus Cafe provides a comfortable and inviting ambience, making it a nice place to relax and dine. The service is efficient and friendly, ensuring a pleasant experience. However, the food is quite average, lacking the flavors or uniqueness that would make it stand out. While it’s a good choice for a laid-back meal in a nice setting, it may not be the best option for those seeking exceptional cuisine, name_person=Rupam Khetan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=This 5-star hotel restaurant exceeded expectations with its vast array of premium quality dishes, catering to both vegetarians and non-vegetarians. From cocktails like the Greon Fairy Sour and Mint Berry Mash beautifully crafted by mixologist Tanishq, to the perfectly cooked Grilled Tiger Prawns, flavorful Tofu Tamarindo, crispy Chicken Tuile Gyoza, creamy Tuscan Spaghetti, and smoky Polo Asado every dish was a masterpiece in flavor and presentation.

We ended the evening with their signature dessert The Pear an indulgent creation with glazed pear mousse, salted honey caramel, and brown butter gelato on pecan crumble the perfect finale to an exceptional meal.

The staff was attentive, courteous, and ensured quick service, making the whole experience seamless. Overall, Mercii is not just a restaurant but a complete premium dining destination highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy world-class food and ambiance in Mumbai., name_person=ABHISHEK}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Mercii is a high-end European & modern‑global fine dining restaurant in Santacruz (West), backed by Arpita Khan Sharma. The name “Mercii” (French for “thank you”) reflects a philosophy of gratitude, hospitality, and treating guests with warmth rather than cold luxury. The brand positioning is clearly premium & aspirational - it's meant to be more than just food — a full immersive dining experience. One of the standout features is the artificial skylight ceiling - during the day, it simulates soft sunlight and at night, it shifts into a starry sky/ambient skyscape. The interiors are luxurious and ornate - plush seating, rich textures, elegant lighting, jharokha (lattice) motifs, and private alcoves or “VIP room” that can host small groups upto 30 guests. The design attempts to balance regal elegance and vibrant nightlife energy, not just static “luxury.” Overall, the ambience is crafted to wow — it’s meant for special occasions, dates, or high-end dinners.
The kitchen is led by Group Culinary Director Dennis Koll, whose background and experience bring a refined European / global sensibility to the menu. The menu is ambitious — it offers European core (Italian, French etc.) with influences and creative fusions. Many dishes include theatrical or tableside finishing touches to elevate the experience. Some Standouts are
• Crimson & Green (salad)
• Furi Spice Rolls (sushi)
• Edamame Ricotta Gyoza (small plate)
• Rosette Ravioli  (large plate)
• The Pear (dessert)
The bar is a focal point. The cocktail program is expansive, creative, and often experimental, combining dessert flavors, smoky / bold elements, fruit, and classic roots. Some standouts are
• Cocktails - Heet Mango Margarita, Greon Fairy Sour, Smoky Terrain , Mercii Murmur, Mercii Rocher, Flower Power and Holy Biscoff.
• Mocktails - Mint Berry Mash and Sweet Kiss.
The drinks are not just side acts — they are integrated into the experience. Staff are attentive, polite and help with recommendations making the experience special. Mercii is not for everyone — it’s tailored for people who value showpiece ambience, Culinary experience with creative food and artisian drinks, top notch service and luxury. Christian Moreau Chablis 2016

It is very rare to find a Christian Moreau Chablis in India, and it was nice to see this wine on the menu at Le Cirque, Mumbai, and I ordered the same for my dinner.

Christian Moreau is one of the oldest and most respected domains in Chablis.
Wine has fruit notes like apple, green apple, pear etc.
A very beautiful and amazing Chablis wine.

Food Review:
A great wine needs great food.
That’s where the restaurant failed badly, and food was below average.

Initially their regular Chef prepared a dish based on lobster, and probably lobster was stale and the food was very bad which is not expected from such a restaurant.
Next a prawn based dish which was completely bad as well.
Finally I had a discussion with the restaurant manager and has concluded to change the regular Chef to another Chef Kamlesh to take over the dishes for dinner.
Kamlesh was comparatively better I felt when he prepared further dishes.

To be frank the restaurant had only me as a customer for the whole evening and it was very empty. Only one more customer came for a very short snacks that evening on another table.
I could understand it’s probably because of the bad Chef and lack of fine dining food menu.
I used to be a regular customer of the same restaurant Le Cirque in Bangalore which was much better as per my experience.

After discussing with Chef Kamlesh, I ordered smoked Scottish Salmon as starters which was very nice.
Followed by Pomfret dish which was quite average.
Next, another baked fish and vegetables.

Dessert:
The Chef Kamlesh suggested a portion of Crème Brûlée + Tiramisu.
Crème Brûlée was nice and tiramisu was average.

Conclusion:
To conclude, the overall experience was far below expectations.
The restaurant also didn’t had any special dishes like fish roe/caviar or scallops on the menu.
Food menu needs a lot of improvements to include fine dining dishes.
I could see that “Leela” failing very badly on expectations in Mumbai.

I will recommend to try lemon chicken and obviously chakali with schezwan sauce as combination tastes really nice., name_person=Janhavi Raut}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹200–400, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=a year ago, review=If you’re looking for an affordable spot to drink and chill in Bandra, Yacht Bar & Restaurant is worth checking out – but don’t go expecting luxury. It’s a no-frills, budget-friendly place that’s been around for ages and is popular, especially with the younger crowd.

Ambience and Crowd:
We visited on a weekend around 11:00 PM and the place was packed. It’s quite congested, so don’t expect much elbow room. We had to wait for 20 minutes before getting a table, which wasn’t surprising given its reputation for cheap drinks. They have two sections – AC and non-AC. We opted for the AC section, which was relatively comfortable.

Service and Drinks:
The staff was polite and fast, which was impressive given the crowd. The liquor here is very affordable, which explains why it’s so popular. It’s perfect if you’re on a tight budget and looking for a place to hang out with friends.

Food Experience:
The food, however, was disappointing. We tried the Chicken Crispy, a recommendation from the waiter, but it was dry and tough to chew. On the bright side, we enjoyed the chakli with Schezwan sauce.

Facilities:
Despite the heavy crowd, the washrooms were clean and there’s enough parking space available, which is a big plus in Bandra.

Final Thoughts:
Yacht Bar & Restaurant isn’t for everyone, but it’s a great option if you’re looking for a budget-friendly place to drink and chill. The crowd and ambiance might not be ideal for a quiet evening and the food could use improvement, but for cheap booze and a lively vibe, it gets the job done., name_person=Alok Shettigar}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Tasty Food Loved the vibe and the staff the waiter was helping Quality place 💯}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good service, food ok,booze genuine days the main thing..}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Great food, cheap prices on liquor, convenient location, helpful staff}"]

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Visited House of Mandarin, Bandra for lunch and had a pleasant experience overall, mainly because of the lovely seating arrangement and the extremely courteous staff. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[1_person, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_ONE, Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Today I stopped by for lunch and chose this restaurant because the atmosphere looked appealing from the outside. The decoration is modern and stylish, making it a nice place for a small party or a gathering with friends.

I ordered two dishes to try. The first was shrimp tempura sushi, which was quite well prepared. The shrimp was fried nicely and tasted fresh. The rice was slightly sticky—I am not sure if it was Japanese rice—but overall it was enjoyable.

The second dish was a mutton curry (I am not sure of the exact name), but it was very delicious. The service here is impressive. The staff were kind and attentive. I especially appreciated my two servers, whose names I did not catch, but they were friendly and paid close attention to details. For example, they even changed the bread to whole wheat, though I preferred to enjoy the curry with rice, which was also very tasty.

The music by the DJ gave a modern vibe, and the restaurant had a pleasant fragrance that made the atmosphere feel fresh and refined. I truly liked it, name_person=Ms.Dear369}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Very loud, hard to hear, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_PARKING_LOT], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=30-60 min, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Great Vibe, But Disappointing Service & Food
Visited Someplace Else at Jio World Drive — the ambience and party atmosphere are undeniably impressive, with vibrant lighting, lively music, and a great crowd vibe. It’s definitely one of the more happening nightlife spots in the area.
However, the service and food were quite disappointing. The staff seemed disinterested, and the food didn’t match the place’s high-energy vibe — bland and underwhelming. Also, a big drawback: if you’re even 5 minutes late for your booking on weekends, they often won’t let you in, which feels unnecessarily rigid.
If you’re here just for the party vibe and drinks, it’s worth visiting once — but if you’re expecting great food or smooth service, this might not be the place., name_person=Nikhil Aher}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR, 9+_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_NINE_OR_MORE], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=30-60 min}, time_line=3 months ago, review=This is a great spot located in Jio World Drive. I’ve been here twice – once with my office teammates and once with friends – and both times the experience was really good. The ambience is lively, and they serve quality food along with a nice variety of drinks.

The place is a little on the pricier side, but you’re sure to have a good time. At night, they have a DJ playing, and there’s a small space near the console where you can dance – or you can simply groove near your own table. Definitely worth a try if you’re looking for good vibes, food, and ambience., name_person=Piyush Potpose}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=I visited here on a weekday and it was good packed. We were very happy with the service and manager was so helpful and cordial. Definitely going to visit here again with my Jam !, name_person=shikhani shah}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=3 months ago, review=This is a wonderful place to spend time with friends. The music was outstanding. The singers and the band brought so much joy and talent to the room that we felt completely immersed in the experience. The service was excellent, and the food was a delight. We especially loved the fries and the tofu. Those two dishes were our favorites and we could not stop talking about them.

The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming. There was nothing pretentious about it. We felt truly seen and appreciated here. It was the perfect setting to celebrate our colleague who had just received a major award in her profession. The evening felt meaningful and full of warmth.

I cannot wait to return. This place is more than just a restaurant. It is a space where good food, good music, and good company come together in the best way., name_person=Lewis Cardenas}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Someplace else at Jio world drive is energetic bar that serves good food.

We tried a couple of dishes like
Barley salad which was flavourful and good.
Paneer tikka with crispy aloo which were delicious. The chutneys served along were good too.
The sushi was good.
The dimsums could have been better. The skin was thick and the filling tasted okay.
For mains I had dal makhani and cheese chilli kulcha. The dal was good.

However the mocktails were a miss. The savage which was beetroot and guava based mocktail did not have beetroot juice in it and tasted guava flavoured water.

The matcha based mocktail was decent.

For dessert ordered the strawberry Icecream which was all melted, tasted artificially flavoured, had a sugary strawberry crush in it and the Icecream itself was icy.

Overall it’s a good place to party however the experience was a hit & miss for me.

Ps.
The service was disappointing overall.
And the hostess/reservationist outside the restaurant was extremely rude., name_person=1TeaspoonLove}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservation required, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Menu_is_all_vegetarian, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_COMPLETELY_VEGETARIAN]}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Awesome place to vibe with your friends and family. reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=a month ago, review=We opted for buffet here and The primary positive point of our visit was the impressive variety and quality of the dishes offered on the buffet and the ambience. The kitchen staff clearly puts effort into preparation, offering a delightful mix of cuisines.

The Cheese Nuggets were a hit—crispy on the outside and warm/gooey inside. The Manchurian Dry was well-balanced and flavorful. Also, The inclusion of diverse items like Pasta, Khowswey, and various Dumplings was a pleasant surprise and added great value to the buffet. The taste of these dishes was genuinely good. The few Indian dishes available were noted for being flavorful and well-spiced, demonstrating skill across different culinary styles. Had the dining environment matched the quality of the food, this would have been a five-star review and a location we would frequent.

But, there are Major Cleanliness and Hygiene Failure
Unfortunately, the entire experience was severely compromised by unacceptable issues with cleanliness and hygiene in the dining and buffet area. The most critical issue was the pervasive presence of flies actively buzzing around and settling on the open food in the buffet line. This is a severe health and safety risk. Due to the sight of pests, we were forced to avoid several dishes entirely, including many we were looking forward to trying. This lack of sanitation completely overshadowed the good food, making the meal stressful and unappetizing. A buffet setup requires rigorous and constant attention to hygiene. The evident lack of clean-up and pest control suggests a major failure in operational management., name_person=Kiara Soni}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SPECIAL_OFFERS=[Happy_hour, E:DINING_SPECIAL_OFFERS_HAPPY_HOUR]}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Had a very disappointing experience at Mitron, Bandra. We were allotted a table only for 3.5 hours, after which they rudely asked us to vacate—even though we had made a booking through Swiggy/Zomato. Instead, they demanded ₹15,000 extra for table if we wanted to continue. Their words were literally, “We are here to make profit, write whatever review you want.”

On top of that, their happy hours have confusing calculations that don’t make sense. While the vibe may look “cool” from outside, the overall experience was unpleasant. I would not recommend—there are plenty of better cafes and bars in Bandra to explore., name_person=akshata nalavde}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservation required, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA, Bar_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_BAR_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Mitron offers a wonderful ambience when it comes to interior designing and seatings. Devendra was absolutely wonderful with his service—attentive, polite, and made sure we had the best experience. The Bollywood music kept the vibe lively and fun, and the food was simply delicious. Highly recommend this place for a great night out!, name_person=Shubhi Chawla}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=2 months ago, review=⭐☆☆☆☆ (Wish I could give negative stars)

If there’s a global award for “How Not to Run a Club,” Mitron would win by a landslide. Let me break down this disaster of an experience:

💸 Cover Charge Robbery: They charged an obscene cover at the entrance, promising a “premium experience.” What they delivered was the exact opposite of premium—think overpriced chaos with zero value. Spoiler: thanks to delays and drama, no one could even finish the amount we’d already paid cover for.

👥 Crowd Density: Imagine cramming three busloads of people into a broom closet. That’s the vibe. You can’t move, can’t breathe, can’t even lift your hand to sip your drink. Fire safety clearly never crossed management’s mind.

🍹 Drinks & Food Service: If you’re into waiting 45 minutes for a watered-down cocktail and another hour for soggy finger food, this is your paradise. The bar staff moved slower than dial-up internet, and the kitchen seemed to be on strike.

🎶 Music Quality: Calling it music is generous. The DJ seemed to be experimenting with broken YouTube playlists—random transitions, distorted speakers, and bass so bad it rattled your bones but not in a good way. Forget dancing, you’ll be too busy cringing.

🚨 Grand Finale: Police Raid: Just when people thought it couldn’t get worse—surprise! Police stormed the place. Lights on, music cut, everyone herded out like cattle. And here’s the kicker: because of the insane delays in serving, we hadn’t even used up their exorbitant cover charge. Basically, we paid for the privilege of standing in a sweaty, overcrowded box before being kicked out early.

👎 Overall: A masterclass in how to ruin a night out. Unjust cover charges, suffocating crowd, incompetent service, awful music, and the cherry on top—a raid. The only thing intoxicating here is the sheer incompetence.

Final verdict: If you want to burn your money while being miserable, this is the place. Otherwise, avoid like the plague.

The soft, soothing music in the background perfectly complemented the atmosphere, making it a great spot to unwind.

We started off with some loaded nachos topped with gooey cheese that was both satisfying and flavorful. The chicken pizza was equally delightful, with a perfect blend of flavors and a crispy crust. The drinks menu offered a great variety, and we enjoyed a few refreshing cocktails that were expertly crafted. To top it off, we decided to try their hukka, and it turned out to be a highlight of the evening—smooth, flavorful, and a great addition to our laid-back vibe.

The service was another plus. Despite the late hour, the staff was attentive, friendly, and quick to ensure we had everything we needed. It really added to the overall experience.

Soft lighting, tasteful interiors, and thoughtfully arranged seating create the perfect setting for peaceful conversations, celebrations, and relaxed dining 💫.

🍸 The bar counter is an absolute showstopper — elegant, vibrant, and visually stunning. It adds a lounge-like charm to the space and instantly uplifts the mood the moment you walk in 🥂. 🤝 The staff truly deserve appreciation — warm smiles, polite conversations, and genuine hospitality. They are attentive without being intrusive and ensure every dish is served right on time ⏱️. 🍛 Main course dishes were rich, wholesome, and deeply satisfying, reflecting both high-quality ingredients and excellent culinary craftsmanship ❤️.
🥤 Mocktails were refreshing, creative, and visually appealing — perfectly balanced in sweetness and freshness, making them a delight with every sip 🍹.
🍰 Desserts were indulgent yet light, offering a sweet and memorable ending to the entire dining journey 🍫🍓.

📜 As Rumi beautifully said, “Where there is ruin, there is hope for a treasure.” Cray Craft feels like that hidden treasure — quietly elegant, deeply comforting, and surprisingly delightful 💭.

📖 And in the poetic words of Rabindranath Tagore, “Let your life lightly dance on the edges of time like dew on the tip of a leaf.” Dining at Cray Craft feels just like that — light, joyful, and timeless 🌸.

💫 Final Verdict:
Cray Craft is a place where ambience soothes, flavours excite, and hospitality touches the heart 🥰. A restaurant that offers not just food, but emotions, memories, and moments that stay with you long after you leave 🌟.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for quality food, beautiful ambience, and genuine hospitality in Andheri East ❤️🍽️

Loved the vibe — a beautiful glasshouse with nature all around! Tried the Watermelon Avocado Mousse, Mushroom Rava Fry, Grilled Cajun Prawns, Thai Grilled Snapper, Truffle Japanese Fried Rice, and the unique Old Madras – their Indian banana split twist 🍌✨ Everything looked stunning and tasted even better!

#TheConservatoryJuhu #RoopammEats #RoopammExperience #MumbaiEats #CafeGoals #FoodieFinds, name_person=ROOPAM LAKHANPAL}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Other, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=We visited The Conservatory a number of times during our short stay in Juhu. We were also visiting with our very busy one year old and the staff were really friendly and gave him a cute light toy to entertain him., name_person=Samantha Jeeawock}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a month ago, review=The conservatory has some really good dessert options all with its unique taste and very rich in flavours. Their dates and miso is really worth a try. Wonderful staff. Perfect ambience for a date night., name_person=ekta bhatt}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=We were so happy that finally Juhu has a place where we can take our golden retriever with us. The ambience of The Conservatory is superb, feels like sitting in the middle of plants and trees like a real conservatory.
We had seen it many times from outside and the interiors didn’t disappoint us at all.
But the food is very very disappointing. I would not like to write a bad review but we actually didn’t complete two of the three dishes  we ordered including the mocktail.
The pizza was just okay. But the Bhel had some ingredient which had a very strong taste and so did the paneer.
Waiters were friendly but didn’t know much.

And it’s toooo expensive. We felt that we were left hungry at the end in spite of having spent quite a bit!!, name_person=Swati Chitalia Leading to Light}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=For a long time, I wanted to visit the Conservatory for its bright sun-filled glass roof terrace setting. We called them at the very last minute on Saturday morning for dinner reservations, and they said we can accommodate you for an early dinner slot between 6:30 to 8:30 pm. We were initially booked for a table in a lower area, but on our request based on availability, they happily moved us to the terrace. In early evening sunlight, the terrace set up was stunning, with light classy furniture and tastefully placed plants everywhere! And then the sun went down and the place glowed warm dim lighting. For starters the Beetroot Thecha Toast with the subtle fiery taste of thecha and loads of avocado and cream was great! The very popular heartily portioned Bombil Fish and Chips was amazing! Only a Bengali chef can do justice to the tricky fish of Bombil, without making it too heavy or oily. For mains, we had the Parsi Mutton Kheema pizza with six slices and lavish kheema topping, which was a great blend of Italian and Parsi cuisines. We ended our fantastic dinner with heart-warming French Toast for desserts, loaded with butter, the right amount of sweetness, and fresh berries. We paid 4k between the two of us for four dishes, which makes it a tad bit expensive. For the posh Juhu ambience, the quality ingredients, and the chef’s innovation and craft, maybe the price is justified! The other reviews for this place are like playing a game of one truth and two lies. Most reviews suggest the staff is unfriendly, the food doesn’t taste good with small portions, and the place is expensive. The truth is, the place is EXPENSIVE, but the food tastes great with rightsized potions, and the staff is super accommodating and professional!, name_person=Naresh Shah}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 weeks ago, review="Glasshouse themed restaurant in Juhu..So I visited a newly opened glasshouse themed European/South East Asian restaurant by master restaurateur Suren Joshi in Juhu.Experience a glass house vibe and food that's inspired from South Asian and European cuisine with nature all around. Loved the cocktail menu and especially floral alchemy.Loved the pesto burrata wood fired pizza, the hummus was also super delicious. The jaffna mutton takes your tastebuds on an amazing journey and the chocolate gateaux literally melts in your mouth.Loved the beautiful vibe!, name_person=Tulsi Mehta}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Avocado_Toast], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Great place in one of the most bustling neighborhoods. Offcourse the terrace is the place to enjoy this unique ambience and its what most patrons walk in for n so its a bit tough if u are in couple n threes  but if you walk in five n six u might hv a better chance as the bigger tables are on the top deck. The food is good n tasty and keeps up to the palate of this upscale neighborhood. The avocado toast, the pesto pizza, the cocktails n mocktails were good, the risotto was sumptuous, and the very atmanirbhar chhena poda with jaggery syrup n a dollop of icecream  made its mark as fibe dine dessert. Tirimisu became pass'e, name_person=Shyam Haridas}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Ambeince is very nice. Liked the upper floor sitting area.
We ordered
1. water chestnut salad - very nice in taste, all the veggies were fresh and tasty, salad dressing was also very good.
2. Avocado toast - This was superb,  we loved it.
3. Hummus and veggies - garlic flavour Creamy humus , awesome in taste with grilled veggies.
4. Speghetti Pesto - this was suggested by the chef. It was ok not that great.
5. Desserts - Chocolate and Coffee - super yummy
Overall a good place to chill with friends, name_person=Preeti Parab}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Nice cosy place to chill, amazing ambiance, good food and decent service.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Amazing vibe, soothing music, super tasty food and delicious cocktails!}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=We also ordered white sauce spaghetti creamy pasta (customised) with veggies.}"]

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Having lived and worked in Japan, albeit many moons ago, I was not expecting to be reminded of the tastes and feel of a typical izakaya in the land of the rising sun, in, of all places, Bandra, Mumbai.
We were ushered to our seating by a raucous welcome from the Kuuraku staff, which was more reminiscent of the Wankhede Stadium than a Japanese restaurant. But there was a effervescence about the staff at Kuuraku, reflecting the confidence that they have in their excellent food.
We ordered the Special Kushi Course, comprising 5 sticks of yakitori. The standout of this was the chicken tail. It was so good that we ordered two extra sticks of this, named bonjiri shio. We also ordered a portion of pork belly yakitori although this was very slightly disappointing as it was a little on the tough side. Another slight disappointment was the chargrilled asparagus wrapped in pork belly. Again, the pork belly wasn't as tender as I expected and the asparagus was a little small and fibrous. However, the edamame challenge was a lot of fun. The idea is to grab as much edamame as possible with one hand - and what you grab is what you get to eat. I used my goalkeeper hands to grab, what the server told me was an over par amount. The edamame was quite good too. The crunchy ebi roll was very generous too coming as a generous portion. The temperature of the rice was spot on as was the consistency. Could the quality of the rice be higher as in Japan? Well yes if you can get that rice but otherwise it really was excellent. The same goes for the pork rice. Here the consistency or the stickiness of the rice was more important than in the ebi roll and if they could get better rice it was be amazing. The slight disappointment was the inclusion of bell peppers. Heresy! Finally, the tea was served in a beautiful black pot, again, very true to Japan.
All in all this was an excellent place with a really true feel of Japan, helped also by the constant stream of Japanese music and the service was particularly excellent. ["{guided_block={}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=I visited Bayroute and honestly, the food and drinks were such a refreshing experience.

Their Hummus Bayroute was super creamy, and the labneh with zaatar and pine nuts made it even better.
I loved the Chicken Afrikaan which was spicy, flavourful and perfectly grilled with that hint of cumin.
The Kebab Istanbul was a melt-in-the-mouth mutton seekh kebab that tasted amazing.
Even the prawns were delicious, cooked in a tangy tomato gravy that balanced the flavours well.
And to end the meal, the Baklava with gulkand ice cream was just heavenly.
Crispy layers, nuts, rose brittles everything came together perfectly.
Overall, it was a wholesome, flavourful meal that felt special from start to finish.
Would definitely go back again!, name_person=Tanishka Chavan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Bayroute BKC never disappoints — but this time, they’ve truly outdone themselves with their Kebab & Meze Festival. The moment you step in, the ambience wraps you in warm golden lights and Mediterranean charm — it’s luxe yet cozy, elegant yet soulful.

I started my meal with the Ruyhan, a bright orange cooler that’s refreshing and slightly citrusy — the perfect start to a rich Middle Eastern feast. Their Zaffrani Chai was another star — aromatic, creamy, and comforting, with just the right hint of saffron.

Coming to the food — the Moroccan Chermoula Prawns were perfectly grilled and bursting with smoky, tangy flavours, while the Djej Al Jibneh was every cheese lover’s dream come true — tender chicken layered with molten cheese that melts in your mouth.

For mains, I tried the Kebab Koobideh, and it was absolute perfection — juicy, buttery kebabs served with saffron rice that complemented every bite. The textures, the balance of spice, and that authentic Persian touch made it unforgettable.

And of course, no visit to Bayroute is complete without dessert — the Chocolate Kunafa was the ultimate showstopper! Crisp golden strands on top, gooey chocolate inside, and just the right level of sweetness — the perfect ending to a luxurious meal.

Overall, Bayroute continues to deliver an experience that goes beyond just food — it’s a full-on sensory journey through the Middle East. Every dish feels thoughtfully crafted, the staff is super courteous, and the attention to detail is immaculate.

✨ Must Try:
•	Moroccan Chermoula Prawns 🦐
•	Djej Al Jibneh 🧀
•	Kebab Koobideh 🥩
•	Chocolate Kunafa 🍫
•	Zaffrani Chai ☕

Peach Iced Tea is a refreshing burst of flavor in every sip.

Kalimiri Cheddar Broccoli
From the moment the dish arrives, the vibrant green of the broccoli is contrasted beautifully by the creamy richness of the cheddar cheese, infused with the subtle yet captivating warmth of kalimiri (black pepper). The aroma is inviting—cheesy, slightly spicy, and earthy.The broccoli retains a nice crunch, providing a fresh, earthy base to the dish. The cheddar is indulgently smooth, delivering a familiar, comforting creaminess. But what sets this dish apart is the kalimiri. The black pepper’s spice gently lingers, balancing the richness of the cheese with a subtle heat. The tender yet slightly crisp broccoli pairs wonderfully with the velvety melted cheddar. Perfect for those looking for something familiar with a hint of spice. However, the spice of cardamom was overpowered and sat on tongue, so every bite was full of cardamom, which made the next dishes taste like it too.

Tiranga Kofte
Visually, the Tiranga Kofte presents itself well, with three distinct layers symbolizing the colours of the Indian flag. The presentation is appealing and sets high expectations for a flavourful experience. However, the dish's appearance slightly outweighs its taste. The kofte has a decent blend of spices, though the flavours don’t quite come together as cohesively as expected. Each layer brings something different—the green layer offers a mild herbiness, the white layer is a bit bland, and the orange section has a touch of heat. However, the balance between them feels uneven, with the spices not blending as harmoniously as they should.
Since the appetizer had cardamom hint which was overpowering, the outer layer green part of kofta also felt it had cardamom which wasn’t pleasant on tongue.

Amritsari Kulcha
The Amritsari-styled kulcha is a delightful treat. Each bite offers a perfect blend of crispy exterior and soft, flavorful interior. The traditional stuffing of spiced potatoes and herbs is well-seasoned, providing a hearty and satisfying taste

Lachha Paratha
The Lachha Paratha is a standout with its perfectly layered, crispy texture. Each bite reveals a delightful combination of flaky. Though they forgot to add butter because it was some miscommunication, It was perfect size not big not small.

Tadkewali Dal
Tadkewali Dal delivers a heartwarming, flavorful experience. The smoky aroma from the tadka (tempering) hits you immediately, preparing your senses for a rich and comforting dish. The lentils are cooked to perfection—and well-spiced. The tadka of ghee, cumin, garlic, and chilies adds depth, bringing a savory warmth to every bite. Each spoonful is a harmonious blend of velvety dal and robust, fragrant spices. It’s a perfect dish for anyone seeking bold yet balanced flavors in a simple, soul-satisfying homely meal.

Jeera rice
Jeera Rice is simplicity at its finest. The delicate aroma of cumin wafts through each grain, giving the rice a warm, earthy fragrance. The cumin seeds add a subtle crunch and a toasted, nutty flavor that complements the perfectly cooked, fluffy rice.

Halwa (Complementary)
Rich and buttery, each spoonful melts in your mouth, releasing a wave of sweetness that’s perfectly balanced with hints of cardamom. The texture is smooth yet slightly grainy, with bursts of flavor from the roasted nuts scattered throughout.

Hospitality
The hospitality at this restaurant is exceptional. From the moment we walked in, the staff was warm, attentive, and welcoming. They ensured every detail was taken care of, making us feel comfortable and valued throughout the meal. Service was prompt, yet never rushed, with the team showing genuine care in their recommendations and interactions. Their professionalism, combined with friendly smiles, truly elevated our experience. Ashish and Prasad served great hospitality to us.

Ambience
The ambience of Rasoi strikes the perfect balance between luxury and comfort. The sun roof, the all glass facade, adds a wonderful charm to the cosy space. The open kitchen also made

10/10 would recommend if you’re feeling a bit bougie and want to impress your date. It’s tucked away enough for it to be a discovery, but also buzzing to not feel like you’re the only people to discover it- a balance that’s so rare.

We ordered quite a few things from the menu, but the highlight of it all were two things: the Pork & Smoke, which was the best thing I’ve tried in a while. Really smoky, succulent, meal-in-your-mouth bits of pork belly, over a mash, and layered with spices, herbs, a little bits of funk. So, so satisfying. If you eat pork, don’t miss it!

The other highlight was the Rasam inspired cocktail- blew our collective socks off. Such a refined cocktail, and so seasonable. Despite the impressive technique, it didn’t feel over intellectual and genuinely had a rasam after taste.

The rest was fine, nothing to write home about. But definitely worth frequent visits (if you can get a spot!), name_person=Sumit Sen}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, 3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Where do I even begin? The vibe, obviously. Imagine a dive bar, but it decided to clean up its act and look classy for once. That’s Bombay Daak. I’m a sucker for dive bars, and this one just gets it. Dark, moody, but still modern enough to make you go “okay, this is cool.” And the music, oh the music. In true Bangalore fashion, they dropped “Santhoshake,” that was it. I was emotionally invested.

Now the food, let me tell you, they had me at Shikaar Ka Achaar. Rabbit preserve in some mango-pickle-style masala, served with pav. I’m not exaggerating when I say I could eat that every day and still not get bored. The rest of the food was great too, but that rabbit? Unreal.

And then came Whistle Podu, a gin-based rasam cocktail. I know, sounds like chaos in a glass, but it worked. Refreshing, a little spicy, and very “what the hell, why is this so good?” kind of moment.

Service? Quick, friendly, and totally on point.

In short, go to Bombay Daak. Eat, drink, vibe. Thank me later (preferably with a Whistle Podu in hand)., name_person=Maanush Dev}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The food, the staff, the drinks everything is just an experience.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=If you love cocktails that celebrate Indian flavours, this is the place to be.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Very small space Seating a bit too close to each other.}"]

But the bar tender Japit was able to guide us to two spirit forward cocktails..of which we would highly recommend the el presidente. The staff was courteous and attentive, ensuring we had a smooth dining experience. Prices are slightly on the higher side, but the overall quality, ambience, and service make it worth it.

Highly recommended for a memorable dining experience or a special evening out!, name_person=prasanjit devnath}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=10-30 min, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=2 months ago, review=One8 Commune is a resto bar co owned by Virat Kohli, with stylish interiors, comfort food, a upscale and nice décor. Juhu outlet is in the famous Kishore Kumar bungalow.

Ambience & Interior - The design is beautiful, with earthy tones, glass ceiling, good lighting, greenery, decorative lamps and mirrors. Multiple types of seating, cozy corners, outdoors, glasshouse style spaces.

Menu - The restaurant offers a mix of global comfort food + twists. Cocktail / mocktail menu is creative. Food is “good” but not excellent for what is charged. Some dishes mentioned not matching expectations for the price. Portions are sometimes seen as small.

Good for Occasions & special dinners. The place has a lively vibe, especially later in the evening.

The staff is polite, but often ignorant, delays, or not being shown to the table properly even if reserved. Reservation issues.
It tends to be crowded, especially evenings/weekends. Waiting time even with reservations.

Restrooms being small, dim or not very clean.

If you’re looking for a visually impressive place, good ambience, something more upscale casually, One8 Commune is a solid choice., name_person=Piyush Kabra}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=The place serves multicuisine food and there is no theme. that said, if you’re in the mood to splurge or just got your bonus, this is a great spot for a cozy dinner and chill evening. the vibe is classy yet relaxed, making it worth the visit.

hogged. logged. signed off with empty wallets., name_person=Raunak Naik}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, 5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT, Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=3 months ago, review=I visited One8 Commune, Bandra recently and overall it was a really good experience.

Ambience: The ambience was amazing, especially at night. It felt pleasant, calm, and premium. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, so you can choose as per your preference. The space is well designed and can accommodate both couples and larger groups comfortably.

Food: They offer a variety of special dishes, right from starters to mains and desserts. Everything I tried was delicious and well presented.
⭐ Chicken Soup – 5/5
⭐ Dumplings – 5/5
⭐ Tom Kha Chicken – 5/5
⭐ Sichuan Pepper Chicken – 5/5
⭐ Truffle Butter Mushroom – 4.5/5
⭐ Greek Chicken – 4.5/5

Price: It is on the costlier side with a 10% service charge, but fair for the overall experience. Approx. ₹4000 for two people.

Overall, it’s a great place to enjoy premium food and ambience in Bandra. Definitely worth visiting for a special outing., name_person=Gokulraj}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Had a lovely dining experience at One8 Commune, Juhu,the vibe and interiors are stylish yet comfortable, and the menu offers some creative vegetarian and vegan-friendly dishes. Here’s what I tried:
•	Veg Tom Kha : A warm, fragrant soup with the right balance of coconut milk creaminess and subtle spices. Comforting and full of flavor, it’s a perfect start to the meal.
•	Miso Spinach Tofu Gyoza : Absolutely delicious! The gyoza were delicate and well-steamed, with a lovely umami hit from the miso and spinach filling. A dish I’d definitely order again.
•	Crispy Lotus Root : This one didn’t work for me. The garlic was overpowering and masked the natural crispiness and flavor of the lotus root. Would’ve preferred a more balanced seasoning.
•	Black Bean Hummus : Smooth, earthy, and flavorful, with just the right richness. Paired perfectly with the accompaniments and had a unique twist compared to regular hummus.
•	Avocado Truffle Bites : A standout dish! The creamy avocado with the truffle aroma was indulgent and beautifully presented. Rich yet light enough to enjoy without feeling heavy.
•	Fresh Juice : Simple, refreshing, and a great palate cleanser between bites.
•	Vegan Torte Texture : The perfect sweet ending. Silky, chocolatey, and well-textured without being overly sweet. A wonderful choice for those who want a vegan dessert that doesn’t compromise on taste.

Overall, I enjoyed the food and the atmosphere. Except for the lotus root dish, everything else was excellent and thoughtfully prepared. Great spot in Juhu for a meal with a modern, global twist., name_person=Padmini Dixit}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=We had  planned to celebrate our 1st wedding anniversary and it was really a very good decision to do so the ambience was well decorated and  so was the food which was served to Us. This is another excellent recommendation by my friend Shakun. We are staying at Novotel in Juhu, so we enjoyed a leisurely walk on the beach to reach the restaurant. We were welcomed very graciously and seated by the hostess. Since we had walked on the beach and were all very sandy, my husband, my daughters (aged 5 and 7), and I went to the restroom to wash up. When we returned to our table, I was pleasantly surprised to find it set up with a kids’ menu featuring lots of activities, along with sets of crayons and a chef hat crown that both my girls promptly put on. This was such a refreshing change on our 13th day in India, as until now we hadn’t seen a kids menu specifically geared for children in any of the restaurants we’ve visited. It was definitely a highlight for me.

We were kindly greeted by our servers Mukul and Manojit Roy, and their service throughout our meal was outstanding. They offered thoughtful recommendations, anticipated our needs, checked in at just the right moments without being intrusive, and treated our whole family with genuine warmth and respect.

For dinner, both my daughters wanted popcorn chicken—actually their favorite back home—and they were thrilled to see it on the menu. One chose a vanilla milkshake and the other a chocolate milkshake. The popcorn chicken was a bit spicy for their mild palates—but they loved the milkshakes.

My husband and I chose the Fish and Mixed Meats kebab platter. Mukul honestly informed us that the fish was unavailable, and substituted another chicken kebab, which we were completely fine with. We ordered the kebabs as served, thinking our girls might want to try them—and it turned out to be an excellent decision. The girls devoured the chicken reshmi kebab. It was so satisfying to see them enjoying something from the Indian menu, knowing we’ve found another safe and delicious option for them here in India.

We also ordered Rawalpindi Gosht, extra spicy, along with roomali roti and rice to accompany our meal. My husband was delighted with the kebabs—every bite was melt‑in‑your‑mouth tender. The Rawalpindi Gosht was succulent and richly flavored; we absolutely loved it. Despite being full, Mukul suggested the baked motichoor rabri for dessert. It was absolutely delicious—the warm, layered sweetness with the motichoor bits and creamy rabri was the perfect end to our meal.

We loved everything about this place. From the walk-in welcome to the thoughtful touches for our kids, the exceptional service by Mukul and Manojit, and the outstanding food, Copper Chimney Juhu made our evening truly memorable. We loved it!, name_person=Nadia Halim Dziobkowska}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations not required, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Tucked away in Bandra’s ever-evolving culinary landscape, Napoli by Shatranj presents itself as a polished neighbourhood Italian eatery. But despite the charming name and the promise of a thoughtfully curated Italian menu, the experience left more to be desired than remembered.

The meal started on a reasonably positive note. The Spaghetti Carbonara arrived with a creamy, well-emulsified sauce that clung nicely to the strands of pasta. The presence of pork gave the dish some much-needed body and savouriness, though it was hard to tell if guanciale was used. The overall flavour was pleasant, if unremarkable, and the dish did what it needed to without dazzling.

Unfortunately, the meal only declined from there.

The Steak, requested medium rare, did arrive at the correct doneness, which deserves acknowledgement. But that’s where the positives end. The cut of meat itself was a poor choice—tough, chewy, and devoid of the tenderness one expects from a properly sourced and rested steak. For a dish that typically commands a premium on any menu, this one felt more like an afterthought than a main event.

The Salmon Bruschetta fared no better. Topped with pallid, clearly farmed salmon that lacked freshness, the dish suffered from a lack of depth and definition. The cream which is meant to support or complement actually ended up dominating the plate. The result was a bland, vaguely fishy bite that could have come from any cold appetiser counter rather than a kitchen claiming Italian sophistication.

And therein lies the central issue with Napoli by Shatranj. While it gestures toward authenticity and finesse, the food rarely lands with the kind of precision or character that might distinguish it. The pricing, meanwhile, reflects a confidence that the food does not back up. At best, it feels like another stylish Bandra restaurant with a name borrowed from Naples but very little of its soul.

In the end, Napoli by Shatranj is not a terrible meal, but it’s a forgettable one—and that might be worse., name_person=Mithun Mohandas}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The menu had a wide variety of options, and the food was simply delicious.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Being vegetarian, this place served me the best spaghetti pasta I could ask for.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good food, great service, convenient location, great ambience}"]
