Tucked away in the Nine Dine food court at Jio World Drive, Indigo Deli is a hidden gem that serves up some of the most delicious and authentic European-inspired cuisine. My friend and I stopped by for a quick bite and tried the Margherita Pizza, which exceeded our expectations in every way.

Margherita Pizza: A Masterclass in Simplicity

The Margherita Pizza at Indigo Deli was a masterclass in simplicity. The crust was paper-thin, with a delicate crunch that gave way to a soft, airy interior. The sauce was tangy and rich, made with the finest San Marzano tomatoes. And the mozzarella? Creamy, melted to perfection, and generously sprinkled over the top. Each bite was a flavor bomb, with the perfect balance of salty, sweet, and savory.

Ambiance: Convenient Food Court Setting

As part of the Nine Dine food court, Indigo Deli offers a convenient and casual dining experience. The food court is well-maintained and clean, with ample seating and a lively atmosphere.

Service: Friendly and Efficient

The service at Indigo Deli was friendly and efficient, with the staff happy to answer our questions about the menu and make recommendations. Our order was prepared quickly, and we were impressed by the speed and accuracy of the service.

Verdict

Indigo Deli is a must-visit destination for anyone craving authentic and delicious European-inspired cuisine. The Margherita Pizza is a standout dish, and I'm excited to try more of their offerings in the future.

Price: Moderate (around ₹500-₹800 per person)

Recommended for: Foodies, pizza lovers, and anyone looking for a quick, delicious, and satisfying meal.

If you’re a fan of Indigo Deli and have always missed out on downing a few drinks with your food, then be rest assured because that department has now been taken care of.

Wait time for each food was around 45 minutes to 1 hr that’s too much, waiters staff are not available to order next dish, pizza was tasteless and bread undercooked. nothing is good to visit this place, we have booked it still waiting time  was high with uncomfortable seats and table.
Spoiled our celebration😦, name_person=Dixita Patel}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_STREET_PARKING, Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=11 months ago, review=We had visited this place for Dinner and we had made a reservation ahead of time through Zomato Dining. This place is housed at the top floor and the route to the restaurant goes through the Mitron cafe. We had to wait and cross through the entire queue which was supposedly for Mitron to get to Roofberries. Although the place is at the rooftop and was expected to be open, it was not. It was covered with plastic from all the sides giving no view of the outside.
This place allows Smoking and offers Sheesha service so it's not recommended for people who are not comfortable with it as we would have other customers having it around us.
We had ordered Pizza, Bao, Lobster Sushi, Fried Rice, and a chicken starter. The pizza was good and flavourful and the Sushi was also nice. However the Bao and the rice were a let down as the Bao didn't have any flavour and felt like we were just eating the Bread with very little stuffing. The rice was sticky and a little on the sweeter side.

Overall I would say this place is a one time visit for the experience., name_person=Kaustubh Acharekar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Born and raised in Mumbai’s suburbs, I’ve dined at countless cafés and rooftops — but Roofberries truly steals the spotlight. Their curated Pan-Asian, Continental, and Indian menu, cozy rooftop vibe, and exceptional team (Mr. Ashish Pawar, Mr. Ashish Amde, Olivia, and Narendra) make every visit unforgettable. Mocktails that deserve sequels, interiors that mesmerize — Roofberries is where food meets feel. Perfect for the festive season and absolutely worth a revisit!, name_person=Shifa Siddiqui}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in}, time_line=3 years ago, review=Prettiest rooftop resturant in mumbai which serves indian, chinese, italian, continental food. The ambience here is just classy, & it looks even more beautiful after 6pm. One of the best place to chill with friends or your partner. Captain Bikram’s service was just amazing. He made sure that everything was just perfect.

In cocktails/ mocktails we ordered the berry booster mocktail, which is definitely a must try option, its very refreshing & tastes amazing. In cocktail we ordered the Dragon G & T cocktail which was based of dragon fruit.

They serve different varities of starters here, but we wanted to go for indo- chinese starters so we ordered the classic paneer chilli & java chicken lollipops. Both the items were delicious & were actually tempting.

In main course we ordered the chilli garlic noodles, which were spicy & very tasty. We also ordered a Quatro Formaggi pizza which was super cheesy & had thin crust.

Captain Bikram recommended us to try the flaming hot chocolate brownie dessert so did we order. The presentation was good & its tastes like brownie with icecream., name_person=Esha kulkarni}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Amazing ❤️ place and amazing cocktails with food like yummy yum!!}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=We had ordered Pizza, Bao, Lobster Sushi, Fried Rice, and a chicken starter.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Great music, romantic ambience, great service by the staffs.}"]

Thank you for taking the time to consider my comment., name_person=Sameer Chougule}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Would not recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Somewhat difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Extremely Disappointing Experience – Not Worth the Hype or the Money 🛑

We visited Agrezi Dhaba on Saturday, 31st May 2025, as a group of 3 married couples along with 2 kids, hoping for a pleasant evening out. Unfortunately, the experience turned out to be an utter disappointment from start to finish.

First of all, imagine walking into a restaurant on a Saturday night and seeing only two waiters managing the entire floor. That alone sets the tone for what’s to come. Service was painfully slow and chaotic, with one waiter literally sprinting from table to table trying to handle everything. It felt like watching a poorly managed event, not a professional dining experience.

I had made a booking through Zomato, only to be told by the waiter that pricing would differ if we paid via the app compared to paying directly. Why play such shady pricing games with customers? This kind of misleading marketing is simply unacceptable.

To make matters worse, some of my friends ordered from the bar, only to be told they were out of Blenders Pride by 9:30 PM. On a Saturday night? That’s basic stock management gone wrong.

Then came the confusing bar menu experience. The waiter actually insisted we decide how many pegs we were going to drink upfront because only then we’d be given a certain rate. Who does that? It’s ridiculous to expect guests to decide their entire order before even settling in. The pricing for single, 6-pegs, and 12-pegs was all over the place and made no sense at all.

The hospitality was shockingly poor. Since we had two young kids, we requested Wi-Fi so they could watch cartoons while the adults had dinner. There was no mobile network coverage, and the Wi-Fi was denied. The reason? According to the manager, sharing Wi-Fi would crash their system. Honestly, it was laughable—we actually joked about it being the “joke of the year.” This level of excuse-making is unprofessional at best.

If all this wasn’t enough, the waiter later rushed us to make the payment, standing by our table repeatedly asking “Google Pay ya cash?” When I asked for 5 minutes, his response was: “Jaldi karo, mujhe bhi ghar nikalna hai.” Absolutely unacceptable. We were still wrapping up our night and he made it feel like we were being kicked out. If there’s a rule that bills must be settled before midnight, then inform guests clearly in advance—not after pressuring them in the middle of their meal.

As for the food, it was bland, overpriced, and underwhelming. For a bill of ₹8500, we expected much better quality and taste. It felt like basic food dressed up with fancy pricing.

In short, Agrezi Dhaba completely ruined our Saturday night outing. Poor service, rude staff, lack of basic amenities, and average food at inflated prices.

I somehow end up having their tiramisu every single time — it’s truly to die for!

The avocado toast and cappuccino are my almost-every-time favorites — simple, comforting, and consistently good. I’ve also tried their risotto and a bunch of other dishes, which are all quite nice, but I always find myself going back to my favorites again and again.

The staff here is well-trained and courteous. Getting a table without a reservation during peak hours can be a bit tricky, but most times I’ve been accommodated politely. The lady at the reception can come across as a tad uptight, though I understand she’s just doing her job.

The tables upstairs are set quite close, leaving little room for privacy, but given Bombay’s space crunch and the café’s buzzing location, it’s understandable.

reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"Kinjal Jethwa\",\"time_line\":\"5 days ago\",\"review\":\"Joshi House had been on my bucket list for the longest time, and finally experiencing their soulful modern Indian cuisine felt truly special. Every preparation reflects precision, thoughtfulness and beautiful detailing. The d\u00e9cor is minimal yet elegant, creating a calm, relaxing space \u2014 a quiet indulgence where city chaos fades away. The ambience, lighting and vibes are effortlessly soothing.\\n\\nThe menu is thoughtfully curated, where taste feels like a language of its own. We began with Pom Rajwadi and Charcoal Breeze \u2014 mocktails that turned flavours into memories. The Balinese Bhel and Sweet Potato Shammi Chaat were outstanding, followed by the heavenly Avocado Chutney Toast. The Lazeez Paneer Biryani was rich, aromatic and perfectly balanced. We ended on a high with Ode to Kerala, a smooth dessert with 75% rich chocolate that was absolutely scrumptious. A truly magical dining experience.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Lunch\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b91,400\u20131,600\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL\":\"Quiet, easy to talk\"}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Pooja Mandal\",\"time_line\":\"4 weeks ago\",\"review\":\"I recently enjoyed a delightful spread at this spot, and the experience truly stood out. The starters were a highlight: the Berry Almond Mingle offered a perfect balance of sweet and nutty flavors, while the Pom Rajwadi impressed with its rich, aromatic profile. The Mushroom Galouti Puff was flaky and savory, and the Sweet Potato Shammi Chaat delivered a satisfying blend of textures. The Tandoori Corn Salad added a refreshing crunch to the table.\\n\\nThe main course, Paneer Khurchan, was prepared exactly as requested\u2014spicy and full of depth, accompanied by three soft rotis that complemented the dish beautifully.\\n\\nService was attentive, and the digital ordering system made the experience seamless. Overall, the food, flavors, and presentation were exceptional, making it a must\u2011visit for anyone seeking a memorable meal.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Lunch\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b91,800\u20132,000\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL\":\"Quiet, easy to talk\",\"GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE\":[\"2_people\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS\":\"Highly recommend\",\"GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS\":[\"Vegetarian_options\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS\"]}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Saloni Jain\",\"time_line\":\"a month ago\",\"review\":\"Had a lovely North Indian meal at Joshi House!\\nThe Shammi Sweet Potato Chaat was just yum \u2014 perfectly balanced and so flavourful.\\nThe Beetroot Malai Kofta was my personal favourite\u2026 rich, creamy and absolutely delicious.\\nAnd the Ghevar \u2014 woww, the perfect sweet ending!\\nOverall, amazing food, great vibe. Definitely visiting again!\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Lunch\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b9800\u20131,000\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL\":\"Quiet, easy to talk\",\"GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE\":[\"Suitable_for_all_group_sizes\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL\"]}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Bhavin Parekh\",\"time_line\":\"2 months ago\",\"review\":\"It\u2019s the relaunched version (2.0) of Joshi House (formerly in Bandra) now in Worli Koliwada. The emphasis is now strongly on Indian regional flavours (especially coastal & Rajasthani). The place is visually striking with good lighting, atmosphere within gives both grandeur and warmth. The space is spread over three floors, each with a distinct mood.\\n\u2022 Ground floor has al fresco seating (patio style), greenery, the entrance has terracotta pots, Jaisalmer stone jaali screens.\\n\u2022 First floor is more formal dining: yellow cement flooring, textured walls, sculptural wood furniture. Softer, more calming.\\n\u2022 Second floor / Bar area: moodier, more intimate. Deep hues (violet walls, etc.), vaulted ceilings, artistic murals (e.g. hand\u2011painted tiger motifs).\\nDetails of Rajasthani heritage show up subtly in decor: brass, stone, carved wood, warm earthy textures - feels lived\u2011in, comfortable.\\nThe cuisine is rooted in Indian regional flavours, especially coastal and Rajasthani. Sea food gets centre stage. Vegetarian fare isn\u2019t an afterthought. Top dishes like Balinese bhel, Dabeli sliders, Sweet potato shammi chaat (must try), Thecha brie toast, Mushroom benne dosa,Truffle Palak Saag with burrata along with makai roti, Beetroot malai kofta along with Malbari parotta etc get good attention. Desserts get creative - the Ghevar (Rajasthani dessert), Paan Magnum Kulfi etc. Nostalgic yet with some innovations. Cocktail and Mocktail is robust: creative mocktails like Sunset sipper, Berry almond mingle, Pom rajwadi, etc. are flavourful and refreshing.\\nService is generally attentive, with staff that understand the menu, guide and explains regional flavours. Joshi House Worli is a strong evolution from its Bandra version - more rooted, more coherent in theme, more local (both in ingredients and aesthetics). If you appreciate ambience, design, and wanting to explore awesome regional Indian cuisine with flair, it's a great pick. For special occasions or a nice evening out, it\u2019s well worth it.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Nidhi jain\",\"time_line\":\"3 weeks ago\",\"review\":\"Loved the place very much. It was perfect for lunch as well as dinner. They have set menu which is totally worth a try. I had tried their starters in vegetarian and I loved their thecha brie toast very much. It was super cheesy and delicious. It was different and worth trying . It was crispy and crunchy. The other starter I tried was their sweet potato shammi chaat and that too was delicious to taste. In main course, I tried their truffle palak saag with makai roti. The subzi was good in quantity and i also loved their innovation in this dish as they added burata cheese on the top of the gravy and the makai roti was soft and tasty. Their cocktails were worth a try. They were innovative. I tried their hazel drink and it had good taste of coffee and the other was also nice. I liked their dessert and mainly their presentation in that. I tried their kerala chocolate ganache and it was served with a sorbet which made the dessert fantastic in taste.\\nThe food was good and the service was also quick and nice.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b91,800\u20132,000\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL\":\"Quiet, easy to talk\",\"GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE\":[\"2_people\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO\",\"Suitable_for_all_group_sizes\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS\":\"Highly recommend\",\"GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO\":[\"Large_vegetarian_selection\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS\":[\"Vegetarian_options\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS\"]}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Nikita K\",\"time_line\":\"a month ago\",\"review\":\"\u201cHuman Jaha Pe Tameez Suey Khaya Hai, Bhuke Hi Wapas Aaye Hai\u201d\\n-A go-getter Foodie.\\n\\nIf luxury had a desi heart, it would look exactly like Joshi House. In the heart of Worli, this fine dining gem is a North Indian food lover\u2019s dream \u2014 blending authentic flavours with a refined modern touch. The ambience is simply stunning \u2014 warm lights, earthy d\u00e9cor, soft music, and an old-world charm that makes you want to stay longer. The perfect spot for an indulgent evening with friends, family, or even a quiet soulful date night.\\n\\nFor mocktails, we started with the Spice Sutra and the House Special J House. Both drinks were beautifully presented \u2014 vibrant, aromatic, and bursting with layered flavours.\\n\\nFor Appetisers,  we called for Sweet Potato Shammi Chaat which was an absolute delight! The soft shammi with the sweetness of potato, dash of ice-cold ice cream (Yes! Ice Cream) layer and tang from chutneys created a perfect harmony of flavours and Chutney Avocado Toast which was a creative twist on the classic! Creamy avocado topped with tangy Indian chutneys, giving every bite a fresh and fusion-style punch.\\n\\nThe bar was already set high by the appetisers, we were looking forward for the mains now. Next we ordered Beetroot Malai Kofta Curry which was smooth, and rich. The beetroot koftas were melt-in-the-mouth soft, perfectly paired with a luscious malai gravy. Enjoyed it with Cheese Garlic Naan, which was fluffy and indulgent and Paneer Tikka Biryani which was Fragrant, flavorful, and perfectly spiced. The tender paneer tikka chunks added that royal touch, making it a must-try for every biryani lover.\\n\\nAaaaand, for desserts we chose  Joshi House Ghevar \u2013 Our absolute favourite! A stunning dessert that truly stole the show. The presentation, the textures, and the sweetness \u2014 everything was on point. A perfect modern take on a traditional Rajasthani classic. Where was this all these years?\\n\\nJoshi House truly stands out not just for its food but for the complete experience it offers \u2014 from the elegant ambience to the impeccable service. A special thanks to Francis for the warm hospitality and for making our evening truly memorable.\\n\\nSuperb food, heart-touching flavours, and that Ghevar\u2026 ahhh still thinking about it!\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Arhan Sarkar\",\"time_line\":\"2 years ago\",\"review\":\"4.0/5\\nJoshi House reminds me of a place where classical architecture meets modern art. The facade is very minimal and can be missed if you\u2019re not looking carefully. Situated on the ever so busy Pali Hill road, it is a cozy atmospheric place filled with elegance and charm. The decor is white and embroidered with carefully placed art pieces like quirky flower vases.\\n\\nFood is as expected quite exquisite. The place is quite famous for its chefs. The carefully done dishes are set apart quite easily and the touch of decadence is very satisfying. It is on the expensive side so be prepared for spending a little extra. It is an experience however. I have been there on two occasions and have been quite pleased with the presentation of food on ever so beautiful cutlery. One area i would like to see improvement is the dessert. I had ordered the raspberry and dark chocolate, pretty safe choice but i had expected a little more creativity from this department. The coconut touille was tasty but could not marry the two wonderful elements together and failed to accentuate the dish. Overall a good gastronomical experience. I would love to try more dishes from here. As should anyone who is looking for places to try in Bandra, this one is a must try.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":4,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":4,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Soumya Chauhan\",\"time_line\":\"2 years ago\",\"review\":\"The experience keeps scaling up as you enter, get served and finally eat.\\n- The ambiance and decor is elegant, beautiful with an old vintage charm.\\n- The service is really good, waiters are helpful, polite and attentive\\n- The food is perfect - We ordered the pesto avocado toast - was yummy and fresh with the pesto giving it a flavour kick; cheese garlic naan with paneer khurchan and dal makhani. Everything tasted amazing. Sadly we were full so could not get their desserts but they had an amazing collection.\\n- they have a really good collection of wines, particlulary led.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b91,800\u20132,000\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION\":[\"Cheese_Garlic_Truffle_Naan\"]}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"Food is tasty but portions are a little small Service needs to be improved\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"Highly untrained staff chatting & seating in sofas while guests are eating .\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"Best place to chill with great ambience and amazing decor and vibes..\",\"guided_block\":{}}"]

Standing in that queue and watching the sheer volume of happy diners inside is part of the fun\u2014it just builds the anticipation!\\n\\nThe moment we got seated, the energy hit. It perfectly sets the mahol (ambiance), making it an ideal place for a group celebration or a date night with a great soundtrack.\\n\\nWe kicked things off with some classic cocktails. The Long Island Ice Tea was potent and perfectly made, and the Long Beach Ice Tea was a refreshing twist. Great drinks to match the great vibe.\\n\\nMurgh Banjara Kabab: Super soft and melt-in-the-mouth, with that rich, smoky flavour. A definite winner.\\n\\nCrispy Chicken Medall: These were light, crunchy, and addictive. If you like texture and a little zing, this is a must-try appetizer.\\n\\nThe menu has great options, but we decided to dive deep into some regional classics, and we were thrilled:\\n\\nKori Gassi with Appam & Neer Dosa: This was the star of the show. Paired with the soft, fluffy Appam and the delicate, paper-thin Neer Dosa, it was a seriously satisfying combination.\\n\\nKepsa Chicken: We also ordered their signature Kepsa Chicken. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=I recently visited Ciel in Andheri East and this pure-veg restaurant genuinely surprised me with its ambiance, flavours, and warmth. The moment you enter, you feel the calm, classy vibe — subtle lighting, elegant interiors, and a beautifully designed Instagram-friendly corner that instantly sets the tone for a great dining experience. They have launched new menu menu which includes Sushi and more.

Their mocktails are fabulous — refreshing, well-balanced, and visually stunning. For starters, I tried the Paneer Bao and the Vegetarian Kebab Platter. Soft bao, juicy paneer, and perfectly seasoned kebabs… both dishes stood out with clean flavours and great presentation.

The mains were the highlight: two different sizzlers that came in piping hot, full of aroma, and packed with flavour. I also tried their spaghetti, which added a comforting Italian twist to the meal.

A special mention — Chayya Ma’am, the owner, personally came to our table to check if we were enjoying our food. That warm gesture truly elevated the experience.

And of course, the perfect finale: their Sizzling Brownie with Ice Cream — hot, gooey, chocolatey, and a must-have!

Overall, Ciel offers great food, great hospitality, and great vibes. If you’re looking for a memorable pure veg dining experience in Andheri, this one is definitely a must-visit., name_person=Nishit Kheradia}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Ciel is a great place. Simple yet elegant ambience.
Service is great.
The food is tasty and excellent choice for vegetarians and Jains.
Almost every dish can be made Jain.
This is a haven for pure vegetarian and Jain folks.
I was blown away by the horizontal mocktail glass and the starters.
Mains were filling and left me wanting more.
Gulab jamun is the perfect ending to every meal.
So if you’re in Andheri East anytime do visit this lovely little vegetarian outl, name_person=urmi chhapia}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=recently visited Ciel in Andheri East, and it turned out to be one of the most delightful pure-veg dining experiences I’ve had in a long time. The calm ambience set a great tone for the meal.

Started with a  Kiwi Mojito which was refreshing and it was very well accompanied with the Paneer Dum Kebab and Spring Rolls which were delicious and carried a perfect flavour of it,in mains we tried their Paneer Shashlik Sizzler which was recommended  by the chef and it turned out to be made a great dish

The food quality, flavours, and service were all impressive., name_person=niket kaskar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=At Ciel we tried the following:

reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=A first for us, visiting a premium whisky lounge. Although I’m not a fan of whisky this place was so appealing I had to visit! Situated inside The Orchid Hotel near Mumbai Airport this place is a delight for whisky lovers with more than 99 premium whisky brands in their bar.

This place gives of a little bit futuristic neon vibes with pink and light blue colours dominating the decor. With the bar on one end and tables across the floor this place is as good as it gets.

They even host live music every now and then, please check with the lounge before visiting. Their drinks section is quite huge with a menu as extensive as it can be. There’s a liquor or cocktail for everyone!

The service is also super fast, staff is very courteous and helpful in guiding through the menu. The dish presentation is also quite neat. Our food was on the table within a few minutes of ordering.

Coming to the food we had a few cocktails and a few veg and non veg starters. The cocktails were really good, they were strong punchy and had a good flavour. Same for the food the starters were really good. Overall we had a really great time!, name_person=Pratik Patil}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=I visited Merlin's Karaoke Bar this weekend with my better half and here I am sharing my experience.

The lounge is located in the 5 star premium property of The Orchid Hotels near Mumbai Airport.

Starting with the ambience. The interiors are eye catching with a comfy couch and lounge chair seating.

The bar is mesmerizing and they serve 99 kinds of Whiskeys. They have a wide spread of options in the Cocktail Menu.

We were attended by Jay and Allen. They were kind and served us with warm hospitality. The service was prompt and they helped us well to decide drinks and starters as per our taste buds.

We started our night with Rob Roy which was a whiskey based cocktail. Just how I like it.

My partner tried their bartender special LIIT which was made with a mix of different white spirits with a twist of cranberry juice and beer.

We started our meal with Cheesy Mutton Seekh Kebab and Malai Chicken Tikka. Both the starters were marinated and grilled to perfection and complimented well with the green chutney.

In mains we loved Extravaganza Pizza. It was a thin crust pizza topped with exotic veggies and mozzarella cheese.

You can enjoy IPL or any sports matches with your partner along with drinks and appetizers here.

They have Live Gigs and Karaoke throughout

Warm hospitality, crafty cocktails and mouth watering appetizers.. couldn't ask for me.

It was a lovely experience for me and my partner. Will surely visit again very soon., name_person=Gurmeet Singh Rait}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Visited Merlins karaoke bar and it was an amazing experience. The vibes here at this bar are just amazing. The live karaoke adds sparkles to your night!! 😍

We had some amazing drinks. They were refreshing and were made with perfection. The presentation was also great 👏👍

We had Murg Tikka and chicken nuggets for the starters and they were soo delicious 😋😋. The tikka was perfectly cooked. It was a perfect blend of all the spices!!

Also we had chicken Bhuna roll which was too yum 😋😋. The stuffing was soo delicious. Still can't get over its taste!! 😍🥰

A great place with great ambiance and food. Highly recommend!! ❤, name_person=Rahul Sonkar}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Merlin karaoke bar is best bar I have ever visited. They have all types of drink included. I have tried many of them. And the food was outstanding. It was best food experience ever. In starters they have paneer zafrani tikka, jalapeños popovers, dragon spring rolls and bruschetta. it is best food in that area. In cocktails I have tried many lifelong island tea, Margherita frozen and mai gui was the best. All should try I out once in a life. You will feel very happy., name_person=Parth Mangukiya}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Today I visited the 5 star hotel Orchid located near Sahara airport. From all the outlets within orchid I visited their famous Medlin Karaoke bar. This place is at a great spot if you’re around the Mumbai airport. Also closer to the Vile Parle station with a rick fair of 50 rupees. Now coming back to the Orchid Hotel: The place can be best described as LAVISH. I mean their fountain ⛲️ must be the tallest of all I’ve seen in Mumbai as it flows right from the rooftop of the hotel. Medelin bar basically consists of some amazing Karaoke nights, live musical nights, and something interesting to try is their Whiskeys.. they have a massive amount of 99+ varieties available! I wish with two of their chilling cocktails named Fallen angel(Gin based)and the Berry sangria- gave me in a really great mood. We also tasted their Dirty Shirley(Vodka Based) and Devil martini(Vodka Based) were also really impressive, crafted beautifully with great flavors and a great options to go for! Apart from this we tried their Chicken Tikka pizza, Cheesy Lamb sticks and Chicken Quesadillas. My fav were the cheesy lamb sticks.. the place is really nice especially to have some amazing corporate nights, groups, The place is suitable and renowned for their snacks and drinks… they don’t have the provision for a main course but obvious being a bar. Overall the place is fun and a must visit atleast once for the experience it provides!, name_person=Indica Roy}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=The first thing that stands out about this lounge is its impressive collection of 99 different types of whiskeys. If you're a whiskey connoisseur, then Merlin's 99 Whiskey Lounge is definitely worth a visit. However, even if you're not a whiskey aficionado, you're bound to appreciate the inviting and calming atmosphere of the lounge.

Merlin's 99 Whiskey Lounge also offers live music, adding to the relaxing vibe of the place. Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day at work or simply enjoy a night out with friends, this lounge is the perfect spot to do so.

Moving on to the food, we had the pleasure of trying their paneer zaffrani tikka, chicken bhuna roll, and chicken tikka pizza. All three dishes were delicious and packed with flavor. The paneer zaffrani tikka was particularly outstanding, with succulent pieces of paneer marinated in a fragrant mix of spices. The chicken bhuna roll and chicken tikka pizza were also top-notch, with generous portions of tender chicken and mouth-watering spices.

The cocktails and mocktails at Merlin's 99 Whiskey Lounge are a must-try. The mixologists here are skilled at crafting unique and creative drinks that perfectly complement the food. Whether you're in the mood for a classic cocktail or something a little more adventurous, the drinks menu at this lounge has something for everyone.

Finally, the service at Merlin's 99 Whiskey Lounge is impeccable. The staff is friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable about the menu. They are always happy to recommend dishes and drinks that suit your taste preferences.

Overall, Merlin's 99 Whiskey Lounge is a fantastic spot to enjoy a night out with friends or a romantic evening with your significant other. •	Water is charged separately (even still water)

✔ Good ambience

Not too loud and not too low either., name_person=Rohit Srivastava}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=3 months ago, review=A blend of good food, some innovation, a bit of gimmickry and a very reasonable price (3000+ taxes for an eight course tasting menu).

The carnival bites were the most innovative, and among those, the pani pur semifreddo stood out - it bursts in the mouth where the cold temperature and the flavours work wonders. Bao bhaji is more mundane, with a bhaji stuff bao. So it is a spectrum.

Kala khatta was a salad done on the table, again using liquid nitrogen. Good, but not great. Maybe reduce the kale and the arufula volume?

Kombdi rasa was fabulous with perfectly flavoured rasa. Same is true of the crab krapow, served in a dish shaped as crab. I was looking forward to the much hyped recardo negro, but not sure it lived up to the hype. The flavour of the mutton wasn't as intense as I expected it to be - I am not talking about the chilli heat here. Champaran duck carnitas were good with perfectly cooked duck, but the table side service was pointless. Saffron and parmesan  khichdi had nice flavours but they need to underplay the saffron a bit - it is a very overpowering thing, and subdues all other flavours.

Carnival Celebration dessert was all gimmick. Lot of show but, in the end, a very ordinary chocolate dessert. So much so that we ordered another dessert from the a la carte menu  - aam sutra, with mango foam and mango sorbet, and uniquely textured coconut rasmalai, which was better. Aam Sutra would be even better with something that adds crunch/crispiness for a variety in texture. As far as Carnival Celebration is concerned, I am fine with all tamasha if at the end of it, I get a mind-blowing chocolate dessert.

( We wanted to book at TresInd, but it is closed for renovations so we had to settle for Carnival by Tresind. Also, a restaurant where supplies are being dragged through the hall, Chef Sarfaraz and along with someone just chatting around in casuals, slightly stained aprons of the chefs live dishes - these aren't things that should happen in a high end restaurant. Maybe we missed Tresind!), name_person=Siddhartha Siddhartha}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Carnival by Tresind is a theatrical modern Indian dining jewel in Santacruz west. This place is a visual and sensory delight - dark, luxurious interiors adorned with metallic accents, neon patterns, masks, and rose-gold decor evoke a carnival-like fantasy with a sophisticated edge. Expect mixologists serving up creative cocktails, preparing live at your table. Even some amazing food and tempting dessert are prepared live giving a theatrical flair experience. The mood blends carnival energy with upscale elegance - perfect for special evenings and Sunday lunch with live music.
Drinks are highly inventive, globally inspired, and expertly crafted. Every sip is bold and gives unforgettable experience.

1. Flower Power  (Nice Carnival inspired) is sweet and refreshing.
2. Chica Picante (Baranquilla carnival inspired) is Spicy and citrusy.
3. Binche G&T  (Binche carnival inspired) is bespoke gin cocktail made live at your table with your choice gin and tonic.
4. Okinawa Sunset (Japanese carnival inspired) is fruity and fizzy.
• More Standout concoctions: Highlights include Java Jamboree (bourbon, espresso, carnival coffee liqueur), Bellino (gin, peach vetiver blanc, bellini ice), MOG (smoky Goan carnival), Scarlet mocktail, and Tiki Tiki with pineapple and hibiscus - visually striking and tastefully bold.
Food and dessert are inventive, bold, flavorful, beautifully plated - modern Indian with a creative twist. Some top picks

• Pani Puri Semifreddo
• Bao Bhaji
• Paneer Tikka Paturi
• Avacado Galouti Kebab
• Nadru Kofta
• Soba Noodles
• Filter Coffee Tiramisu with Baileys Ice Cream: Elegant and rich.
• Aam Sutra: Mango sorbet with coconut ras malai - refreshing and balanced.
Try out its Tasting Menu where “Every dish tells a story”, a carnival of cullinary delights, mind-bending experience throughout from small and big plates to the dessert section.
Service is warm, helpful, and attentive and the staffs are friendly enriching the overall experience. Highly recomended for foodies seeking Fusion surprises and Cocktail lovers looking for conceptual, playful drinks. Overall, Carnival by Tresind is less a meal and more a vibrant performance - where inventive food and cocktail mixology collide. If you're seeking a Mumbai dining outing that doubles as a show, this is an unmissable pick., name_person=Bhavin Parekh}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Charcoal chicken made with a dash of Thai curry and served on a bed of hummus.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Amazing food, with best service and vibrant ambiance best place to dine in 👍🔥🫡}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The 8 course set menu had taste, flavour, styling.}"]

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS=[Not_sure, E:NOT_SURE], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Paid_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_PAID_PARKING_LOT], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=a month ago, review=We were back to Khyber after quite a number of years. After hearing mixed reviews regarding the food, we were quite unsure on what to expect, however, with high hopes, we still decided to visit.

Started off with their chicken tikka and the masala roomali roti. Didn’t disappoint. The chicken tikka was soft and very well seasoned. It was one of the very few I have had that doesn’t require the squeeze of lime to accentuate the taste. Paired with the roomali it was a started to get us started.

Moving on we had the butter naan along with the chicken tikka masala. Another stellar combo. Hot, fluffy naans with perfectly spiced chicken tikka masala with that perfectly caramelised onion flavour, something you should definitely order.

Next we moved to the chicken biryani. It’s a light biryani. Not too oily not too heavily reliant on array of spices. Simple yet tasty. Perfect lunch is what I would say.

Despite the reviews we managed to enjoy the food to our hearts content, name_person=Amol Surve}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_STREET_PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION, Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Great restaurant. Beautifully designed and good service. The menu is a great Northern Indian journey. Quite sophisticated and not only your Indian classics. Good mix of Indian / Mogul cuisine. I had a chicken curry cooked to perfection as well as a great mutton masala kebab. Only thing: the waiter asked for tip a bit too pushy. I was happy with the service and would have given a generous tip anyway. But that was annoying., name_person=Christian Breitkreutz}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, 3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Average taste, great hospitality, interesting ambience.
Located at a prime spot, Khyber gives you the impression that it’s a classic where nothing can go wrong with the food. While it does not do anything wrong with the food, it also does not do anything marvellously well with it. The chicken kathi roll and the paneer tikka were so mildly marinated, one could barely get a sense of the spices used in the dishes. Even the cheese garlic naan was an average nibble.
The staff is warm and courteous., name_person=karman khanna}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=I tried a garlic Naan for the first time in Khyber back in 2015. I visited it for the second time in 2025 and I was as mesmerized as I was 10 years. But this time what stood out was the afghani chicken kebab. It was creamy, tender and so so flavourful. Would definitely recommend for a delightfully family Indian meal!, name_person=Anushka Pillai}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 months ago, review=We found Khyber through reviews, and it truly lived up to the hype. North Indian food never disappoints, and this place is a gem. The restaurant has a beautiful cave-like setting with warm vibes, and the servers were very polite.

We loved the chicken biryani – flavorful and aromatic – and the butter chicken was so creamy with perfectly tender chicken. Portions are decent and satisfying. Overall, if you’re looking for vibrant North Indian cuisine with great atmosphere, this is the place to go!, name_person=Anggie Puji}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Very quiet, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=3 months ago, review=The restaurant has a nice ambiance and the food was okay in taste. However, the service was quite slow and the food was not served hot, which affected the overall experience. With faster service and better attention to food quality, this place could be much better. Hoping to see improvements on my next visi, name_person=Mahesh Maurya}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=This was out first visit to this venerable Mughlai restaurant in Kalaghoda, in south Mumbai. The first thing that strikes you is the massive, ornate wooden door and once it swings open one can see the really beautiful archtecture of the restaurant featuring floating staircases and traditional furniture that is reminiscent of the northwest frontier though I noticed that the ceiling of the upper floor is extremely low.
I was tempted to compare Khyber to Punjab Grill, having visited the latter several times but Khyber now for the first time. Certainly the decor of Khyber is more earthy, more rural and yet more elegant. Punjab Grill now looks a little dated in some ways.
As for the food what I liked about Khyber was that the dishes were quite simple and the spices were mild and not overpowering. We sampled the corn tikkis, lamb rara and chicken tangdi. All were excellent and each dish was served separately as a course of its own. This was accompanied by naan and pudina paratha. For the three of us the bill came to less than Rs4,000, which was great value for money. Be warned, however, that this restaurant gets pretty busy and walk-in's could face a long wait though it's worth it, name_person=Indrajit Advani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=4 months ago, review=tried the Chicken Tikka, Chicken Butter, and Chicken Biryani — all were absolutely delicious! The flavors were rich and well-balanced, and everything was cooked perfectly. A great spot for anyone craving authentic Indian food., name_person=Hessa Alrowahi}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review= Starters are sooo yummy 😋 ambiance also good lovely food I enjoyed a lot}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Best service with nice ambience..good place to hangout with our family}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=People say this North Indian restaurant offers flavorful dishes and tender meat.}"]

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a month ago, review=For appetizers: Ordered crab meat that was tossed in chillies, garlic, spring onions and some fat like butter I guess. This crab dish was good. Then came the bombil fry that wasn't upto the mark. The fish wasn't that fresh and big and the floury batter was thick and raw inside in some areas. Then came the prawns ghee roast that looked orange in colour and wasn't roasted at all. You know a good ghee roast must have that intense red roasted colour. Another disappointment was the fish Gassi. I had to send it back because the fish wasn't seasoned with salt before adding to the curry and plus the gravy was a basic otm masala with a very weak coconut flavour. I didn't taste the authentic Gassi masala?. The Neer Dosa was good.
I am happy that they did get a few things right. But after spending close to 3k for that meal it wasn't worth it., name_person=Aaron D'costa}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=Edited 7 months ago, review=This place has become a personal favorite when it comes to seafood—I've been a regular here, and it never disappoints!

The variety they offer is fantastic, and the quality is consistently top-notch. Despite the 1+1 seating setup, the place is always crowded, which speaks volumes about how popular it is. If you're a fan of South Indian-style seafood, you're in for a treat—their preparations really stand out.

Some dishes you must try include the Seafood Soup, the rich and flavorful Seafood Gassi, and the tangy Pulli Munchi. We were also recommended the Prawns Kadipatta—it was absolutely delicious. If you’re into crab, they’ve got some great options there too!

What I love most is that it's not just tasty, but also easy on the wallet. Great seafood, great flavors, and great value—what more can you ask for?, name_person=Stephen Fernandes}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=2}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Recently visited Harish Lunch Home for a non-veg dinner, and I have to say, my experience was quite mixed. While the restaurant does have a parking facility and offers both bar and family seating sections, the food and service left much to be desired.
This place is known for its seafood and bar setup, so I had some expectations going in. We ordered a variety of dishes:
•	Manchow Soup
•	Chicken Ghee Roast
•	Butter Garlic Prawns
•	Bombil Fry
•	Chicken Crispy
•	Egg Fried Rice

Out of everything, only the soup was passable. The chicken ghee roast was underwhelming—the masala wasn’t cooked properly. Butter garlic prawns lacked flavor and freshness, and the bombil fry didn’t meet the usual seafood standard either.

The chicken crispy was the biggest disappointment. It was hard and chewy, nowhere near the crispy texture we expected—it honestly ruined the mood of the meal.

For the main course, we ordered egg fried rice, but the waiter failed to guide us properly with portion sizes, especially considering we were a big family. This led to a shortage and overall dining discomfort.

In short, service was poor, food was mostly below average, and portion sizes were not family-friendly.
I would not recommend this place for a proper family dinner. If you’re looking for quality food and attentive service, I suggest you explore other options., name_person=Siddhesh Kotian}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Neer_Dosa, Stuffed_Bombil, Prawns_Gassi], GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=If someone is a seafood lover , this place you must put in ur bucket list . Varities of Seafood available. I had prawn gassi with neer dosa & steamed rice with some masala sippi ., name_person=aebi vlogs}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Very quiet, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Amazing service!
Some of the best I’ve ever experience.
The fish dishes are choicely!
A very nice experience.
Delicious crab and prawns as well as chicken lollipops.
Very nice atmosphere upstairs too., name_person=MÖzil 99 (Mo)}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Neer_Dosa, Tandoori_Pomfret, Stuffed_Bombil], GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=The food here is out of the world. It's fresh, it's tasty, and it's authentic. We ordered the drinks and the starter first and sipped while deciding the main course. We had a Cosmopolitan and a Jamaican breezer accompanied by stuffed Bombay duck or Bombil as it is locally known. We then ordered for a stuffed pomfret and a plate of sukha mutton with neer dosas. Finished off with ice-cream. A great afternoon feast! I commend the chef for his cooking and the waiting staff for their service. Thank you., name_person=Rohinton Ranji}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Somewhat difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a month ago, review=From outside anyone will get a feel of a Bar but walk inside and then upstairs, you will see all the families busy relishing the delicious food served here.

Been here many times and will keep visiting to keep the taste buds busy and of course happy.

This time we had ordered the Squid Butter Garlic and it was so awesome that we ordered it again.

A must visit for anyone who loves seafood and the south indian way, name_person=Lalit Pawar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=9 months ago, review=Everybody MUST try this place...you will start believing that if you get good taste food all go seaching for it...very quick service..solid tasty local food..highly highly recommend, name_person=DR.SACHIN NARHAR JOSHI}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Paradise for sea food lovers 👌👌 Friendly staff 🤝 Fast service Homely ambience}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good Seafood, tried butter garlic prawns, Neer dosa and chicken ghee roast}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=We had ordered here butter chicken,chicken crispy,and crab soup!!}"]

Highly recommended!, name_person=Sakshi Singh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Not sure, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Visited this place recently to celebrate a friend’s birthday, and overall, it was a nice experience. We ordered a mix of dishes — a couple of pizzas, spider roll (sushi), dumplings, and the tortellini pasta.

The food was good in my opinion — flavorful and well-presented. Though some people might find it a bit on the milder or subtle side, I personally enjoyed it. We recently visited and regret going there., name_person=Jay Ganatra}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=4 years ago, review=Utasv is a simple and elegant restaurant for family and friends. This is a Veg restaurant. Just because it’s a veg restaurant they have introduce a lot of innovative dishes to the menu and all. This restaurant is small and cozy with around 7-8 tables with a total sitting capacity of 40 people. This is an old restaurant who has kept them self-updated with latest food trends and drinks. The Ambiance of the restaurant is also smile and plan with nothing much in designs.

The first dish I tried was Aloo Nazakat. This is a small appetizer with a good burst of flavors. It’s a small potato cut in half which is marinated with a spicy marination. Then it is topped with cheeses later baked in grill. I liked this dish mainly because of it size. I would say its like a small boom of flavors. I would recommend you to try this dish and pair it with a sweet mocktail.

The second dish was The Corn Cheese Kurkure. This is a very good veg starters and I would go for this dish over many non-veg starters. This is a crispy dish with a very creamy filling. The inner filling is made up of palak paste mixed with cheese and corn, which is wrapped around spring roll wrap and the entire thing is deep fried until golden brown. This dish is served in shot glasses filled in green chutney and garnished with cheese. You can eat this dish like a finger sticks and its really enjoyable dish.

The Next dish was the Falafal Pocket. This is a middle eastern dish which is prepared very nicely by the restaurant. Basically what this dish is a fluffy form of pita bread which is stuffed with a creamy salad. This restaurant fills the bread with very little salad and serves the rest as side dish so as to fill it more as per your individual needs. They also serve Humus sauce which is prepared by their chef to go along with this dish. The texture of the dish is very tempting wanting you to fill it with more of the salad. If you want something new to eat go for this dish.

Then I went for the Main course in which the first was Panner in Coriander Sauce. This was a nice pan Asian dish prepared with delicate sauce. The Texture of the dish was dark and thick whereas the aroma was very light on the nose. This is a stirred fried dish which is cooked along with spring onion , scallops and herbs. The panner is soft and tender and well submersed in the flavor of the Coriander sauce. A must try dish along with some drink.

Next up was the Dunger Panner Biriyani. This dish was more on presentation then its taste. The texture of the dish was rich and the aroma was very strong everyone in the hotel could smell the dish as it comes to your table.  The dish is mixed with a creamy panners and aromatic rice. This dish is best suited to have it along with a group of people at the end.

The last dish was the Desert i.e. Gulab Jamun Cheese Cake. The cake is exactly as it sounds it to be. This is a cheese cake filled with Gulab Jamun throughout. The cake is light with a crummy base and filled with lots of Gulab Jamun. I really liked this dish and ended up eating 2 of it. I recommend you to try this dish for sure, name_person=Akshay Mashelkar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Roomali_Roti], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Menu_is_all_vegetarian, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_COMPLETELY_VEGETARIAN]}, time_line=2 years ago, review=The staff was cordial and suggested good options for lunch.

The restaurant is located on the hotel's top floor and has both options of sitting indoors and outdoors. However, in terms of ambiance, we found out the first roadblock was that the lights were too dim. There were times when we had to use our mobile flashlights to scourge the menu.

We began our menu by ordering a Veg. Manchow soup, a few plates of Jalapeno cheese poppers, and some animal fries. The Jalapeno cheese poppers were true to their name. Being filled with cheese that had melted and mixed with jalapeno was an absolute cheese lover's delight. The dish was so good that we went for another round. The animal fries were crisp and freshly fried. They came in with two types of dips, with one being mayo. Also, the quantity of the fries was great.

The manchow soup was delicious too. It had a decent mixture of chopped veggies, and the quantity of fried noodles as a top-up was great too. Next, we ordered some veg. Kebabs and thai cottage cheese skewers. Both the dishes were excellent to taste, and the skewers came in with their portion of fries to be had with the cottage cheese. And the cottage cheese in itself was soft and juicy, made absolutely to perfection. We also ordered a plate of capriccio bruschetta and were delighted to have them.

For the main course, we went ahead with two veg. Pizzas, two plates of burnt garlic fried rice, and two plates of stir-fried vegetables. The pizzas were close to a thin crust with tons of veggies and a delicious layer of mozzarella cheese. The burnt garlic fried rice did contain a decent mixture of veggies, but it was close to a regular vegetable fried rice with almost no taste of garlic. And the stir-fried vegetables tasted delicious with the rice. Finally, we ended with five plates of chocolate mousse. Honestly stating it was the best mousse I had ever had served with a generous portion of vanilla ice cream—the perfect ending to a sumptuous dinner.

The biggest problem we faced was the order delivery was way too slow. The soup that was ordered first came in after nearly 70 mins which was too much. We complained multiple times, and we could understand that the quantity of the orders was huge, but the time taken was unreasonable, and we never really had to wait for so much time to eat. Thus, this space needs considerable improvement and also on the lighting issue.

But apart from that, the staff was pleasant and professional, and the food was indeed a foodie's delight. I would definitely recommend trying out their food. They’ve recently launched their European Exclusive Menu, and every dish I tried was packed with flavour, beautifully presented, and crafted with real passion. From the Chicken, Potato & Leeks Soup to the Gambas al Aglio, Crisp Fried Chicken, Rigatoni, and the outstanding Coq au Vin with Herbed Pilaf Rice, everything tasted premium and thoughtfully curated.

The vibe of the place is stunning with indoor, outdoor, and rooftop seating, each corner has its own charm. What really stood out was their hospitality. The staff is polite, professional, and extremely attentive. I even experienced their unique chocolate hand wash ritual, which made the evening feel so special and luxurious.

Their drinks were another highlight especially Mango Fizz, Essence of Guava, Smoke & Oak, and The Royal Wedding all beautifully prepared right at the table.

Ended the meal with their in-house signature Tiramisu, and it was a treat not just to eat but to watch, as the chef prepares it live at your table. They have six varieties, and both the Sesame and Biscoff versions were outstanding.

A big thanks to Faizan Shaikh , the chefs, mixologists, and the entire team for taking such amazing care of everything.
Onrique isn’t just a restaurant it’s a complete dining experience that you will truly remember. Highly recommended!, name_person=ABHITHEFOODIE}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a week ago, review=Had a lovely experience at Onrique. Overall, a great spot in Bandra that’s definitely worth visiting., name_person=Mona Juneja}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=a month ago, review=A breezy rooftop, beautiful ambience and food that actually lives up to the vibe. Onrique was the perfect place for a date night! The ambience feels really warm and aesthetic. Perfect for a relaxed dinner, good conversations and some great food.

Here’s everything we tried:

Chicken & Charred Zucchini (Recommended)

A thin crust authentic Italian Pizza with smoky charred zucchini, juicy chicken and perfect balance of cheese. Light, crisp and flavour-packed.

Gambas Al Ajilio

An absolute treat consisting of plump and buttery prawns swimming in a garlicky olive oil base alongside toasted garlic bread. The taste really stood out.

Crispy Fried Chicken

Golden, crunchy and really soft inside, it was some well seasoned chunks of fried chicken. Loved it totally.

Rigatoni Alfredo Chicken Pasta

Then came the cocktails—

As if that wasn’t enough, I ordered another. This time, it was bold, tangy, and not even remotely sweet—exactly how a well-thought drink should punch you: with character, not confusion.

The food followed, and it didn’t disappoint.
The Chicken Spaghetti was a protein-lover’s dream—light on oil, laced gently with garlic, and sprinkled with greens that weren’t an afterthought but a part of the experience.

And then, a pleasant surprise: Chicken Kori with Appam—comfort food executed with restraint and finesse. No excess oil, no spice overpowering the senses—just subtlety, balance, and technique.

If you haven’t been here yet, trust me—it would be regretful not to.
I forgot the heart robe “tiramisu” which they prepped fresh for us from scratch.

Whether it’s the dosas, curries, or starters, everything is cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The flavours are authentic without being overly spicy, appealing to a wide range of palates.

The service is excellent, with staff who are attentive, polite, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations are spot-on, and they ensure you’re comfortable throughout your visit. Highly recommended., name_person=Aniket Pargaonkar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Brunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=30-60 min, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=2 months ago, review=We ordered a jackfruit cutlet which was the only decent thing there and portion wise alright. Another thing we ordered was Mini Gunpowder Idli which was horrible compared to the price we paid and which had everything except the gunpowder masala. The mini idlis were not at all soft.
Then for the main course I ordered Rasam Rice  (Rs 550) which was supposed to be served along with Vatha Kolumbu, Porial, Papad and Pickle. We were told the portion can serve two people. But it was utterly disappointing - in terms of taste, quantity and plating.
Rasam was bland, it looked and tasted like thin tamarind juice just fell on an ocean of oil - no zing and simply bland. Anyone who is familiar with the cuisine of the Southern states of India would disapprove of the kind of Rasam they served.
Vatha Kolumbu felt like store brought Tamarind chutney. And Porial lacked fresh coconut - they sparsely put some shredded coconut maybe to show authenticity. And it was a basic store brought pickle with one Papad which they said would serve two people.
Even their hospitality is bad. We were made to wait after we got a call that there is a table for us. The lady who was the register book handling the reservation lacked hospitality instead was rude. Another lady who was walked us through the menu was extremely uninterested to do so and didn't bother answering our queries.
Banking on the growing popularity of the Southern cuisine of India they're scamming people, especially the ones who have not tasted authentic food from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala. Anyone who has not tasted ghee podi masala, gunpowder masala would not know the difference so yeah that's how The Tanjore Tiffin Room operates. It was an extremely disappointing experience. Walking into Tanjore for lunch, I had no great expectations, but this restaurant managed to completely flip my mind. It's simply amazing South Indian food, delivered with impeccable style.
The Culinary Highlights
The star of the show, and the dish that truly caught us off guard with its taste, was the Karaikudi Prawns. They were simply delicious—a must-try that showcases a mastery of flavor.

Furthermore, the waiter did an amazing job in explaining each gravy thoroughly, earning extra points for that level of detail and guidance.
I paired my meal with their Sour Patch mocktail, and it was definitely not a regret. It was a refreshing and well-balanced drink that perfectly complemented the spice of the food.
Service and Atmosphere
The service at Tanjore is impeccable. The staff is always attentive and there to guide you through the menu, making the entire experience smooth and enjoyable.

After what went down yesterday, I honestly can't tell.

I usually ask bartenders to measure my wine before pouring, but this time I forgot. So I politely asked them to check it after. Turns out, it was 5–10 ml more than the standard serving - no big deal, right?

Apparently, it was. Instead of simply pouring the measured wine back, the bartender (Bhavesh) decided to keep the extra wine for himself and snapped, “You wanted the standard serving - this is it.”

When I said, “If that’s your attitude, I don’t want this glass,” but he refused to cancel the order.

Now the other 2 Jokers - The Two managers.
They were right there. Watched everything. Said nothing :)

It’s funny - you might actually have a decent time here as long as nothing goes wrong. But the moment you raise a concern, the service attitude changes completely.

If you’re looking for a chill bar on that street, there are plenty of others (some even cheaper) that understand basic courtesy better than this place, name_person=Nigel Dsouza}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Three Wise Monkeys 🐒 was the perfect spot for our karaoke night. They serve dishes from various regions of India, including Rajasthan, Kerala, and Maharashtra, offering a rich and diverse culinary experience.

The quality of food here is exceptional—comparable to top-tier establishments like Taj Santacruz, if not better. Upon being seated, you’re welcomed with a refreshing Kokum drink and crisp Kerala chips, accompanied by three chutneys. The mango pickle is my personal favorite. Based on the waiter’s suggestion, I tried the Kerala and Rajasthani cuisines, and they were absolutely delightful.

In keeping with traditional Indian culture, the restaurant encourages eating with your hands—though cutlery is provided upon request. Even the moringa soup was rich, flavorful, and comforting.

The staff is courteous and well-informed about the menu. They’re happy to guide you through the offerings, and I highly recommend trusting their suggestions—they know what they’re doing.

For those arriving by car, valet parking is available, making your visit even more convenient.

All in all, this place delivers an authentic and satisfying Indian dining experience. Whether you’re a fan of traditional Indian flavors or exploring them for the first time, it’s definitely worth a visit. You’ll leave full, happy, and already planning your next trip back., name_person=Vikash}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=3 months ago, review=If you’re looking for authentic Indian food, this restaurant is a must-visit They offer a variety of flavors from different states like Maharashtra, Kerala, and Rajasthan.

We had a table reservation for 9:45 PM and arrived by 9:55 PM. Despite being just 10 minutes late, we were made to wait another 10 minutes before being seated—even though we could clearly see 4–5 empty tables inside. This initial delay set the tone for what turned out to be an underwhelming evening.

Once seated, we weren’t provided with menus until we asked for them. After deciding on our soups and starters, no server approached us for over 10 minutes, prompting me to personally request someone to take our order. There was no water on the table, and even after requesting it, the server simply forgot—walking past our table multiple times to serve others. Eventually, I had to approach someone who seemed to be the manager, only to be told, repeatedly, that “the staff is busy” and we needed to “co-operate.” Frankly, it doesn’t take much effort to bring menus, take an order, or serve water—basic expectations at any restaurant.

As for the food:

Soups: The Manchow soup was lukewarm and seemed like it came straight from the buffet, with soggy fried noodles on the side. The Tomato soup, on the other hand, had a nice basil flavor and was decent.

Starters: The Paneer Chilly was flavorful and enjoyable. Among the non-veg options, the Korean Fried Chicken had an odd fishy smell, although the sauce was good. The Pan Fried Chicken Momos were tasty, though the accompanying dip was overly sweet.

Main Course: The Chicken Tikka Masala and assorted breads were well-prepared and satisfying. However, the Chicken Biryani was disappointing—bland and lacking any real depth of flavor. The vegetarian mains—Vegetable Stir Fry in Hot Garlic Sauce and Pink Pasta—were good but took an unusually long time to arrive.

Mocktails: We tried the No-jito, a twist on the classic mojito, which didn’t stand out, and the Guava Mary, which was refreshing and enjoyable.

No desserts were ordered, mainly because by the end of the meal, our patience was running thin.

Overall, the dining experience was marred by disorganized service, inattentive staff, and inconsistent food quality. While a few dishes did manage to impress, they weren’t enough to outweigh the frustrating delays and lack of basic hospitality. For a restaurant that seems to take pride in its offerings, the service fell severely short.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a week ago, review=Tanatan Juhu delivered a wonderful dining experience with great flavours and warm hospitality. The Oreo Milkshake was rich and creamy with the perfect chocolatey blend, while the Tanatan Sangria was refreshing with a well-balanced fruity kick with crunky apple

Zucchini Paneer Rollatini was a new take beautifully crafted with soft paneer wrapped in flavourful zucchini layers.
Sarsoon Broccoli had a lovely smoky char and a bold mustard marinade that stood out. The presentation was gorgeous

In mains, the Aloo Kulcha was soft, generously stuffed, and baked to perfection, paired with Pindi Chole that had deep, robust spice notes. Authentic flavours, great taste

So, it was 6 of us and we ordered 7 dishes and orange juice.

The English breakfast was as it should be. The hash browns were crunchy.

The spicy mutton keema with pao was ok. Have had better.

The s’mores waffles looked so pretty and tasted good. Same with the old fashioned pancake. The only thing is these days restaurants don’t serve chocolate sauce with it. It’s an add on which you have to pay for. It’s a peev that my kids have with all places serving waffles and pancakes without chocolate sauce or Nutella. But that not withstanding, the taste was great.

Now coming to the 2 things we didn’t like. The chicken croffles, looked like batter fried chicken breast on a waffle and it looked too dark as if deep fried for too long and didn’t taste well. Barrel Mansion is the new talk of the town. This is a club with a great ambiance, quick service and amazing food, really I just loved this place. This place is open till 3.00 am. Located within the Sahara Star hotel in Vile Parle East Mumbai.

The ambience of this place is certainly the best part of the place. It gives us these crazy vibes as soon as we enter. I visited here few days ago and enjoyed my time.

We started with Som Tam Salad had the punch. Dressing was perfect. Bang on flavors. Raw papaya in a traditional sour and spicy marinade. One of the best salads I have tried in recent time.

Dynamite Prawns: Medium sized battered prawns served in a margarita glass made in chef special sauce. Prawns has an amazing texture and was delicious. The topping of black and white sesame was icing on the cake. Loved this one.

Stir Fry Chicken: Chicken chunks and fresh exotic veggies tossed in sauce and spices. You can feel sweet and spicy taste at a same time.

Prawns Crackers: One of the best option to nibble with a drink.

Black Bean Sauce Chicken: Loved the punch of pepper in it. Goes very well Chicken Fried Rice. Combination is superb. Black Bean Sauce was more on spicier side. But, still go for it.

Sesame Ice Cream: Its creamy hand churned icecream made in-house and topped with black sesame

Tab Tim Grob: Not so good for me. The presentation was good but tasted okayish.

Overall, Loved the ambience, service and food. Keep up the good work. Cheers!!!

Food: 5/5
