This was our second visit to Mahesh Lunch Home in two nights during our four-night stay in Mumbai—that’s how much we love this place. Many friends told me to try their garlic‑butter specials, so we ordered garlic‑butter prawns for my 5‑year‑old, and she devoured them. The garlic‑butter sauce left on her plate was so good, I happily took it with my rice.

My 7‑year‑old, not a seafood fan, enjoyed her beloved reshmi kebab again—soft, flavorful, and exactly to her taste.

For us adults, hubby and I ordered the lobster lajawab and lobster Malabar chilli, paired with roti and rice. Each dish was absolutely delicious—rich, aromatic, with the perfect balance of spice. The lobster lajawab was buttery and indulgent, while the lobster Malabar chilli offered a beautiful heat that lingered just right.

We were thrilled to see Sunil and Vinod again—they remembered us and once more took exceptional care. Attentive, warm, and effortlessly thoughtful, they made the evening feel like catching up with old friends. We loved everything about our dinner. Highly recommend.

Visited July 15 2025 - Day 12 in India

My friends highly recommended Mahesh Lunch Home in Juhu so we went for dinner after it reopened as it was closed yesterday due to the Maharashtra bandh on July 14

Sunil the captain and Vinod our server took excellent care of us. They were attentive thoughtful and made sure every detail was taken care of without us even having to ask. From making sure the kids were comfortable to anticipating our needs they were warm courteous and professional throughout the evening

For dinner my 5 year old wanted the chicken sweet corn soup. Sunil thoughtfully split it into two bowls so both my 5 and 7 year olds could have their own. My 5 year old loved it and the 7 year old was okay with it

For the kids Sunil recommended chicken reshmi kebab with no spice and they enjoyed it with rice. It was soft flavorful and mild enough for their taste

We ordered tandoori pomfret for my husband and me. We got to choose our fish and it was cooked to perfection. Spicy smoky and delicious we loved every bite and did not leave a crumb behind

We also ordered the Mahesh special prawn curry which was outstanding. The curry was rich creamy and full of flavor and the prawns were generously portioned and perfectly cooked. We had it with tandoori rotis and rice and everything was just delicious. The flavors were deep and satisfying with just the right amount of heat and seasoning

My husband had ordered fish and chips thinking the kids might not eat the reshmi kebab but they did not touch the fish and chips at all

Not wanting to waste food we packed the untouched fish and chips the remaining prawn curry and rice. Later that night we gave it to an elderly lady living in a tent near our hotel and she was very grateful

Finally got to visit Izumi Bandra, and it definitely lived up to all the hype! It’s cozy, warm, and gives that perfect mix of fine dining and comfort food energy. 🇯🇵✨

Here’s what I tried:

🍤 Tempura Sushi Rolls – absolutely delicious! Crispy on the outside with soft, perfectly seasoned rice and fresh fillings inside. Each bite was full of texture and flavor — definitely a must-try for sushi lovers.

🍱 Chicken Teriyaki Rice Bowl – comforting and full of flavor. The chicken was tender and glazed beautifully with that sweet-salty teriyaki sauce that hits just right. It’s one of those dishes that feels simple but perfectly balanced.

🍜 Chicken Paitan Ramen – warm, rich, and satisfying! The broth was creamy and flavorful, with perfectly cooked noodles and soft, tender chicken. You can really taste the depth in the broth — ideal for anyone craving authentic Japanese ramen.

🔥 Mini Hot Pot (New Addition) – such a fun and hearty dish! Loved the idea of getting to enjoy a mini version of a traditional hot pot. The flavors were bold, comforting, and perfect for sharing or enjoying solo.

Overall, Izumi Bandra completely nails it with food, presentation, and atmosphere. Every dish feels thoughtfully made, and you can sense the authenticity in each bite. It’s easily one of the best spots in Mumbai for Japanese cuisine — whether you’re a sushi lover, ramen fan, or just want a cozy, flavorful meal.

The entire experience was fantastic, from food to ambience to service. We went with the waiter’s recommendations, and every dish was absolutely spot on. From appetisers to mains and desserts, everything was delicious, no complaints at all. Honestly, it’s hard to recommend just one or two dishes because everything we tried was genuinely amazing. The place does lean towards the expensive side, but it’s totally worth it for the experience, food, and vibe. A heads-up: on Fridays, the bar night starts at 11:15 PM, so they politely inform diners to wind up dinner if you’re seated downstairs, which is fair. They also have an upstairs seating area, once you exit the lift on the 9th floor, there’s a staircase leading up. You can ask the staff to assist with seating upstairs if you prefer.

The ambience is beautiful, the interiors are tastefully done, and the music post 11:30 PM (especially on weekends) is really great, perfect for a lively night out. The crowd was pleasant, and hygiene standards were well maintained, including the washrooms. Special mention to the staff polite, attentive, and gave us some of the best food recommendations. The restaurant features creative dishes and cocktails in a visually stunning and calming ambiance.

Started with the Beetroot & Avocado Noritakosu , basically a nori taco stuffed with sushi rice and yuzu black bean aioli. Fresh, flavorful, and absolutely loved it , full marks!

The Megumi Guacamole was a nice touch, simple yet satisfying.

Then came the Megumi Special Tempura Roll, crispy asparagus tempura (I opted out of the enoki mushrooms), tofu, spicy mayo, and a sweet sauce all rolled together. Great balance of crunch and flavor, definitely a win.

If you’re looking for a place where great food meets sporty vibes, The Studs is the ultimate destination! From the moment we entered, the ambiance gave full stadium feels – big screens, energetic crowd, and a lively atmosphere perfect for match lovers and foodies alike.

["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Baroke is a very beautiful place located inside Krishna palace hotel at grant road. Service is super prompt and staff is very humble. We loved our visit to this place. Music is amazing and total chilled out place. Security is perfect. Its a wonderful place to chill with your friends.

We ordered for

Cheese chilli toast (5/5)

Bruchetta (5/5)

Corn tempura (5/5)

Hunger bowl (5/5)

Veg cheese pasta (5/5)

Cosmopolitan (5/5)

Orange cooler (5/5)

We would love to visit here soon.

Cheers, name_person=saloni shah}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=4 months ago, review=I don't know if the name is still B lounge. But a new renovated place at same spot is very good. Very posh layout and good ambiance. High priced due to location and ambience, name_person=TJ Sean}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=It was a Friday night and we really wanted to start our weekend with something interesting and happening. We came across this recently opened place called Baroke at Grant Road.

Location is bit confusing with maps, however the manager helped us in finding it very quickly. Place is situated on the first floor of Krishna palace Hotel.

Ambience and decor actually cheered up our mood. It is a perfect party and chill out place for you and your gang. Place is spacious with limited yet comfortable sitting area with a dance floor.

Coming to the food, food menu is not so lengthy with some veg and non veg quick bite items. We loved all the dishes that we tried. The Bar menu offers some really good options in cocktails.

We totally loved phuljhadi chicken tikka, fish tikka and baby corn tempura. Also the white sauce pasta for main course was creamy and delicious.

From Bar menu we tried Cucumber rosemary gin tonic, Gauva Daiquiri and Coffee caipirinha. We totally enjoyed our drinks. All of them were refreshing.

Baroke sets up a perfect weekend mood with good food, great music and classy ambience.

Totally recommended.

Happy eating.😊., name_person=snehal dalvi}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Baroke was something where I didn’t go with great hopes but trust me visiting here changed my outlook for a good reason. Lot of pubs have come up these days in Mumbai but this place reminded me only 90s where the interior is rustic and gives a classic look. The music was dapper and the crowd is happening.

The manager was very much helpful is suggesting us the best food as per our liking. The food was impeccable. I am sharing few recommendations and I bet you will go there again to have them - chilli cheese toast, chicken tikka pizza, stuffed masaledar Kulcha served with Dal makhani. Although the menu is not that extensive but it does fulfil the need.

Highly recommended place for great taste of music and yummy food., name_person=Pushpak Vanjari}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=5 years ago, review=If you're looking for a place to party in SoBo, Baroke is the place to go. Quite close to the Grant Road station, this place has a dance floor with good music and lights.
We tried quite a few dishes and mocktails. In starters, we loved corn fritters and cheese chilli toast. Bruschetta was decent too. Chicken tikka was a showstealer. Really tender and juicy chicken cooked well.
We had mint melon cooler and coffee chocolate martini to wash down the food with. Loved the drinks and their presentation.
In mains, we loved the stuffed kulcha with dal makhni. Also had noodles with green chicken. Didn't quite like this one. The green gravy wasn't working with the noodles.

Overall, it was a nice experience and a good place to party., name_person=Shreya Bharti}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Baroke was on my list as I have been hearing a lot about them offlate, this indeed a great night life bar which is operational on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday only till 3:00am which is so nice.

📍This place is located at a jump distance from grant road west station.
Cited inside Krishna palace hotel on the first floor.

>Ambience - Dark theme bar having trippy lights , huge bar , super comfy couches to dine , pretty interiors is what baroke all about.
>Food - It basically serves different cuisines and bar/finger food. It absolutely delivers a gastronomical experience!
>Hygiene- The place is maintained well , right from lounge arena and even smoking zone everything was hygienic.
>Value for money- Being cited in south bombay , this place definitely delivers a great night life to the patrons. The prices are charged perfectly.
>Our order -
R: denotes Recommendations.

•DRINKS:
1)Black currant(R)- Black currant crush topped with soda and dash of lime juice and bit of salt mix in it was refreshing and delicious.
2)Blue lagoon- Blue curracao , lime juice and soda mixed together resulting into a great refreshment.

•APPETIZERS:
1)Cheese corn balls(R)- corn and cheese mixture in ball shape served in 8 pieces , this was really delicious , the cheesy texture and crisp coating from out was done well , served with ketchup and mint dip.
2)Chicken in hot garlic sauce(R)- Chicken pieces sautéed in hot garlic sauce having perfection of spice and flavor balance ! It is a  best one if you want to fave something with your drinks.

•MAIN COURSE:
1)White sauce pasta(R)- Super cheesy macaroni made to perfection. It had generous portions of chicken in it and the best part was the creamy texture which was superb.
2)Kulcha with dal makhani- 4 pieces of freshly made aloo kulchas served along flavorful dal makhani , it was indeed splendid one.

•DESSERTS:
1)Pastry- Though it wasn’t available, it was sourced from out by them , loved the sweet gesture of the staff.
It was something we demanded and we got. Loved this too:)

-•- Overall experience was superb and we really loved the vibe of this place. It’s absolutely a perfect place to party on weekends.

•Food - 9/10
•Ambience - 10/10
•Staff- 10/10
•Value for money - 8/10
•HYGIENE- 10/10

*REVIEW IS BASED ON PERSONAL EXPERIENCE!, name_person=Vedant lad}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Baroke:

Recently visited the newly revamped Baroke!
Divided into 2 lounge and Dance floor area are totally different. Lounge is dark with flash light placed with Comfort Velvet royal sittings.. loud music & well stocked bar also ample place for people to dance & soak themselves in peppy music.. To my surprise the compact menu is droolicious.
The Cocktail and Mocktail presentation is vibrant and settle in taste.
Must Try Cocktail: Pineapple Caribbean!

What I ate:
CHICKEN FULJADI KABAB:
I think they had marinated the chicken for 24 hours.. the chicken that was succulent and juicy that beautifully marinated in indian spices. That texture of kabab that will make you gulp all in no time.
HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

LEMON BABY CORN TEMPURA:
this particular this was super delicious and met with all the elements when it comes flavors, the crackle texture from crunchy fried baby Corn.. tossed in sweet and sour sauce.
HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

CHEESE CHILLI TOAST & TOMATO & OLIVE BRUSCHETTA:
These two baked to perfection with the right crisp from toast..
Perfect for siders.
RECOMMENDED, name_person=Freeda Bhati}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Baroke (The Flute) is one of the oldest party places in town. Since it is located in Krishna Palace (hotel) it stays open till pretty late in the night. So one doesn't need to worry about deadlines, let the hair loose and party all night.

Located at level 1, Baroke hasn't changed much over these years. Wooden doors at the entrance and couple of doors to actually enter this club. One of the rare few places in town which has a such a big dance floors. And decently big bar to cater to the drinks of people. Baroke has about 6-7 tables to accommodate large groups, always recommended to reserve before heading out.

Talking about what all I tried at Baroke -

Since it's a club, where people primarily come to dance and drink, the food menu is concise, however includes most of the things. We concentrated mainly on the starters and one odd main course. In starters we had a platter of Bruschetta and Chilli Cheese Toast. Later followed by Lemon Chilli Babycorn Tempura. All starters were decent but order of preference would be exactly the same as written - Bruschetta followed by Chilli Cheese Toast followed by Tempura.

Along with food, ordered couple of mocktails, mixed quite well - Cranberry and Orange Coolers. Mocktails were good, hence I am sure cocktails would be too. For main course, we had the highlight of the evening. Masaledar Kulcha with Dal Makhani. Easily the best dish at Baroke. One cannot miss this, highly recommended.

If one doesn't want Indian, they can go for Pizza and Pasta as well. Had visited Baroke a long time back, brought back few pleasant memories. As far as place is concerned, if you want a place to party at reasonable rates without deadline pressure, head to Baroke. Music is more of EDM. Wait around till late to have a good time, both from dancing / drinking as well as food perspective., name_person=Jatin Shah}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Cheese Chaska Cheese balls with an amazing Indian twist served with chutney.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Highly recommended place for great taste of music and yummy food.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The Bar menu offers some really good options in cocktails.}"]

For the mains, we had Chicken Lehsuni, Bhatti Da Murg, and Cheese Garlic Naan – the Lehsuni Chicken was undoubtedly the star of the show with its bold, garlicky taste. Mutton Rogan Josh also stood out with its rich spicy and aromatic flavour. The Chicken Biryani that followed was aromatic and satisfying.

Desserts were a highlight – the Butterscotch Ice Cream, Malai Kulfi, and the indulgent Pull Over Chocolate Cake were all top-notch, especially the chocolate cake, which was rich and gooey.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Somewhat difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=Edited a month ago, review=Disappointing Experience on Diwali
We were a group of 5 who had booked a table a day in advance through Google for 20th Oct, 9pm. On calling the restaurant in the afternoon about parking, the manager suddenly claimed they have “stopped online reservations” — even though the slot was available and confirmed on Google. When I asked his name (atleast thriceA) he disconnected the call without telling.
Not taking a chance, we reached at 7:30pm. The restaurant was barely 40% occupied. Our waiter Kabir was polite and helpful — full marks to him for service.
The major issue happened at billing — they flatly refused to accept Zomato payment despite Zomato showing a good discount option. There was no notice displayed, and we were not told at entry or while ordering. The manager “Shrikant Pedhnekar” was unapologetic and defensive instead of clarifying or expressing regret. While we were leaving, another manager (name unknown) also argued with us. In this era of 'Customer First', not once these managers showed any signs of being apologetic nor regret. The high-handed attitude spoiled our mood. Especially when the prices are comparable with premium restaurants. While prices match that of premium restaurant, the customer-centric attitude does not.

Other aspects:
• Ambience feels dated — furniture and décor easily 15–20 years old
• Prices are comparable to premium restaurants but food is only average in taste and portion
• We ordered for two cocktails but they were not well made.
• Service charge of 10% was added automatically while most restaurants of this level charge 5% (we got it removed)
• Restaurant is on 1st floor - No lift so elderlies and people with mobility issues will find it difficult to reach the restaurant

Overall, good food and smiling service of Kabir the waiter saved complete disaster. One star is for him. 4 stars goes out for an unprofessional and disappointing handling of guests. Valet is available., name_person=saloni shah}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Kebab Korner is a restaurant with beautiful blue and white interiors along with artistic chairs which gives it a very royal look. To top it all this place has an amazing view of Mumbai’s Queen’s Necklace. It looks stunning, especially during the Monsoon Season.

The Cuisine here is Indian and they specialize in Kebabs and North Indian Curries. I have tried a lot of Vegetarian dishes here, which is mentioned in detail below.

Truffled Mushroom Baby Kulcha

Small Soft Kulchas Stuffed with a Mushroom Paste. It comes straight out of the tandoor to your plate! It was very soft when I tried it and it had a very mild flavor from the Mushrooms. However, I couldn't taste truffle anywhere, I was expecting the use of some truffle oil at least.

Chili Cheese Baby Kulcha

Another version of Soft Kulchas Stuffed with Cheese and lots of Red Chili Powder, I could taste a lot of cheese and the spice from the Red Chili was also not overpowering. I would prefer this over the Mushroom kulcha even though I LOVE Mushrooms.

Jaituni Paneer Tikka

Giant Cubes of Paneer Marinated in Tandoori Marinate and it was sliced from between to stuff in some Olives. That gave it a tangy flavor and it was an amazing way of serving the Paneer Tikka. The only thing I didn't like is the quantity of Olives was very less and I could hardly taste any Olives.

Kumbh Dak Banglow

Button Mushrooms marinated in a Mustard Paste and cooked inside the tandoor until they become soft.

Daal Makhani

A bowl full of richness, it was exactly what you expect from a Daal Makhani. Melt in mouth Daal in tonne loads of Butter & Cream with superb flavors coming from spices like Clove, Cumin and Cardamom.

Lehsooni Palak

A very creamy concoction of Spinach and Fried Garlic, this was hands down the best dish which I had here. It is a must try if you love Spinach.

The service here was very quick and the staff had total knowledge about the Menu. Overall this place was amazing and I would definitely recommend it to someone who loves to have North Indian Food., name_person=Paras}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=InterContinental - the iconic Hotel located at Marine Drive is home to Kebab Korner. Kebab Korner is an ultra luxurious fine dine place with breathtaking bayview and serves authentic Indian cuisine along with some fusion dishes / desserts as well. Kebab Korner is located on Level 1 alongside Long & Short, which is a lounge which serves European cuisine.

Kebab Korner has recently introduced Thalis - which is a lavish 3 course Indian meal including appetizers, main course and desserts. They offer Express Lunch Thali which caters to corporate as well and is priced at INR 1800 excluding wine. For dinner they offer "Experience Thali" which is an easy going complete meal, where you can take your time and enjoy scrumptious meal. This is priced at INR 2400.

Heading straight to what was on offer for Experience Thali - Veg

To begin with we were presented with a palate cleanser - Amuse Bouche. Crispy and Spiced Masala Chana Dal packed in edible plastic. I was intrigued about the ingredients used and technique to make this, but it stays as a secret with the restaurant and chef. Very unique and impressed I must say!

We started with Appetizers and were served three of them - Jaipuri Paneer Tikka, Bhune Subz Ki Shami and Sarson Brocolli Tandoori. Paneer Tikka was smoked cottage cheese marinated with olives. The olives gave it a bitter taste for me and I personally love the smokey effect given to cottage cheese. However in this process the cottage cheese might have become a little hard. Something, which can be looked into.

Next we had the Bhune Subz Ki Shami - Round shaped Patties / Tikkis with peas and spiced beans as filling, fried to perfection. Highly recommended to try! After this, we tried the Sarson Broccoli Tandoori - marinated with mustard and grilled to perfection! Loved it! Must try!

Before heading into the mains, we were served another palate cleanser - this time around it was Mango & Lemon Sorbet served in a cutting chai glass. Loved the combination and was very refreshing. Again very unique!

And now coming to the Star Veg Thali at Kebeb Korner - 5 Vegetables and 1 Dal with Assorted Indian Breads along with choice of steamed rice / Khichdi. The thali was presented in a beautiful way. They have a shiny steel arc where all the individual bowls are placed. So all of these 6 bowls along with a bowl of salad is placed in front of you at one go, unlike other thali places where different people serve you continuously which can be irritating at times.

The best part here at Kebab Korner is that you get a thali experience without any hassles. Coming to the 5 vegetables - Bhuna Gobi Masala, Paneer Butter Masala, Subz Miloni, Lehsooni Palak and Beawar Bhindi. Amongst the five my preference would be Beawar Bhindi, Bhuna Gobi Masala and Paneer Butter Masala. Crisp Bhindi (lady fingers) with perfect potli masalas and cherry tomato. Personally I am not a fan of Bhindi, but with the way it was made and tasted, loved it.

Bhuna Gobi Masala, chopped cauliflower tossed with Indian spices and Paneer Butter Masala -creamy cottage cheese in a rich onion and tomato gravy, both came a close second for me.

Dal in the thali was Kebab Korner Signature Dal Makhani. Creamy Black Lentils Dal to be enjoyed with Indian Assorted breads as well as with Steam rice. Tasted real nice. I also tried the Khichdi, could be a good light option after heavy meal.

Finally moving to the desserts, we had the Gulab Jamun and Gulkand Pannacotta - a fantastic fusion of Indian and Italian desserts! Sweet thickened cream topped with Gulkand and Gulkand! Loved the dessert, must try and highly recommended! And towards the end we were presented with a platter of paan - Meetha (Sweet) and Saada (Plain). Couldnt have asked for more!

Overall, if I need to define my experience at Kebab Korner in one word, it will be awestruck! We visited The Bayview Restaurant at Marine Plaza, Churchgate for their breakfast buffet, and it turned out to be a truly delightful experience.

The setting is nothing short of stunning — with an amazing view of the Arabian Sea, especially on a monsoon morning. Watching the rain roll in while enjoying a warm breakfast was a beautiful and calming way to start the day.

The buffet spread was impressive, offering a great variety of both Indian and continental options. From fresh fruits and hot South Indian delicacies to eggs made to order and flaky pastries, there was something to suit every palate.

The staff was exceptionally well-trained, courteous, and helpful, ensuring everything ran smoothly and making the experience feel personalized and pleasant.

If there’s one area that could use a little refinement, it would be the dessert selection — while adequate, it lacked the finesse and variety you’d expect from an otherwise well-rounded buffet.

That said, it was an overall excellent experience. The combination of a serene ambience, great food, and attentive service makes this a spot we’ll definitely be returning to. It lacked the authentic flavors that one would expect from a good tandoori dish. The spices seemed dull and lifeless, completely devoid of the vibrant blend that should have brought the dish to life. It left my taste buds wanting more, but not in a good way.

Furthermore, the excessive amount of oil on the tandoori chicken was completely off-putting. It appeared as though the chicken had been deep-fried rather than being cooked in a traditional tandoor oven. Every bite was extremely greasy, making it difficult to truly appreciate any subtle flavors that might have been present.

To say that I was disappointed with this tandoori chicken would be an understatement. I expected better from a renowned restaurant known for their Indian cuisine. The lack of attention to detail and the poor execution of such a classic dish left me feeling unsatisfied and regretful of my choice.

In conclusion, my experience with the tandoori chicken from Amrit Panjab was far from satisfactory. The taste was bland and unremarkable, while the excessive oil made it difficult to enjoy. As a lover of Indian cuisine, I believe it's important to prioritize quality and authenticity. Unfortunately, this restaurant fell short of meeting those expectations, making it difficult for me to recommend their tandoori chicken to others., name_person=Sheela Solanki}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=4 years ago, review=Good food nice location just outside of Mumbai Central railway station. Everybody Liked it., name_person=Prashant T}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=9 months ago, review=Unchi Dukan Feeki Pakwan.

You must have heard of this proverb.

We experienced it at Oh! Calcutta. We ordered Pressure Cooker Mutton, chicken biryani and Luchi and two mocktails, Watermelon+Basil and Aam Pora Shorbat.

In total we paid +2700₹.

Overall the taste of the food was good, but quality and quantity must have been better.

We have eaten at Leopold cafe, Mirchi and Mime, Ranjit da Dhaba and so on. Mentioning this so that you know we have already considered the level of the restaurant and speaking only after analysing that.

So here is my story. After finishing our meal, we were given a feedback form in which I gave mixed reviews according to the food and services provided.

In specific, I mentioned that the quantity of the food should be increased according to the price.
But this was never a problem untill the manager came to us cross questioning why we gave an average feedback. And on top of that he started to argue and tried to make us seem small that we only ordered items for ₹2700+ (Seems as if he was not ready for any suggestions at all and wanted us to order food for ₹5000 or more).

When we gave this feedback, he said that this is normal.

I don't have a problem whether this is normal or not or whether you choose to give that much quantity in this price.

But the main problem was they are just arrogant and ignorant to guests satisfaction. They think that they deserve 5star irrespective of their service or food and only a fool would give them a lower rating.

Lastly they took additional Service Charge which is not legal to take on the bill and is completely optional however they are taking it from everyone. Bill is attached for the reference.

So, for us, it was the first and last time there. Wish you all a better experience than mine., name_person=Viswajeet Kumar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=2 months ago, review=In quiet corners where hunger brews,
Oh! Calcutta, my heart thanks you —
For a feast so gentle, steeped in grace,
Where Bengal’s soul found its rightful place.

The Cholar Daal, a golden dream,
Sweet with coconut, rich with cream —
Each spoon a hymn, each bite a prayer,
A whisper of home in saffron air.

Then Paneer Paturi, wrapped divine,
Banana leaves and mustard’s shine —
A melody soft, yet fiercely true,
Of rivers, rains, and skies of blue.

Kaju Kismis Pulao, what art!
Fragrant rice with a poet’s heart —

Second visit for me but, i don't find anything drawing me back., name_person=ranjeet mahtani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=9 months ago, review=For our Valentine’s Day dinner, we visited this charming Italian restaurant, and it turned out to be an unforgettable experience. Given the occasion, reservations were essential, and we were lucky to secure a table.

The ambiance was warm and cozy, with soft lighting and elegant décor that set the perfect romantic mood. The staff was incredibly attentive, ensuring we were comfortable throughout the evening. Their service was prompt, friendly, and efficient, adding to the overall delightful experience.

Now, let’s talk about the food—undoubtedly one of the best Italian restaurants in Mumbai! We began with some cocktails, which were decent, though not extraordinary. Moving on to the appetizers, we opted for the mushroom ravioli, and it was simply divine. The rich and creamy mushroom sauce paired perfectly with the stuffed chicken ravioli, creating a dish that literally melted in the mouth.

For the main course, we tried the Pollo Picante pizza. It had a bold, spicy kick that added a unique twist to the classic flavors. While it wasn’t the best pizza we’ve ever had, it was still delicious, with a perfectly crispy crust and generous toppings.

The real showstoppers of the evening were the desserts. The Tiramisu was, without a doubt, the best I’ve ever had—light, creamy, and full of rich coffee flavors. The chocolate goey cake was equally indulgent, with a soft center that was pure perfection.

Yes, the restaurant is on the pricier side, but for an evening of exceptional food, top-notch service, and an intimate atmosphere, it’s absolutely worth it., name_person=Anjali Kubal}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=I live right next door and have had pizzas from all over the world, and I can honestly say Gustoso is right up there with the best. Their Arrabbiata Pizza is my absolute favorite, perfectly baked with just the right kick of spice and that unmistakable wood fired flavor.

The pastas and gnocchi are also amazing, full of flavor and always cooked perfectly. You can taste how fresh everything is.

It’s one of those rare places that gets everything right – great food, warm atmosphere and consistency every time. Any ways food is good., name_person=NOSHIR KATRAK}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=A Timeless Culinary Journey at China Garden

China Garden isn't just a restaurant; for me, it's a cherished institution, a place I've been visiting since childhood, and truly nothing short of legendary. In an era where culinary trends come and go, China Garden stands as a steadfast beacon of classic elegance and unparalleled flavor.

What draws me back, time and again, is the inimitable vibe – an aura of "old money style" that permeates every corner. From the sophisticated decor to the perfectly attentive service, it's a nostalgic journey to a bygone era of refined dining, yet it feels perfectly timeless. This isn't just a meal; it's an experience rooted in tradition and comfort.

On my recent visit, the culinary journey was, as always, exceptional. We savored:

The comforting warmth of the Sweet Corn Soup.

The perfectly balanced flavors of the Gin Chicken.

The ever-dependable delight of the Hakka Chicken.

The essential accompaniment of Fried Rice.

And the rich, savory depth of the Sapo Chicken Gravy.

Every dish was executed with the consistent perfection that China Garden is known for. Beyond the exquisite food, the service truly shines. A special shout-out to Karan, whose attentive and impeccable service made our experience even more delightful.

For anyone seeking an authentic taste of classic Chinese cuisine delivered with legendary style and grace, China Garden remains, without a doubt, the ultimate destination. The bar section was also well-managed with a good variety of drinks and quick service, which added to the overall experience for the adults.
The only downside was the loud music — not the best environment for babies under 2, as it can get overwhelming for them. Overall, a wonderful celebration with just a small hiccup for parents with little ones., name_person=Priyanka}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservation required, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Visited one of the amazing buffet restaurants at Atria Mall, Worli, and I must say, I was completely amused by the vast spread of starters, main course, and desserts! What impressed me even more was that they have an equally lavish spread for vegetarians too.

We were so busy exploring the non-veg starters that we couldn’t make space for the veg dishes — though they all looked absolutely delicious and quite different from the usual buffet fare.

They have live sushi counters with at least 4–5 vegetarian and 4–5 non-vegetarian sushi options — super fresh and beautifully presented. The salad section also deserves a mention for its variety and freshness.

Among the ready starters, the prawn tempura is an absolute must-try — perfectly crisp and flavorful. There’s also an interesting section where you can pick up chits to decide which starter you’ll get — a fun and quirky touch that adds to the experience!

Overall, if you’re a foodie, this place is a must-visit. The ambience is elegant and relaxed — definitely offers a fine dining experience with a buffet twist., name_person=Snehal Chaulkar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=I recently visited Glocal Junction in Worli, Mumbai, and overall the experience was just average. I tried their nachos with avocado, which were okay but nothing special. The waiter suggested a small cheese-stuffed kulcha paratha as an appetizer, but it was quite underwhelming, the flavors didn’t stand out and the kulcha was too chewy. We also ordered avocado panuozzo bruschetta, but it took so long that the staff seemed to forget about it entirely, it tasted okay when we finally got it. A perfect combination of 5 star service, great quality food & top of the range music. Staff were extra ordinarily warm, proactive and professional., name_person=Amisha's Sattvalife}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Whether you go for corporate or family gatherings for lunch or dinner and maybe party, you will experience different mood and event every time and I'm sure that every time of your visit at this place will be awesome.
Glocal Food
Food is all Glocal. It offers fusion of the global famous cuisines amalgamated with that of our local authentic.
To get to taste the innovative twist, their 'Bat Pizzas' are delicious served in half metre and One metre on Bat trays. I chose my bat as 'Roasted Bell Pepper, Jalapeno, Bocconcini and Olives' and 'Four Cheese-Parmesan, Cheddar, Bocconcini, Mozzarella and Baby spinach'. More of middle-eastern varieties turned me on to opt for 'Cornetto' from 'Pick on it' snacks and
'Chicken Adana Kebab'. There are extremely scrumptious with all that Arabian touch. The harissa and creamy garlic sauce in Chicken Adana tastes exactly like Arabic food. 'Cornetto' with each layer of hummus, salsa and grilled mushroom was delight in every bite.
Glocal Cocktails
They have classified cocktails; some classic, some new and some of them classic turned fusion cocktails.
'Toxic' was one such a kind that was surprisingly served in a box made with vodka, litchi, and lemon grass. Another vodka based drink known as 'Thailee' was obviously a thailee which is a hindi term meaning packet, had a sweet and sour taste. 'The Glocal Slammer' and 'Black Magic' also has their own wonders to your taste buds. Black Magic made with whiskey and smokey orange looks magical to the eye due to the smoke burst as soon as its top glass is removed. The presentation of the cocktails are amazing; you should never miss a chance to slurp on their classified cocktails as it will be beyond delightful.
Glocal Dessert
For me, Kolkata Paan cheesecake was enough to drool me. The cheesecake rolled within Paan leaf was is something that you will in this. It looks and tastes delicious., name_person=Roshani Batra}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Huge and nice place, Good variety in food, nice service and Polite staff.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Really yummy makhani sauce, shredded chicken, cheese & sour cream.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Coorg style chicken dry fry : Good size portions and soft chicken balls.!}"]

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Masque was very good, but just shy of being amazing. Would rate this 3.5/5.

The food was consistently good, but not great. Everything was beautifully made, perfectly presented but the taste of everything left us feeling a bit lacking. Or as my wife said, it missed “ooomph”. After having spent the last few weeks at other restaurants like the Bombay Canteen, Papa’s, O’Pedro etc, the food at Masque felt like the bottom of this group. It is actually surprising how it was ranked number 2 on the top 50 restaurants list. Not saying the food is bad, not by any means. It is really good, but not worthy of being number 2.

The service was good, but staff can be better trained to be more cohesive, quiet and smooth. This could be a high standard having spent time experiencing the world class service at Papa’s.

The atmosphere was simplistic, slightly modern and feels cold. It’s not a warm and cozy atmosphere, it’s slightly more formal. The bar occasionally gets very very loud with the sound of ice shaking but other than that, it’s quite comfortable. Staff is attentive and happy to help.

We did really like the experience of them bringing us into the kitchen for the first course, but again, kind of felt like a gimmick. This can be done better.

The bill for 6 of us with a few drinks came to about 60,000. For this price, the quality and taste of the food was not worth it. We felt quite disappointed, specially considering the reputation, reviews and ranking that Masque has.

There are other restaurants of much higher calibre. If you want to spend similar money and are fortunate enough to get a table, go to Papa’s.

For a slightly more accessible experience, go to Bombay Canteen.

We’re glad we tried this, it was a unique experience, but probably won’t return unless there’s a completely new menu., name_person=Nirav Tanna}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=From start to finish, this was one of the best tasting menu experiences I’ve ever had. We were invited into the chef’s kitchen at the start of the evening, where the team greeted us warmly and took a photo — a memorable way to kick things off.
Once seated, the magic really unfolded. The 10-course tasting menu came with no preview, which made each dish a fun and delicious surprise. Every plate was beautifully executed, creative, and perfectly paced.
The service was equally outstanding. The waiters were not just professional but incredibly knowledgeable about each dish, its ingredients, and the cooking techniques behind it. Their enthusiasm really elevated the experience.
A phenomenal meal and an even better overall experience. Absolutely worth it!, name_person=Hema “Hem” K}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Not sure, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, 3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Overall not worth the cost. Service wasn’t exceptional. Only few dishes were actually inspired and up to the mark like the dosa, palate cleanser and the burnt ghee ice cream. Most dishes had some or the other ingredient that was way too overpowering, couldn’t really taste other flavours making the overall dish taste average., name_person=Nishant Goel}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS=[No_special_event, E:DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS_NO_SPECIAL_EVENT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SPECIAL_OFFERS=[Not_sure, E:NOT_SURE], GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Masque was a wonderful experience - top-notch food, great service, and a lovely atmosphere. It was the first of four fine dining restaurants we tried in Mumbai, and it set the bar really high. The execution and flavor mastery of every dish was spot-on. The trip to the kitchen for a palate cleanser (and a Polaroid-style photo memory) was a fun surprise. They were also the only restaurant that served our champagne in Zalto glasses, which perfectly matched their attention to detail throughout. When you find yourself in Mumbai, Masque is a must., name_person=Miro K}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=3 months ago, review=So we keep trying the set course menu at most of our special occasions and would rate  Masque as the 2nd best

Woukd rate Tresind over them but they surely outscore Indian Accent in terms of flavour and creativity and definitely much ahead of Ekaa., name_person=Ankush Manwati}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=Edited 6 months ago, review=The journey to Masque begins with a whatsapp interrogation regarding the prospective guest's dietary preferences, allergies and information that a Rs 5000 deposit for two guests is mandatory which will be set off against the final bill. Your preferred table booking time will be confirmed only if the appropriate answers are provided. After an analysis of your answers you  are accepted! BUT only if you are not late by more than 15 minutes of the appointed time. But if you are - all is lost - the food, the 5000 and your mood. There were multiple messages regarding being on time.
Once you arrive at the Masque - you see a black wall and a black door which opens to reveal the restaurant. If you are early you may choose your table. Once at the table, each seat has a cocktail (Rs 5500)and wine pairing (Rs 5500 to Rs 7700) lists. You will also get sheets of listing of mocktails (Rs 2250), progressive cocktail pairing (Rs. 7700). This is in addition to the 10 course tasting menu priced at Rs. 6500 per head.
The food is flavourful. Except for the main course, which was dosa and smoked pork or Koji Sunchoke the rest were small portions. The gelatos were very tiny. The dish preparations were interesting in the way thupka or ravioli were recreated. The pomfret/besara/trout roe and the lamb/rezala/confit duck were very nice.
We selected the progressive cocktail menu. The first drink was of gin (mountain goat) where there was no flavour of gin. The tequila and mezcal cocktails were good. Rosso made from bourbon was ok.
The staff knew the food well. But they kept changing and each had a different attitude. One of them was quite dismissive of some premium Indian wine we asked about which was not listed on the Masque wine menu.
Ritwik at the bar was a helpful staff member and enlivened the evening with his fliar behind the bar.
All in all an ok, ok experience., name_person=SS Gill}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Really really good cocktail program - the Mezcal pairings were great.

Food, outside from the corn course and cocoa course was pretty forgettable and in some cases, thematically incoherent (guava + squid, briyani + roulade, melon + cheese).

Vegetarian subs were also not very well thought through.

To top it all of, this was the first (and hopefully only) time ive ever been upsold packaged food (chocolate) to bring home after eating at a fine dining establishment., name_person=Adrian Chew}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=It was an experience. To begin with, many basic food items were out of stock. When I tried to reorder a simple starter made of baby potatoes — something that is available in almost every restaurant — I was told they had run out. Later, when we ordered naans and rotis, unbelievably, those were also out of stock. For a hotel of this level, this is unacceptable, especially when handling a pre-booked group of 27 guests.

The taste of the food was another big disappointment. The black dal was extremely blend, and I was told they only make Jain dal, which definitely did not justify the poor taste. I’ve eaten far better dal in regular restaurants.

On top of this, the service was shockingly careless. One of the staff members dropped chutney on a guest’s outfit. At a 5-star place, where guests are dressed in expensive clothes, such negligence is simply not expected. The overall attitude of the staff felt carefree and unsupportive, especially whenever we ordered anything extra — all we heard was “out of stock.”

This dinner was meant to be special as we were celebrating my father-in-law’s 75th birthday. We had requested a pineapple cake, something most 5-star hotels offer complimentary for such occasions, but we were charged for it. Despite the hotel’s multiple mistakes, our bill came to ₹90,000 and they didn’t offer even a 1% discount to acknowledge the inconvenience.

To add to the frustration, the chef claimed the black dal was their “best-selling dish” and even said he would “teach me how to make it.” This kind of attitude is unprofessional and unacceptable.

Overall, the experience was highly disappointing — from the food quality and stock issues to the staff behaviour and lack of accountability. A 5-star hotel cannot function with such poor management and attitude. I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for good food, good service, or a memorable dining experience., name_person=Krinita Makwana}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good service excellent food Enjoyed the atmosphere and the decor}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=High quality food, Good ambience, Gentle staff, Economical and best attention}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The menu had a variety of options and the prices were reasonable.}"]

Overview
AER at the Four Seasons is a rooftop experience that lives up to the hype. Perched high above Worli, it delivers sweeping Mumbai skyline and sea views, a modern yet warm ambience, and consistently polished service — ideal for both special evenings and relaxed drinks with friends.

Ambience & design
- Incredible vantage point: panoramic views of Mumbai and the Arabian Sea are the star — especially dramatic when clouds roll in or the city lights up at night.
- Roof engineering: the covered rooftop feels state-of-the-art — thoughtfully designed to shelter guests during rain while preserving the sense of openness. Even in a downpour the space felt airy and comfortable, with rain adding to the drama rather than disrupting the experience.
- Vibe: stylish, contemporary décor with an upscale lounge energy. Music, lighting and layout encourage both intimate conversations and lively groups without feeling crowded.

Drinks
- Negroni: expertly executed — perfectly blanched (clean, balanced bitterness and bright aromatics), with excellent temperature and presentation. The cocktail showcased strong technique and attention to classic proportions.
- Cocktail program: creative but respectful of classics; bartenders clearly know their craft and tailor drinks to taste.

Food
- Guacamole prepared tableside: a highlight. Watching it made fresh added theatre, and the result was vibrant, aromatic and packed with flavour — creamy texture, bright citrus and just the right seasoning. Superb balance of richness and acidity.
- Overall tasting: dishes leaned modern, high-quality and well-seasoned. Portions are geared for sharing and designed to complement the cocktail-led experience.

Service
- Attentive and professional without being intrusive. Staff handled the evening smoothly, from timing of drinks and food to accommodating the rain cover without fuss.
- Knowledgeable servers and bartenders willing to recommend pairings and adjust drinks to preference.

Pros
- Unmatched views and rooftop atmosphere.
- Weather-proofed design that keeps the rooftop enjoyable even in rain.
- High-caliber cocktails and memorable live-prep elements (e.g., guacamole).
- Polished, thoughtful service.

Cons / notes
- Popularity means it can get busy; reservations are recommended for prime seating.
- Price point is upscale — expect to pay a premium for the location and experience.

Who it’s for
- Couples seeking a romantic, skyline-backed evening.
- Groups celebrating special occasions.
- Cocktail enthusiasts who appreciate skilled bartending and well-executed classics.

Bottom line
AER at the Four Seasons is a standout rooftop destination in Mumbai. Between the dramatic views, intelligent roof design that allows enjoyment in all weather, expertly made cocktails (that blanched Negroni is a must-try) and the theatrics of fresh guacamole made tableside, the experience feels both luxurious and lively — well worth a visit., name_person=DonD Marley}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 months ago, review=A bar of two halves—chill vibes (James Blake and Sampha) on the city side, and Ibiza house tunes on the sea side. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=A school friend sent me a reel about Poe and Pao in Chembur. I decided to go chasing Poe and Pao. Since I was already in Bandra, I thought I’d try their Matunga outlet instead.

Now, if you’re a true-blue Mumbaikar, you know traffic jams aren’t an inconvenience, they’re a lifestyle. So there I was, stuck in the middle of one, wishing for a restroom more than anything else.

When I finally reached, they said, “Go next door.” I stumbled into Dakshin Culture Curry and found the cleanest restroom in Mumbai. Small, but spotless. You can’t do pranayama there, but you’ll definitely come out feeling zen.

Feeling human again, I stepped out… and somehow found myself in Diva Maharashtracha. For a moment, I thought I’d taken a wrong turn in life. That’s when someone explained that Dakshin Culture Curry, Goa Portuguesa, and Diva Maharashtracha are a trilogy, same team, shared menu, different cuisines. And Poe and Pao? The latest addition to the family.

One look at the menu, and I knew there was no way I was walking back to Poe and Pao.

I started with a Sushegad Shot (feni, lime, and kaffir leaves) -  Goa in a glass. Then came the Khekade Kalimiri Soup, a crab-and-black-pepper combo that doubles as a natural sinus reliever. After that, Ravas Moile, Tender Coconut Cashew Nut Sukke (their signature dish), Chicken Modak, and Appam n Amboli.

The Chicken Modak was the surprise star—moist chicken kheema wrapped in a soft, pillowy coating. Though, between us, it did look slightly jaundiced.

They ended the meal with complimentary Caramel Custard—light, soft, and just the right sweetness.

The staff were courteous and attentive, the ambience warm and welcoming.

Ambience: A+
Food: A+++

What started as a quest for Poe and Pao turned into a delicious detour, a reminder that some of the best finds in Mumbai happen purely by serendipity., name_person=Happy Wanderer}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_STREET_PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Had an Amazing time at Diva Maharashtracha. The assortment of different cuisines was really interesting., name_person=Anush Mishra}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Dakshin culture specializes in various South Indian dishes. The ambience is so quaint and beautiful. The bright lights and soft music makes it so peaceful and enjoyable.
The menu has vast range of dishes, with fish preparations, chicken, mutton.
Their motto is that South Indian cuisine is much more than Idlis and Dosas.

What we ordered:
In Starters 🍢
🔸Fish Fry Porichaphu 🐟❤️
This was a very tempting dish. Pomphret which was nicely marinated was served in red masala and fried. It had a nice tangy sweet taste. The covering was crisp with hint of spices and the sauce served along was tangy sweet. A must try!

🔹Spice Rubbed Rawas ❤️💯
Rawas fish marinated with spices and yogurt and nicely grilled. The flavors were soaked in the fish. The dish was so well prepared that all I wanted to eat was this yummy Rawas. My new favorite.

In Cocktails 🍹
🔸Cosmopolitan 🍸❤️💯
Our usual favorite. This Cocktail was well prepared. Just the way I like it. Nothing can ever go wrong with Cosmo. Went perfectly well with the starters.

🔹Mango Margarita 🍹❤️
This was tangy sweet due to the mango flavor but again a yummy boozy drink. Well served with sugar coated at the rim. It was an eye candy.

In Mains 🍛
🔸Prawns Manglorean Sukkha 🍤❤️💯
This was a delight. If you want something light to go with your breads then this is it. This was so flavorful and tasty. Hint of all the spices nicely marinated in prawns. The prawns were in good number and juicy.

🔹Chicken Chettinad 🍲❤️❤️💯
This was the best Chicken Chettinad. Spicy and tasty, with so many flavors. I could eat it everyday. Just like homemade gravies but much more flavors and spices. Too yum. A must must try here.

🔸Malabar Paratha
It was served hot and crisp. Went really well with Chettinad gravy and the chicken pieces.

🔹Appam ❤️
They've a special counter to make appams. And my mum loved it to the core that through out the meal she had more of appams. Beautifully made and served steaming hot.

🔸Neer Dosa
Soft and light. Non sticky and thin slices. The beauty of neer dosa. Just perfect.

In Desserts 🍦
🔹Shahi Tukda ❤️
Fried bread stuffed with rabdi. The rabdi was so so good. Specially made by the chef. It was full of rich milky flavors.

🔸Watalappam 🍮❤️💯
Similar to our beloved custard but a famous South Indian dessert made from Coco and jaggery. Only if you taste it then only you can understand what I'm saying. It was so soft and tasty. Loved it!

The service is a bit slow, but once you taste the food you'll be on a joy ride. The food is so well prepared and so delectable. Each dish is pretty unique and delicious. It is a melange of flavors dancing in your mouth.
The servers are well trained and will help you with your selections. You'll definitely leave with a happy stomach and a smile on your face., name_person=Sonal Vartak}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Dakshin Culture Curry is a great place for experiencing some traditional and authentic South Indian dishes. The food served here had that authentic touch and was very flavourful.

We had Andhra Chicken and Pepper Prawns Fry for starters, the taste was simply amazing.
Melon Cooler was a fresh and delicious mocktail.
Chicken Chettinad is a must try here with freshly made Appams..it was mouth-watering. Ended the meal with the classic Shahi Tukda!

Staff was very courteous and helpful. The owner is also very friendly. Service is good too. Overall a great place to enjoy your meal with friends and family. Must visit!, name_person=Amit Patra}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Dakshin Culture Curry

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)

Tamnak Thai in Dadar Shivaji Park, Mumbai, has solidified its place as my absolute favorite Thai restaurant after multiple delightful visits, with my latest being on September 1, 2025. Nestled on Veer Savarkar Marg opposite Starbucks, this spot offers an authentic Thai escape with its warm, oriental ambiance—think elegant sculptures, soft lighting, and spacious seating that feels like a trip to Bangkok. The staff, including our attentive server who expertly guided us through the menu, delivered courteous and efficient service, enhancing the cozy in-house experience at Table No. 5. The absence of a service charge is a thoughtful bonus in Mumbai’s dining scene.
Our meal began with refreshing drinks that set the tone perfectly. The Cinderella mocktail (₹460) was a delightful blend of tropical fruitiness with a fizzy twist—light, sweet, and utterly refreshing. Paired with it, the Himalayan mineral water (₹140 per bottle, 2 bottles at ₹280 total) offered a crisp, pure hydration that complemented the flavors ahead. The Iced Tea (₹240) brought a chilled, subtly sweet note, while the Kiwi Kooler (₹460) burst with fresh kiwi and a tropical fizz, and the Virgin Mojito (₹460) delivered a classic minty-lime zing—each generously portioned and served promptly.
For appetizers, the Phad Khi-Mao Kung (stir-fried prawns with basil and chilies, ₹1040) was a spicy masterpiece, with juicy prawns and holy basil creating a bold, aromatic dish. The Satay Kai (chicken satay skewers, ₹860) featured tender, perfectly grilled meat with a creamy peanut sauce that balanced sweet and spicy notes flawlessly. Mains were a highlight, starting with the Tom Yam Kai (chicken Tom Yum soup, ₹520) and Tom Yam Kung (prawn version, ₹560), both tart and fragrant with lemongrass and chilies, warming us up delightfully. Pla Rad Phrik (fish in chili sauce, 2 portions at ₹980 each) offered crispy fillets in a tangy chili-garlic glaze, while Kaeang Phed Kai (red chicken curry, ₹780) was rich with coconut milk and tender chicken, paired with aromatic Khao Hom Mali (sticky rice, ₹380). The Koi Tiow Phad Thai Kai (Pad Thai noodles with chicken, ₹560) rounded it off with its sweet-tangy tamarind sauce and wide rice noodles, every dish arriving hot and fresh.

The total gross amount was ₹9120 before taxes, with CGST and SGST at 2.5% each (₹228 apiece), bringing the bill to around ₹9576—a fair price for the quality and authenticity. The fresh ingredients and genuine Thai flavors, honed over visits, make the cost worthwhile.

Tamnak Thai consistently delivers an explosive taste experience, seamless service, and a relaxing vibe. It’s my go-to for Thai cuisine in Mumbai, and I can’t wait to return. Going out here for drinks is preferable. Food,we haven't tried much but it was okish good.. Right at the Entrance of Hindu Colony. You might never notice this Cafe while passing by. Good for small group of friends or couple who prefers drinks.. Thanks, name_person=Nikhil Rane}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=ideal place for a small group to hang out over a beer or plan your travel. youthful atmosphere of the bar adds to your enthusiasm. the place is walkable from dadar station making it an ideal choice for a group comprising people from diverse places.  liquor is reasonably priced. food variety is good and tastes very well. seating capacity is a bit limited but there are many high chairs for solo travelers. service is quick and with a smile., name_person=Anand Patil}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=Located near Dadar station, Prithvi's Cavern is a small hangout place with chilled vibes, and not like the unnecessarily loud and boisterous clubs that are popping up everywhere. Last evening we went there early, (we were the first one's to enter in fact) and were greeted by a polite staff, dim lighting and mellow music. We opened our account with Smirnoff and peanuts, which come in two varieties, salted and masala. The Salted Peanuts were, well, salted peanuts, while the Masala Peanuts were really nice, with a seasoning of tomato and onion, not dissimilar to masala papad you might have had. Up next we ordered Chicken Meat Balls, (which weren't ball shaped) nice chunks of chicken, could've been better with some cheese in it. For the next round of drinks we had McDowell and Tropical Cooler, the latter being a mocktail which is converted into a cocktail by adding your choice of spirit to it. It was reminiscent of Blue Lagoon, a commonly served cocktail, since I chose to add vodka to the mocktail. A pointer regarding happy hours, they apply to beer only. Our next starter was Sausage Pepper Chilli Garlic and this was the standout dish for me. Sliced chicken sausages, spiced up with lot of chilli and pepper, with just a hint of garlic, this is a must have here. To end our innings we opted for Cheesy Chicken Nachos and a round of Old Monk. The nachos were a letdown, not as much cheese on it as expected, it was quite bland, even the accompanying salsa couldn't save it, you can give this a miss. To sum up then, Prithvi's Cavern is more a place for drinks and finger food than a wholesome dinner, (no desserts in the menu at all), and does it job quite well without burning up a big whole in your pocket. A bit cramped one might say, but I like the ambience, the music, and had no complaints with the service. I'll definitely be dropping in here again., name_person=Rohan Bidi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=\u20b9600\u2013800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS=[Themed_nights, E:DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS_THEMED_NIGHTS], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a week ago, review=had a great time here! love the vibe and food both! server is very polite and helpful, name_person=DS}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Very poor experience. No tables had reservation tag, neither the tables were next to each other, giving them benefit of doubt that one party might have booked all. No value for a walk-in customer. Never coming back., name_person=ANVESHA ANERAO}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=This place is near Dadar railway station in east. Ambiance is good. Price were too high for the quality of food they offered., name_person=Umesh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Paneer_Bullet], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Delivery, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=Durga Restaurant and Bar - A Culinary Delight!
We recently had food from Durga Restaurant and Bar, and I must say, the food was nothing short of amazing! We tried the Paneer Bullet, Paneer Handi Biryani, Aloo Masala Kulcha, Corn Salad, and Raita—and each dish exceeded our expectations.

The paneer deserves special praise—it’s hands down the best paneer in Mumbai. The Paneer Bullet had the perfect balance of crispiness and softness, while the Paneer Handi Biryani was incredibly flavorful, with rich spices and perfectly cooked rice. The Aloo Masala Kulcha was delicious and complemented everything beautifully. Even the Corn Salad and Raita were fresh and full of flavor.

Everything was fresh, and absolutely delicious. Highly recommend Durga Restaurant & Bar in Matunga for anyone looking for excellent food!, name_person=disha doctor}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=5 years ago, review=In a locale distinguished for vegetarian South Indian eateries, we stumbled upon a compact restaurant and bar, Durga Lunch Home, not far from Matunga Central station. As opposed to expectations it wasn't dimly lit, with fairly luminous lighting over every table. Being the 50th anniversary of the outlet, they had a couple of goodies, reduced prices on drinks and 5% off on the food bill if you upload a post on Instagram or check-in on Facebook. I opted for the former to avail the food discount. After browsing the vast menu, we opened our innings with a couple of whiskeys, and Prawns in Red Sauce. The seafood was an absolute pleasure, I rank it amongst the best prawns preparations I've ever had. The succulent prawns, the spicy sauce and the grated cheese all made for one heck of a starter. Up next was Chicken Israel, in white sauce. It was on the sweeter side, so may not be for everyone's palate, but I loved it, something of a discovery for me, sweetened meat in white sauce. The capsicum and peppers which garnished the dish were particularly well cooked, as well as juicy. This was followed by Chicken Teriyaki, one of the tried and tested chicken variants, and it was up to the mark. While the quantity was not as much as expected, taste-wise it was flawless, the viscous dark sauce working its magic on the meat. Our final order was Chicken Bullet, a spicy, flaming serving, with a sauce I felt to be very similar to the one used for the prawns. It turned out to be yet another winner, and I was more than happy to lap up beyond my share as my friend was feeling too full to intake anymore. To sum up then, Durga Lunch Home is a hidden gem in, what is a treasure trove, Matunga Central. The fact that it's existed for 50 years in an area I've frequented all my life and yet I've never even known of it shows how underappreciated it is. It's not exactly inexpensive in my opinion, but you do get a very loud bang for your buck, be it food or drinks. The service is quick and helpful, if at times a touch overenthusiastic. The waiters occasionally stand right next to the table, I hope they are better trained in the future to give the customers their privacy. Also, if some desserts are added to the menu, then this restaurant becomes a one-stop-shop for a full-fledged meal. I'm bound to be back soon, to try out the other delicacies on the expansive menu., name_person=Rohan Bidi}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Worst food ever. Ordered Veg Noodles which had 80% cabbage and 20% noodles and other veggies. Chicken crispy was pathetic too. For the price paid the food , service , ambiance all was waste. Too expensive for the quality & quantity of food + the ambiance is very congested.Many better options available around. Visit if u want to waste money and regret later, name_person=Juilee Thakur}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Atmosphere is good but 1 star is for cleanliness of the washroom here.

Although we initially had a bit of difficulty locating it, we eventually found it just beside INOX📽, tucked away in a cozy corner. The hunt was totally worth it!
As soon as we entered, the ambience caught our attention — a perfect mix of rustic charm and modern fusion, aptly justifying its quirky name. The lighting was aesthetic💫, and the music beautifully matched our relaxed, evening mood.🎊
Here’s how our experience unfolded:

Starters:🥗🥣

We ordered two paneer dishes, which seemed to be flavoured with black pepper. The taste was bold and comforting, and the presentation was on point.

Main Course:🍱

For mains, we went with biryani and noodles.

The biryani was aromatic, but both varieties tasted slightly similar, which was a minor letdown.

What we loved:

Fast and efficient service — no long waiting!

Spacious seating, ideal for small groups or cozy dates.

The decor and ambience made for Insta-worthy moments.📸

A good spot for food lovers seeking something different around Dadar., name_person=Mrudul Chandan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR, 5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT, 9+_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_NINE_OR_MORE], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Angrezi Dhaba is a bit of a hidden gem – quite literally. Finding the place can be a challenge, tucked away as it is, but the anticipation builds for what promises to be a unique dining experience. Upon entering, the decor and setup immediately impress. It's clear a lot of thought has gone into creating an inviting and stylish ambiance, blending a modern aesthetic with classic dhaba charm.
And then, the music hits.
While the food at Angrezi Dhaba is genuinely excellent – flavorful, well-presented, and a testament to a skilled kitchen – the entire experience is relentlessly undermined by the deafening volume of the music. Despite the place being relatively empty, and our polite requests to lower the volume, the staff claimed it was "difficult" to do so. This unaccommodating stance utterly destroys the potential of such a well-appointed space. What could be a pleasant meal with friends or family turns into a shouting match over the booming bass. Their lunch service goes on till 4:00 pm, with the last order taken at 3:15 pm. Luckily, we managed to reach just in time at 3:10 pm.

We ordered the KOKO Signature Roll (avocado, tempura asparagus, crisps, and KOKO sauce) along with Hong Kong Soy Noodles with chicken.

Our stay at ITC Grand Central was ruined by this restaurant experience.

We ordered one murgh tikka, lamb tawa, and 1 kashmiri roti, 1 paratha and one jeera rice (rice is NOT on the menu but we were able to order via the waiter). However our experience was totally dampened when we received the bill. The jeera rice was listed for 2635 rupees (we are from London and this equates to £24.50 for a bowl of rice). Ridiculous. We flagged to the waiter who confirmed this is the correct price. We requested the manager, who also confirmed its the correct price and asked how we would like to pay. We said no way are we paying for rice that expensive, charge us appropriately we said. He then went away for 10 minutes and came back with 15% off the rice. We were shocked to see the rice was still on the bill. We said no, the rice was not on the menu and they should charge us properly and appropriately for rice!! He said it is on the menu and we didn’t look properly. We then showed him the online menu from which we ordered from where not one single rice dish is mentioned and he said the menu must vary by device. He then went away for 10 minutes and came back with the rice removed.
