reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Qey - Sip & Vault in a sterling place for drink and dine Best suited for date night, group of friends, after-work drinks, stylish dinner outing. The design and interior are chic, elegant, spacious and beautiful. Music, lighting, and overall vibe are tailored for an special evening out - DJ sets, live performances are awesome. The “vault” membership concept adds a luxe, exclusive feel. The well curated menu offers European, Mediterranean, Middle Eastern fusion - chefs seem to play around with flavours and presentation - very fresh with great taste.
If you’re after a stylish evening with well-presented, flavour-forward plates rather than simple comfort food, QEY delivers. For food-centric visits, you might want to pick signature dishes in vegetarian like
• Cottage cheese kebab
• Turkish Manti
• Zaatar cottage cheese pide
• Tuscan Pici
• Taqueria bowl
• Desserts seem to leave a good mark - Salted caramel torte, Baklava cheesecake, Qey Sundae are scrumptious.
QEY has a strong focus on cocktails and a unique “sip & vault” concept: buy your bottle, store in their vault for next time. Cocktails and mocktails are beautifully crafted, perfectly balanced and unique. For cocktails and a premium bar experience, QEY hits strong. Loved its
• Grapefruit Picante
• To the Moon & Back
• Pink Coupe
• Cranberry elderflower serenade
• Summer Breeze
• Orange Chocolatini
The staff are attentive and friendly. The service is quick too. QEY is a strong choice for an upscale evening out in Lower Parel: great design + good food + standout drinks + lively ambience totally worth trying., name_person=Bhavin Parekh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a week ago, review=I recently visited QEY at Lower Parel (Kamala Mills), and wow — it was hands down one of the most outstanding dining experiences I’ve had in Mumbai. From the moment I walked in, the place felt grand, almost palatial: high ceilings, luxe interiors and a vibe that immediately transported me somewhere more international than local.
It was a Sunday lunch, and the light filtering through the space added a beautiful glow — calm, airy, and perfect for a relaxed, indulgent meal.
What I ate was nothing short of a feast: we went all out — there was chicken, prawns, fish and even clams. The clams especially stood out — tender, fresh and so flavourful — and the fish deserves a mention too; I’d go back just for that fish any day. Every plate arrived with such thoughtful presentation that it felt like art on a table.
We also tried a few of their cocktails — mixed live at the table — which was fun and added a playful, classy touch to the meal. And of course, I couldn’t skip dessert: I had one rich chocolate-based dessert and another creamy one — both wonderful ways to end the meal.
All in all, QEY feels like more than just a restaurant — it’s an experience. Between the ambiance, the food, the drinks, and the overall vibe, it made for a memorable outing. I’d absolutely recommend it to anyone looking for something special, and I know I’ll be back there soon., name_person=Shillpa Kataria Singh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Qey — Where the Sip & Vault concept turns dining into an experience.

Qey’s idea of Sip & Vault instantly sets it apart — it’s not just a restaurant, but a space where great conversations, inventive drinks, and artful food come together seamlessly. A very unique concept of storing your bottles in a vault makes this as a very convenient place to come again and again.

Ambience:
The space feels chic yet intimate — warm lighting, plush interiors, and a stylish crowd that gives it a cosmopolitan energy without being loud or overdone.

Food:
Every dish is thoughtfully crafted — the Mushroom Baklava is pure innovation, while the Mezze Platter is vibrant and full of character. The Harissa Spiced Chicken hits the right balance of spice and tenderness, Gambas Al Ajilo is buttery perfection, and Chicken Fricassee delivers deep, comforting flavour. The Baklava Cheesecake is a must-end — light, nutty, and indulgent.

Drinks:
The cocktail lineup truly completes the “Sip” experience — the Biscoff Royale is a decadent favourite, Pink Coupe elegant and refreshing, and Yuzu Ka bright and zesty with a creative edge.

Experience:
Qey masters the balance between concept and comfort. With its stunning design, crafted cocktails, and standout food, it’s easily one of the most well-executed new spots in town and the service fantastic

Place is bustling with it’s regular crowd and vault members overall a fun atmosphere and a must visit place, name_person=saurav verma}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Bar_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_BAR_AREA]}, time_line=a week ago, review=We recently hosted an office party at Qey Restaurant and Party Bar, and it was a wonderful experience overall. The ambiance was lively and perfect for a corporate gathering as well as casual celebrations.

The food quality and taste were excellent. There was a good variety of dishes, and everything was well-prepared and flavorful. The staff was courteous, cooperative, and ensured smooth service throughout the event.

The music, seating arrangement, and overall vibe made the party truly enjoyable. All our team members had a great time, and the place definitely added to the success of our office celebration.

I would highly recommend Qey Restaurant and Party Bar for office parties, group events, and celebrations. I love their theme of candle light dinner for couples. My finance took me there for a surprise. They displayed a legendary movie (I won't reveal it's name). I also liked how they have covered the AC duct with unique concept.
The food was authentic and delicious too., name_person=komal samjiskar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservation required, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Right in the heart of Kamala Mills, Lower Parel — Qey’s got that warm golden glow, chill beats, and the kind of vibe that instantly slows down your weekend.

Starting off with the Cranberry Elderflower Serenade — tangy cranberry, sweet pineapple, and that hint of elderflower… fresh, floral, and just happy in a glass.

Then came the Pesto Arancini — golden, crisp on the outside, soft pesto risotto inside, and that saffron mayo steals the show.

Next, the Orange Chocolatini — citrus meets chocolate in the most indulgent way possible. Sweet, rich, and slightly zesty — absolute mood.

The Cottage Cheese Kebabs followed — smoky, creamy, perfectly spiced, sitting on that soft zaatar pita. Comfort food done right.

Cut to the Taqueria Bowl — creamy avocado hummus, tangy salsa, grilled corn, all the textures in one perfect bite.
Then Tuscan Pici — burrata, pesto, and broccoli twirling together like an Italian daydream.

And dessert? That’s where Qey goes wild.
The Enchanted Brownie Forest — gooey, nutty, straight-up chocolate heaven.
And the Qey Sundae? Brownies, berries, cookie cream — pure happiness in a bowl.

Qey proves Jain food can be fun, fancy, and full of flavor. Bookmark this spot — your next craving starts here.

[{'name_person': 'Frahim Adajania', 'time_line': 'a week ago', 'review': 'I recently had dinner at Nara Thai and it turned out to be a really satisfying experience overall.
The standout dish of the evening was definitely the softshell crab — perfectly crispy on the outside, tender inside, and packed with flavour. It was easily my favourite dish of the night. The pandan leaves wrapped chicken was another highlight; beautifully fragrant, juicy, and well-seasoned, making it both comforting and indulgent.
The papaya salad was decent — fresh and balanced, but it didn’t quite wow me compared to the other dishes. It felt a bit milder than expected in terms of punch and spice.
We ended the meal with mango sticky rice, and it was a lovely finish. The mango was sweet and fresh, paired well with the creamy coconut sticky rice — simple, classic, and done right.
Overall, Nara Thai delivered on flavour and quality, especially with the starters and dessert. Spanning a generous 15,000 square feet, this rooftop eatery by restaurateurs Gaurav Dabrai and Kabir Luthria offers a laid-back vibe that’s perfect for watching the sunset—truly a luxury in the hustle of Mumbai.

The moment you step off the elevator and climb a short flight of steps, you’re greeted by soft amber skies (around 6 PM), friendly staff, and plenty of space to unwind. The seating includes cozy cabanas and tables under sail shades spaced far apart, giving the place an inviting, island-like feel. In fact, if you’ve experienced the nightlife in Greece, Praia’s atmosphere will remind you of the energetic bars in Mykonos.

One of the standout features is their dedication to live performances. There’s a stage set up for jazz dinners, supper theatre, weekend DJs, and more, ensuring a memorable dining and entertainment experience every time. Although they run only an evening service, Kabir points out that it was a deliberate choice to maintain a distinct nighttime charm at this location.

Whether you’re there to savor the scenic views, indulge in innovative cocktails (especially if you’re attending a launch like I did), or simply lounge under the stars, Praia has positioned itself as an unmissable spot in South Bombay’s dining scene. The highlight? Mommy’s Special Pizza, crafted in collaboration with Mommy’s Kitchen — comfort food reimagined with a luxe twist.

Their diverse global menu means you’ll find something exciting no matter what you’re craving.
The star of the night? The kebabs—assembled right in front of us by the chef and served piping hot.
We started with the truffle hummus topped with shaved truffle, and it was pure indulgence.
The sourdough pizza had that perfect crisp base and just the right amount of chew.
Cream cheese dimsums were soft, delicate, and packed with flavor.
The jackfruit adana kebab was a brilliant vegetarian twist—smoky, tender, and full of depth.

Overall, Cosy Box is the kind of place you go for the food but stay for the energy., name_person=Pankaj Kaklotar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Had a lovely evening at Cosy Box Mumbai! Chang’s at Lower Parel is one of those places you walk into with a certain set of expectations — especially for dinner. Big space, familiar menu, and that promise of bold Asian flavours. Our visit was mostly enjoyable, but a few things definitely held it back from being a great meal.

Let’s start with the biggest issue of the night — temperature. A surprising number of dishes arrived almost cold. Not “could be hotter” warm, but genuinely needing to be sent back. We had to request reheating more than once, which took away from the flow of the meal. For a restaurant of this scale and reputation, that was disappointing and honestly shouldn’t happen.

Drinks came first. The Samurai Fizz (2.5/5) was… fine. Refreshing, yes, but pretty forgettable. It didn’t really stand out in flavour. On the other hand, the Passionfruit Iced Tea (4.5/5) was excellent — well-balanced, refreshing, and easily the best drink we ordered.

Soups were a letdown. Both the Hot & Sour Soup (2/5) and Chang’s Noodle Soup (2/5) lacked depth and warmth — in flavour and temperature. They felt rushed and flat, which is a shame because these are usually comforting starters.

Things picked up once the appetisers started rolling in. The Shrimp Tempura Roll (4/5) was nicely done — crispy shrimp, clean flavours, and well-balanced textures. The Pan Fried Handmade Shrimp Dumplings (2/5), however, were underwhelming. Soft, yes, but bland and missing that punch you expect from dumplings.

Vegetarian dishes did surprisingly well. The Kung Pao Potatoes (4/5) were addictive — crispy, spicy, and full of flavour. Easily one of the better plates on the table.

Among the chicken dishes, both the Orange Chicken (4/5) and Dynamite Chicken (4/5) delivered what you expect — crispy, saucy, and comforting. No complaints there. But the real star of the night was the Ring of Fire Shrimp (5/5). Perfectly crispy, bold flavours, and just the right amount of heat. This dish alone made the wait and reheating worth it.

The Mongolian Tenderloin (3/5) was a mixed experience. The meat was beautifully tender, cooked just right, but the flavour was surprisingly bland. It needed more sauce or seasoning to really shine.

For sides, the Hong Kong Egg Fried Rice (4/5) was simple and satisfying, and the Chicken in Black Bean (4/5) was solid — comforting, flavourful, and reliable.

Desserts wrapped things up nicely. The Great Wall of Chocolate (4/5) was rich and indulgent without being too heavy, while the Banana Spring Roll (4/5) was crisp, warm, and a crowd-pleaser.

Where P.F. Chang’s really scored was service. The staff was extremely friendly, attentive, and handled the reheating requests politely and efficiently. They genuinely tried to make the experience better, which made a big difference. The atmosphere was pleasant — lively but not chaotic — making it a comfortable place for a dinner outing.

Overall, P.F. Chang’s Lower Parel had some strong dishes and excellent service, but the repeated issue of food being served cold brought the overall experience down. If they can fix that one major flaw, it would easily be a much better dining spot. There are both indoor and outdoor seating options, including a rooftop or outdoor area with cover, which is perfect in evenings.\\n\\nThe food is mostly modern Indian with creative twists: great starters like Khow Suey Samosa, Beetroot Mozzarella Seekh, Zafrani Tangdi, and mains like Butter Chicken, Paneer Achaari, Dal Bukhara with Laccha Paratha etc.  Desserts like Gulkand Cheesecake and Matka Rabri Gulab Jamun get very good feedback.\\n\\nThe drinks/cocktails are also a highlight. Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Ditas Mumbai, and the experience left me thoroughly impressed. Here's a detailed review of the delightful dishes we tried:

1. **Bruschetta Plank:**
The Bruschetta Plank was a perfect start to our meal. The crispy toasted bread paired with a medley of fresh tomatoes, basil, and drizzled with balsamic glaze was a symphony of flavors. Each bite was a burst of freshness, setting the tone for the culinary journey ahead.

2. **Greek Salad:**
The Greek Salad was a refreshing and authentic rendition of this classic dish. Crisp vegetables, feta cheese, olives, and a zesty dressing created a harmonious blend. The quality of ingredients shone through, making it a standout salad that I would happily order again.

3. **Sweet Potato Sliders:**
The Sweet Potato Sliders were a revelation. The sweet potato patties were perfectly seasoned and had a delightful texture. Coupled with fresh greens and a unique sauce, these sliders offered a satisfying combination of sweet and savory that left us craving for more.

4. **Baked Vegetable Cannelloni:**

No bollywood songs until its 10:30pm. Post that its bollywood + hollywood. So if you’re thinking to dance on Indian songs, this is a very bad choice., name_person=Mithun Sawant}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=8 months ago, review=Visited Permit and Co. by Gymkhana 91, with my family on a buzzing Friday night, and it instantly transported me back to the charm of 90s Mumbai bars. The retro-inspired interiors, dim lighting, and soulful music create a nostalgic vibe that feels both familiar and fresh, like a modern homage to Bombay’s bar culture. We totally loved this concept, something which bought our memories back.

I must say the place was lively, packed with energy, and had a great playlist that kept the mood upbeat all evening. Service was smooth despite the crowd, and the staff was warm and attentive., Specially Amar, he was a great server and ensured we had a great time, loved his recommendation on food.

The food was flavorful and well-curated!! The highlights for us were the Veg Himalayan Thukpa, Dosh Momo, and Paneer Cheese Kebab.
And yes the must must try cocktails taking inspiration from old Bombay, it completely stole the show — “Oh My Darling” and “LIC” are a must-try. They’re inventive, well-balanced, and absolutely worth it, also the Sobo Snob, I loved it.

Permit and Co. isn’t just a place to eat and drink, it’s a vibe, total nostalgic with their food menu and chakhnas to pair with. A Perfect place for anyone who loves good food, great cocktails, and a setting that stirs a bit of nostalgia., name_person=shikhani shah}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=11 months ago, review=Permit & Co. brings the nostalgia of 80's and 90's Bollywood music similar to Bombay Daak. The food is good, with portions that match the ambiance, but the menu lacks originality. Standouts include the Chakna tray , similar to the one they had at Bombay canteen .

House cocktails are nice but don’t have anything Whisky based suggestions , but classic drinks are made well.

The ambiance is lively, with an outdoor , convenient smoking area on the same floor . Staff are attentive and friendly, especially the welcoming hosts. However, the washroom experience was a letdown due to ongoing construction., name_person=Chirag Patel}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=7 months ago, review=Such a lovely vibe and a tribute to the permit rooms of older Bombay! Lovely drinks and food that takes you down memory lane, with some absolutely stellar service! You will definitely go back once you’ve been there!, name_person=Charles Victor}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=8 months ago, review=Permit & Co by Gymkhana 91 is a fantastic place to chill, hangout, party and dine.

The food here is delicious with some unique combinations and flavours.

The complimentary Chakna is super fun to eat with their cocktails. We loved the imli chokha and chilli guava and raw mango.

Must try-
Kuber chilli cheese kulcha.
Spicy, gooey, cheesy goodness.

Jhol momos.. spicy.. yet delicious.

Phodni Burrata… creamy, tangy, sweet.. yum

Laping cheung fung ..

Naga chilli dal khichdi .. super spicy, little sweet, garlicky.. yum quite unique.

Loved the food here!

The cocktails and mocktails were good!

Overall a good place to try., name_person=1TeaspoonLove}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Delivery, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=10 months ago, review=Permit & Co brings the old nostalgic era of iconic Permit Rooms in Mumbai (Then Bombay) an ode to the drinking culture!

Opened 3 months ago, this place will transports you back in time with its vintage décor with minimalistic interiors (Wooden chairs & tables, checkered table cloth, servers in Tie) and a massive bar at one end.

The Cocktail menu is inspirational from different aspect of Bombay while the food menu boasts about everything from a wholesome Chakna platter to intricate Himalayan Thukpa!

From the Cocktail section, we highly recommend “Oh My Darling”, “Aam-Chi Permit” for the perfect blend of concoctions and the taste in each sip!  And if you’re someone up for a sneaky affair, then “Smuggle My Negroni” is your go-to drink!

From the Appetizer section, we absolutely loved the “Madrasi Chana Hummus” followed by “Nizaami Haleem” – Both were different & Impeccable!  The “Paneer Cheese Kebab” was supe soft & cheesy in each bite, and of course, we treated ourselves to the full-fledged “Timepass Chakna Platter”

From the Mains, we enjoyed the flavours of “Himalayan Thukpa” & Naga Dal Khichdi” and also indulged in ”Bacon Butter Chicken” to complete our meal!

Couldn’t resist the dessert section when it boasted about “Tiffin Tiramisu” & Ferrero Rocher Chocolate Dome” We ordered both these items and were a perfect sweet ending to a lovely dining experience.

Mr. Akbar, thank you for taking care of us, and we will be back again soon!, name_person=Vinu Vijayan}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Pricing is fair given the location, ambience, drinks & food menu.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The dumplings were juicy and flavour-packed, classic Indo-Chinese.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=& I appreciated the staff recommended good food & Service.}"]

The restaurant is located in the Kamala Mills compound, so getting there is pretty easy.

The ambience is great. The restaurant is well maintained, clean and beautiful. The outdoor seating should probably be avoided during the monsoon. The tables are well spaced and the music is just the right volume so you don't need to shout to talk.
The service is quick and friendly. They will explain the menu and the contents of the dishes very well. They also accommodate dietary restrictions. They charge 10% as service fee.
The menu is fully vegetarian and expansive. They mainly cover Asian, Italian, and Mexican cuisines. We started with the comforting and tasty hot and sour mini soup. The Italian Tartine was tasty, the crostini were perfect to munch on. The Chilaquiles Filo Cups were a miss, the cups were nicely crisp but the guacamole was totally bland. The udon noodles were extremely tasty and were the second best item we tasted. Mind you, the noodles portion is large (for three, I'd guess). The kitchen seems to have nailed the Asian and Italian cuisine.

Overall, the experience was largely comforting. Definitely recommended, would revisit to taste more of the large menu., name_person=Viraj Khedekar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Chilaquiles_Filo_Cups], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=8 months ago, review=If you're a guac lover like me, you're in for a treat! We kicked things off with the Chilaquiles Filo Cups, and let me tell you-the guac was chef's kiss! The crispy, flaky texture of filo cups made every bite a delight.
Next up, the Mexican Tacodillas-creamy, with a simple yet satisfying filling.
For mains, the Genovese Pizza stole the show with its perfect crunch and just the right touch of caramelized brown onions. Then came the 2 Cheese Ravioli, generously topped with basil pesto sauce-because, let's be honest, cheese + pesto is always a winning combo!
One of our absolute faves? The Cottage Cheese Twists!🤤
The gravy was packed with flavor, and pairing it with sundried tomato olive roti? Game changer. 💯
They also have great cocktails & mocktails, trust the bartender's choice for it.
To wrap it all up, we indulged in the Lotus Biscoff Tea Cake with Coffee Ice Cream-an absolute must for coffee lovers ☕️ Rich, decadent, and a total devour-worthy dessert.
Beyond the food, the restaurant boasts ample space, elegant interiors, and picturesque wall; making it a great pick for parties, get-togethers, girls brunch or even a cozy date. Cafe Trofima, located near the bustling Shivaji Park in Dadar, has garnered attention as a popular hangout spot, but it falls short of the hype for several reasons.

Food

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. While it has some redeeming qualities like decent seating and satisfactory service, the compromised food taste, lack of parking, and high prices make it hard to recommend wholeheartedly. It could work as a one-time visit for those curious about its breakfast platters, but better options are available in and around the area for a more satisfying experience.

This all-vegetarian gem truly exceeded my expectations. I tried their Crispy Lotus Root starter and the Paneer Shashlik Sizzler, and both dishes were absolutely delicious. The lotus root was perfectly crisp with a unique flavor that stood out, while the sizzler was sizzling hot, full of flavor, and generously portioned with tender paneer and grilled veggies.

The ambiance was cozy and welcoming, and the staff were warm and attentive throughout. Whether you're a vegetarian or just someone who appreciates good food, this place is a must-visit. I’ll definitely be coming back to try more from their menu!

Highly recommended! 🌱✨, name_person=Komal Gala}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Mexican_Tacos_with_India_Pulka, Mediterranean_Platter, Chinese_Sizzler, Hummus_Platter, Hummus_Plate], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Menu_is_all_vegetarian, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_COMPLETELY_VEGETARIAN]}, time_line=a year ago, review=Overall rating: 4.5/5
Taste: 4/5
Service: 5/5

- Tom yum soup
Rating: 5/5

- Mediterranean platter
Rating: 6/5

- Cottage cheese taco:
Rating: 4.5/5
Taste: Nice! Soft paneer and tasty sauce. Tastes good with lemon.

- Malai broccoli
Rating: 2.5/5

- Chef garden pizza

- Veg sizzler with hot soya chilli
Rating: 5/5

- Watermelon and normal mojito
Rating: 4/5

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 weeks ago, review=​Hands down the best Japanese restaurant in Mumbai right now! I’ve tried many places across the city, but Donmai in Worli is on another level.
​We ordered a variety of dishes and the authentic taste really stood out. The Chicken Karaage was perfectly crispy and juicy, and the Salmon Sashimi was incredibly fresh—truly melt-in-the-mouth quality. You also have to try their Signature Sushi Rolls; the texture and balance of flavors were spot on.
​The vibe is a perfect mix of chill and upscale. If you are looking for top-tier, authentic Japanese food, this is the place. Highly recommended!, name_person=Rohit Sharma}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 months ago, review=The food was decent overall, though nothing particularly memorable. We tried the *asparagus uramaki sushi*.. it was okay, but quite ordinary. The *Togarashiii* (smoked tequila cocktail) was actually quite good, and the *furikake chips* made for a nice snack. The *wasabi fries*, however, were quite off. The real standout was the *Kinoko Don pot rice*.. beautifully flavoured mushrooms and a really comforting, well-balanced dish. That was definitely the highlight.
Ambience was decent but not extraordinary, and prices felt a bit on the higher side for what it offered. Overall, an okay experience..nice to try once, but not a place I would go back to., name_person=Neha Desai}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Ambience was very good. Food was also very good. They helped us with suggestions. We ordered, shrimp tempura sushi, kareman, chicken miso ramen and japanese cheesecake to eat and cherry mocktail, matcha boba and wasabi mocktail to deink. All 3 were amazing. I didn't check the bar menu. If I had more appetite I would have definitely tried to find some cocktail in the cherry mocktail. Kareman was not on the menu as it will be launched for the next month menu. This was a veg option with egg or beacon as add on option. We had egg. The base of both the ramen were of oat milk which gives a flavour and texture similar to coconut milk with peanuts. We liked Kareman more than Chicken miso ramen. Japanese cheesecake was amazing. It was freshly baked. They gave it along with seasalt icecream and some crumbs. I think it was something like pie crumbs. The whole dish was complementing each other but I would have preferred the crumbs to be a little less sweeter and seasalt icecream was too salty. I wish it had less salt. The icecream had a zing of orange which was subtle and was complimenting the dish overall so well. It's like having salt, sweet, very little tangy and absolutely spongy cheesecake.
They ask for dietary restrictions and allergens before taking the order., name_person=Arushi Joshi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=2 months ago, review=The place is spacious and the sushi is amazing. We loved the staff’s recommendation for food and drink. Potion size is quite small though. One thing which was very off putting is multiple flies (fruit-flies) around our table which made us rush through our lunch. Even the staff didn’t do anything to address the issue, name_person=Hussain Kagzi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Valet parking available. The restaurant has a wonderful decor. The bar area and the ceiling hanging catches the attention on entering. The temperature inside was very cold to our discomfort but inspite of repeated requests they couldn’t unfreeze the temperature

The service was very slow and the waiters were not making any eye contacts although loitering around.

Post order the food arrived fast. The portion is limited thus order intelligently. Pricing is premium, definitely due to the location

Overall was not very satisfied probably due to the chillness inside that made me uncomfortable and did not allow me to enjoy the food., name_person=Indradeep Roy}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=So good!! Celebrated a special occasion with family and everything was perfect. The food was tasty, the coconut matcha latte which was recommended was superb and the service and ambience amazing.

Price was so reasonable as well for how much we ordered!!

The Chicken Fried rice and matcha fondant dessert were the highlights!

Will definitely be back!!, name_person=Lameeya Bandukwala}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Would not recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a month ago, review=Great place with a great ambience
The Halloween theme during my visit was great addition
This place is great if you want to eat authentic japanese cuisine
Although some people might find the food a little low on the spice level it's mainly because our Indian palate is used to high spice levels
Overall loved the experience, name_person=shailesh kotian}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=5 months ago, review=The Hotpot that is a monsoon speciality was everything it should be. Warm broth with fresh vegetables n mushrooms, udon noodles, rice ,seafood which we have to blanch ourselves. Such a warm hug on cold rainy days ..highly recommend it !, name_person=nisha b}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Excellent menu and vibe, good service, great selection of food}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Enjoyed the Gomai, Avo Sushi, Yasai Yaki Noodles, Katsura Curry..}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The combination of crispy, savory, and umami flavors is absolute perfection.}"]

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Not sure, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=2 months ago, review=I visited Masoli recently and honestly, the experience was very disappointing. The service was pathetic — no staff attended to us until we had to repeatedly ask, even for basic things like water. Drinks were served late, and overall, there was no attentiveness at all.

The food was another letdown. We ordered Pomfret Fry which was undercooked, with most of the flesh still raw. The Bombil Thali was completely bland — the javla had no taste and no salt (even after adding salt, it was flavorless). The kolambi masala was extremely spicy but without any real taste or balance, and I usually have a high spice tolerance. On top of that, the bhakri served was not rice bhakri but maida, chewy and totally off.

Special mention to the staff handling our table, Manish — he was not attentive at all and definitely needs to be trained in customer service. If customers are paying their hard-earned money, the least expected is basic hospitality and properly cooked food.

Overall, a very poor experience.

We tried:
🥔 Sweet Chili Potato – Amazinggggg! Crispy, tangy, and full of flavour.
🌮 Nachos – Packed with layers, cheese, and crunch. Way too good to miss.
🍜 Garlic Coriander Noodles – Must must must try! Bursting with bold Asian flavours.
🍫 Asian Garden Dessert – A dreamy treat for dark chocolate lovers. Absolute heaven.

Perfect place for a date night or group hangout., name_person=Khushi Porwal}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=6 months ago, review=I recently visited this restaurant on my wife's birthday, drawn in by its great ambience and inviting atmosphere. The decor and setting were well thought out, making for an enjoyable dining environment.

We ordered a couple of starters, sushi, and a main dish. While the starters were flavorful, the quantity did not justify the price, leaving us feeling that the portions could have been more generous. The real disappointment came when we discovered a long hair in our sushi. This instantly raised concerns about the quality and hygiene of the food.

When we pointed this out to the staff, they handled the situation politely and professionally, taking the dish away and offering us a replacement. While this was appreciated, the incident had already dampened our experience, and we chose to simply request the bill instead.

Surprisingly, the bill still included charges for the sushi as well as service charges. Upon bringing this to their attention, the staff quickly removed those charges. However, they should not have been added in the first place, given the situation.

One positive takeaway was the politeness and courteousness of the staff, who handled the issue without hesitation. Menu covers Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese cuisine. Among non alcoholic drinks, Kumbocha is worth trying. Dim sums as well as Sushi are good. Butter garlic prawns also worth trying. There are very limited dessert options here., name_person=Supriya Devasthali}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=8 months ago, review=Visited Ping’s Café Orient in Lower Parel for a dinner catch-up with friends, and it turned out to be a mixed bag. The place has a cozy, quirky vibe, they’ve got Vietnamese hats hanging on the walls and framed photos that give off travel café aesthetics, which I really liked.

Coming to the food, we tried the drunken noodles, veg SoBo fried rice, veg cheesy dimsums, and veg crackling sushi. The dimsums were the star of the meal, super soft, cheesy, and just the right kind of indulgent. Honestly, I’d go back just for them.

The SoBo fried rice tasted good but was quite dry, and the portion size was underwhelming. The sushi didn’t work for me at all, lacked balance in flavors and texture. We were served rice crackers with five kinds of dips, which was a nice touch, though.

Some of my non-vegetarian friends tried the Thai-style chicken rice, and the feedback wasn’t great, dry and bland, unfortunately. For the six of us, the bill came up to ₹6,000, which felt steep considering the portion sizes.

The staff was polite and welcoming, though they seemed a bit short-handed. Service was decent but could’ve been quicker.

Overall, it’s a cute spot with potential, especially for the ambiance and those heavenly dimsums. But if you’re going for a full meal, don’t expect large portions or consistent quality across the menu.

Location: 2nd Floor, Customer Square, C K Narar Marg, Shivaji Park, Dadar West, Mumbai

We were a group of 10 looking for an indulgent seafood and coastal meal in Mumbai and Coast & Bloom delivered beyond expectations. With a modern, minimalistic ambience and a menu that is curated Malvani inspirations and there were some mains like Chettinad, konkani and goan, this spot is perfect for both celebrations and leisurely meals.

What We Ordered

Our feast included a fantastic mix of seafood, meats, and sides:

- Crab Kakori

- Shallow Fried Malvani Bombil

- Chicken Chilli

- Chicken Malvani Masala

- Prawns Bhujane

- APC Pomfret & APC Crab

- Pasta Arrabiata for kids

- Rice Bhakri, Ghavane, Wade

- Solkadi

Everything was rich, flavorful, and well-prepared, especially the seafood, which was fresh and cooked to perfection.

Service Excellence

Special shout-out to Chandani, Chandan, and Roshan, they took exceptional care of us from start to finish. For a table of 10, the service was quick, warm, and always attentive. They made excellent suggestions and ensured every dietary need was handled with care.

Price & Value

Medium to high priced considering the generous portions and seafood quality. Value for money for group dining with great ambiance.

The ever-popular 145 franchise has now opened its doors at Kamala Mills, adding yet another reason to visit this buzzing hub. Tucked away on the quieter back road of Kamala Mills, this outlet blends the relaxed charm of a café with the energy of a lively bar, making it a perfect pick for both day and night outings.

Pros;

1. The biggest highlight is the ambience — spacious, welcoming, and full of life. The warm colour palette, comfortable seating, and a small dance floor create just the right vibe for a good time.

2. Fresh, well-prepared food that delivers on quality every single time.

3. Generous portion sizes, ideal for sharing between two people.

4. Prompt and attentive service that keeps the experience smooth.

Cons;
None worth noting.

What we ordered;
🔸️ Ferrero Rocher Freakshake; RECOMMENDED
A chocolate lover’s dream! Thick, creamy, and indulgent, this freakshake is packed with chocolate chunks, syrup, and milk, crowned with colourful Gems and chocolate treats. Heavy and rich — perfect for serious sweet cravings.
Rating: 4/5

🔸️ Oomph; HIGHLY RECOMMENDED
One of the best cranberry-based mocktails I’ve tried. Fresh cranberry juice muddled with pear, topped with ginger ale and lime — a refreshing duo that works perfectly together. A must-try for non-alcoholic drink lovers.
Rating: 4.5/5

🔸️ Chili Paneer; RECOMMENDED
A quick Chinese-style bite in a café bar setting. Soft paneer tossed with green chilies, ginger, and onions, making it a crowd-pleasing starter. Definitely worth ordering.
Rating: 4/5

🔸️ Jalapeño Poppers; RECOMMENDED
Golden, crispy bites filled with cheese, jalapeños, corn, and chili. A starter that’s universally loved — even better when paired with a cocktail.
Rating: 4/5

🔸️ Paneer Makhanwala Biryani; RECOMMENDED
A vegetarian take on the Butter Chicken Biryani we loved last time, featuring paneer tikka and a rich makhanwala gravy. While slightly on the dry side, it still stood out as a flavorful North Indian option.
Rating: 4/5

🔸️ Chicken Manchurian Fried Rice; RECOMMENDED
An all-time classic! The fried rice was well-cooked and paired with flavorful Manchurian — simple, comforting, and exactly what you’d expect.
Rating: 4/5

Final Verdict;
Every place has its strengths, and this one offers more positives than negatives. Prices are on par with most popular cafés, making it a great value for the quality and portions served. From flavour-packed dishes to an ambience that sets the mood, 145 Mills delivers a memorable dining experience. A big thank you to the team for making it special — I’d absolutely recommend visiting to enjoy the food, the vibe, and the service. Younion season 2 is something you shouldn't miss out on.

Location: Younion is located at one of the most happening places of the town known for some really good places to hangout and night life i.e. Kamla Mills, Lower Parel.

About the Place:
A perfect place for a perfect night out along with your friends is what we would say. Younion has everything that will impress you. Each wall is beautifully decorated.   The artificial plants hanging through ceiling, nicely spaced seating arrangements, amazing music played over here and the crowd that visits this place helps to create that perfect vibe.

Younion has more than 300 shots and 25 variety of new cocktails at an affordable rates on their menu for your gang. They also have 50 new LIIT's & the menu is also made vast with more 80 dishes, largest pizza, burger & Dimsums. The food over here is also good. They have some really good fusion food perfect to have along with your drinks.

We visited this place on a Friday evening and trust us it was packed. The place is really good and the moment we entered the place we knew that we gonna spend a good time..!! The service at this place is quick and they really help you when you are confused with what to order. Kudos to Pravin for helping us with the order. We quickly ordered our drinks and food and here's what we had. Jain food is also available here.
In Drinks we tried mocktails & cocktails.
-Berry cooler, hangover, you must try this, courgae basil. Lovely drinks is what we would say.

In food we loved the
-Loaded sheet pan nachos  which was loaded with chhedar & mozzarella cheese and served with jalapeno, bell pepper & sour cream. Highly recommended.

Also not to miss out on their delicious
-Truffle shroom Burger-
Shittake mushroom, with truffle mayo & cheese. It was one of the best burger we have had in recent times. Highly Recommended..!!

Avocado green out pizza
Pizza based topped with avocado, sun-dried tomatoes, olives, parmesan & jalapenos. It was good to taste.

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservation required, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Very quiet, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=I visited Waarsa after seeing a few reels about their Biryani Festival, but honestly, it didn’t quite live up to the hype. I tried the Islampuri Chaap Biryani — the mutton was well-cooked and flavourful, inspired by Bengal-style biryani. Interestingly, they used sweet potato instead of the usual potato, and the classic boiled egg was missing. The mutton portion was generous, but the rice quantity was just enough for one person. To be fair, the staff was kind enough to offer an extra bowl of rice for my friend.

I also tried the Tangdi Kebab, which was soft, juicy, and nicely done — not extraordinary, but definitely enjoyable. The Mutton Galouti Kebab was the real winner — absolutely delicious. The Dal Makhani was standard, like what you’d get at most restaurants.

Maybe I went in with high expectations after seeing all the hype online, but overall, I’d say it’s a decent experience made better by their warm, courteous staff and good service., name_person=Aditi Datta}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=4 weeks ago, review=It's difficult to find good North Indian delicacies in Mumbai. For starters we had,
Rajma Chukander ki Galouti: 4/5
Kairi Shakarandi ka Tikka: 4/5

In mocktails,
Divine Passion: 4/5
Zero Proof Americano: 6/5

For mains,
Kache Kale ke kofte: 5/5

Taftan: 3/5

All and all, an experience worth reliving., name_person=Rohit Rawat}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Waarsa at NCPA, Nariman Point, is a gem serving authentic Awadhi cuisine.

The food is flavorful yet light, with dishes like Raan-e-Mukhtar (slow-cooked goat leg) and Zafrani Lagaan Murgh stealing the show.

Vegetarian options like Bhindi Kali Mirch and Lauki aur Chana Dal Shikhampuri are equally delightful.

The Kesar Phirni was the highlight—creamy, aromatic, and perfectly sweet.

Their cocktails, like The Emperor’s Rose and Gin Gilori, are creative and pair well with the meal.

The ambiance is stunning, with salmon-hued walls, intricate ceilings, and elegant decor, creating a warm, royal vibe.

Service is top-notch, attentive, and friendly, making the experience special. Chefs Rahul Akerkar and Mukhtar Qureshi, culinary geniuses, craft a menu blending royal and home-style Awadhi flavors.

Owned by Aditya Birla New Age Hospitality, Waarsa is a must-visit for food lovers seeking an unforgettable dining experience in Mumbai.

Cocktails:

Emperor Rose: A refreshing, floral drink.  Gin Gilori: A gin-based cocktail with delicate flavors.  Court Jester: Gin with pickled Bhavnagri chili, jasmine, and mint.   Despite some inconsistency in early reviews, the drinks complement the cuisine beautifully.

Popular Dishes:Non-vegetarian: Raan-e-Mukhtar, Zafrani Lagaan Murgh, Murgh Gilafi Seekh Kebab, Rampuri Kacche Gosht ki Tikki.

Vegetarian: Bhindi Kali Mirchi, Lauki aur Chana Dal Shikhampuri, Awadhi Tawa Paneer Pasanda, Kasundi Baingan Tikka.

Desserts: Kesar Phirni, Angoori Rabdi.  Others: Chilgoza Shorba, Gucchi Biryani, Daal Q-Man.

•chipotle chicken wings :

•Quesadilla

•pork belly ‘pernil’
Not to be missed this Puerto Rican roast pork is perfection, skin is crisp meat is tender. The sauces are chefs kiss and bring together each bite.

•Taco Al pastor
This one was fire and really just 👌
We could’ve eaten 2 plates of these.
I can’t even begin to explain. The masa? 🥹 its freshly made. Are they nixtamalizing the corn themselves?! Cause tortilla perfection.

•Shrimp Tacos

Not gonna lie to you these tacos slapped absolutely undoubtedly — but I’m a salsa girl at heart if I eat a taco, I want to slap some extra salsita in there; not a complaint just know chef makes delectable sauces so any salsa he could think up for the table with tacos 🫡 I’m sure would be bomb.

Overall t’was a fiesta of a date night we were too stuffed for desert (don’t worry we regretted it later when we were less stuffed)

Over all?
Chef Alex has done it OTRAvez ;)

I usually start with 5 stars and deduct or mark up based on my experience.

We came here as my son wanted to compare the Taj, we have been to a few times, and the Oberoi. We had just watched the India Women's team face the Aussies at the Wankhede and no taxi would take us the short distance to the Oberoi so we legged it. It was nice to see Deepti Sharma picking up her keys after watching her make a 50 about 30 mins ago.

The staff welcomed us into the restaurant and we placed our orders for starters and mains. The prawn cocktail and grilled prawn starters were well presented, and cooked well but there was nothing special about their taste. Mains were the seafood risotto and the pan seared barramundi. The presentation was much to be desired from though they tasted ok but nothing special.

I would suggest the chef should spend a few weeks as a sous chef with Gordon Ramsay to learn presentation. If theu can't afford Ramsay I would suggest a week in my kitchen, in London, will definitely help them up their game.

Why I mention presentations is because Frangipani isn't inexpensive and the only reason for being inexpensive shouldn't be because they are based in the Oberoi. The chef needs to make an effort to cook and present well when they work in good quality restaurants.

Oh and did I mention that they couldn't offer us any pizza or bruschetta as the oven was broken thus further reducing the limited choice menu down., name_person=Rajesh Gosain}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=Edited 2 years ago, review=This was my first visit to this restaurant.

Upfront, I was served the bread basket having 4 varieties of bread, amongst which the red was the best. As opposed to my prima facia thought, it was neither sweet nor related to red velvet in any way.

In the main course directly, I tried a Salmon here in their default preparation, and it was very good although the sides primarily having couscous didn't taste nice. Reckon the traditional mashed potatoes would have been a better option.

I also tried another Salmon, this time specifically asking for traditional mashed potatoes at the sides, and it was given the way I would have wanted ( medium-done ) and was very good too.

The preparation time for both was c 25  mins, which is the average time for such dishes. The quantity was between small and medium when juxtaposed with the competitors.

In between, I wanted to try out an item from the buffet, a couple of cheese cuts, and the staff courteously allowed me to do so.

The mocktails were nice too despite not really corresponding to their descriptions. The first one ( orange-coloured ) ( exact name forgotten ) was quite different in taste, and on a bit thicker side. Kinda seemed like fruit juice more than the soda-based mocktail which it was ideally supposed to be. The second one viz Brazilian Virgin Mojito was the same as the normal Virgin Mojito one gets everywhere with medium power soda. I can only reasonably hunch that the prefix 'Brazil' is added to gain an attraction. Both were served within 10 mins, and the quantity was medium when juxtaposed with the competitors.

At the end, I was offered some special dark chocolates, they were delicious and I am thankful to the staff for the same.

The decor when compared to the neighbouring India Jones is not very fancy, there are about 25 tables in the restaurant which also serves the buffet and the area is quite big, and the background setting is medium ( India Jones in comparison has dim lights ). The chairs are of the same type, and at medium-level seating. The beverage menu is either not available or significantly incompletely uploaded on online food/dining sites/apps and necessary amends should be made on those respects. Also, the food menu uploaded on the food/dining app/sites is not updated, so the latest one would be appreciated.

Overall, it was a nice experience, and I will definitely visit again.

Second Visit

I began with the complimentary bread basket consisting of 4 types of bread, just like the previous visit. Coming to the main course directly, I ordered fish&chips on my second visit to this restaurant. As is the norm, it came along with French fries and tartare sauce. Slightly on the bitter side as they always are, and not severely fried ( so weren't too oily, which is appreciated ), and tasted nice. 4 medium-sized pieces so overall the portion was bigger than average. The French Fries were stale though, and upon complaining, a fresh portion was bought but this took quite a while ( ~15 mins ) and I had to give a reminder. The tartare sauce wasn't white and not on the thick side as normally it is ( but very liquidy ), and this was the smallest quantity I had got with a fish and chips dish hitherto. However, upon asking, the staff bought another quantity of the incredibly small tartare sauce.

The mocktail Sangria was fit as per the description, and I could feel the bitterness of the tonic water it consisted of. The drink came with apple cuts and tasted very nice. Different members of the kitchen team explained each dish in detail. The team was very passionate and sweet. The tasting menu experience easily takes two hours and we are very grateful for the innovative dishes and the hard work behind it.

We weren't completely in love with the sweets, but maybe that's more on us not having much of a sweet tooth.

Small note: we usually don't have leafs that are already eaten by worms. Despite being heavily processed there is always a chance that their is egg residue left behind. All of us at the table noticed it but somehow while leaving we forgot to mention it and show our appreciation for her.

But I this is what sets apart the best restaurants from the good ones. It’s not just food, which Ekaa is obviously excellent at, but it is this attention to detail that keeps us coming back. This is what makes Ekaa Ekaa., name_person=Anshul Shah}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The place itself has a chill vibe, super friendly staff, and great music.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good ambience , good service, good food , fine classy taste..}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=We got 5 tapas, 5 mains and 2 desserts + cocktails between 5 people.}"]

Mumbai's dining scene just received a stunning upgrade with the opening of Otoki at Apollo Bunder, a new sanctuary dedicated to specialty Japanese cuisine. From the moment we were settled at the intimate sushi tables, we knew we were in for a memorable experience. Otoki’s dedication to pristine ingredients and technical skill quickly turned our lunch into a true celebration of flavour, leaving us with broad smiles.

The Sublime Sushi Experience
Our focus was entirely on the raw bar, and Otoki delivered a masterclass in precision and quality. Every piece was a miniature work of art.
The Nigiri selection was flawless: the classic Bluefin Tuna Akami was pristine, and the Unagi (eel) was perfectly glazed. The Hotate (scallop) melted delicately on the tongue, but the true surprise was the Pickled Tomato nigiri—a burst of innovative, acidic freshness that elevated the traditional lineup.

The Sashimi course was a moment of sheer indulgence. The Bluefin Tuna Otoro offered that characteristic, luxurious marbling that defines perfection, dissolving on the palate with a rich, buttery texture.

The Maki rolls were meticulously crafted and perfectly balanced. We thoroughly enjoyed the traditional Norimaki, the bright, citrusy notes of the Yuzu Salmon, and the clean simplicity of the Bluefin Tuna Akami roll.

To cap off the meal, the desserts provided a sophisticated finish: the earthy sweetness of the Warabi Mochi paired perfectly with the sharp, aromatic brightness of the Yuzu Ice Cream.

Hospitality and Passion
While the food was phenomenal, the exceptional hospitality truly elevated our visit. The chefs at Otoki are a delight, well-informed, and visibly passionate about their craft.

We were fortunate enough to be looked after by Chef Yunus, who ensured we loved every bite and guided us with spot-on recommendations. He was wonderfully accompanied by Chef Rahul. Chef Yusuf, was wonderful at ensuring we were comfortable and made time for great conversations. A great host.

The entire staff is great, friendly, and contributes to the welcoming atmosphere.

Looking Ahead
Otoki currently operates a limited menu for lunch, but based on the exemplary quality we experienced, we are already counting down the days until our next visit for dinner. We look forward to being surprised with what more they have to offer.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, 3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Visited Across, Kala Ghoda and had a really warm and comforting dining experience. We ordered quite a few dishes — Pomelo Bliss, Fresh Lime Water, Fry Bread, Mushroom Choila, Mustang Black Dal, Ghee Rice, and the Mountain Road Brownie. The food reflects the authentic flavours of the Himalayan region, and you can taste the use of mustard oil in certain dishes, which gives it a very homely, regional touch.

The staff surprised us with a complimentary Churpi Cheese Dip with crisps while the Mustang Black Dal was getting prepared. Churpi cheese is traditionally made in Himalayan regions — slightly smoky, chewy, and packed with natural flavour. The dip version they served was delicious and definitely worth trying! Honestly, the fact that they offered it complimentary because the dal was taking time (I’m guessing they make it fresh) felt very thoughtful and added to the experience.

We weren’t drinking alcohol, but based on how good the Pomelo Bliss mocktail was, I’m guessing their cocktails would be quite interesting too.

The place is slightly on the pricier side, but since we were celebrating our first date anniversary, it felt completely worth it. Overall, a cosy spot with great service and flavourful, comforting Himalayan cuisine — definitely a memorable meal!, name_person=Ketki Yash}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Across in Kala Ghoda, Mumbai, is brought to life by Viraf Patel and Prakriti Lama, who traveled the Eastern Himalayas to craft a menu celebrating its rugged flavors.

The restaurant specializes in Himalayan cuisine, blending traditional ingredients with modern techniques. Expect authentic dishes from Nepal, Bhutan, and Northeast India, featuring bold spices, local produce, and unique pairings

.Cocktails: The cocktails are a highlight, with the Mezcal Negroni stealing the show—smoky, balanced, and served with homemade Churpi cheese, elevating the experience

Fing Salad: A vibrant mix of greens and herbs, punched up with a zesty, umami-rich dressing, beautifully presented for a fresh, flavorful bite.

Veg Momos: Juicy, perfectly steamed dumplings bursting with flavor, paired with a tangy, spicy dip that adds a fiery kick.

Fry Bread: A unique treat with gooey Kalimpong cheese, drizzled with spicy honey dip for a delightful sweet-spicy balance.

Solu White Beans Hummus: A creamy, standout dish made from Himalayan white beans, topped with oyster mushrooms and fried onions, served with “insecurity bread” for scooping.

Bhatti Chicken: Slow-roasted chicken cubes marinated in roasted cumin and Nepali spices, served on puffed rice with fried onions—tender and packed with flavor.

Prawns in Mustang Jimbu: Perfectly cooked prawns with garlic, chili, and Himalayan wild chives, offering a fresh, aromatic twist.

Mustang Black Dal: The star of the menu, this Himalayan delicacy is a soulful, slow-cooked black dal served with ghee-infused rice and condiments—a hearty, comforting meal.

Darjeeling Aloo: Twice-cooked potato wedges dusted with Timur pepper and chili, delivering a crispy, spicy punch.
Desserts: The desserts are fabulous, with indulgent options that round off the meal perfectly

Ambiance & Service: The place is always buzzing, with a lively vibe. The staff is quick, attentive, and welcoming.

Reservations are a must due to its popularity.

Overall: Across is a must-visit for its bold Himalayan flavors, creative cocktails, and warm hospitality. Kudos to the team for an unforgettable dining experience., name_person=Prithvish Ashar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a month ago, review=Most unusual and enjoyable menu. The chefs have finally nailed a different and curated tasteful menu. Lovvee the cocktails and the meat is cooked with love and care.. A must go if you enjoy tasting food from different regions and have an accepting palette., name_person=Monaz Cooper}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=It's a good place to try out non veg food. The food is decent but it's expensive and the quantity is less.
The ambience is nice. They have candles and it could be a good place to go for a date, etc. The tables are however small and difficult to eat comfortably if you order more dishes.
The service was mixed. They suggest food nicely however they don't serve the items on your plates. Even the items were not very hot and lukewarm on general.
Overall good for tasting and exploring once., name_person=Bharath Kota (Ksb)}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a week ago, review=This restaurant serves Himalayan belt food from different parts of regions, and honestly the food was phenomenal.

Across is Himalayan food reimagined and oh, so so good. The churpi yak cheese is too die for. The fried bread with cheese on top is an absolute must try. Darjeeling Aloo Dum and Cheese Gnudi are my absolute favourites. This place excels better at veg food than non veg. The pork belly can be made better. Even the chicken kothey. But nonetheless, the cocktails more than makes up for it. To end the night, don’t forget to try their warm walnut and chocolate cake with churpi shavings on top. The best sweet to keep you salivating throughout the night with a smile., name_person=Debasmita Roy}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Really enjoyed the comforting food with such a variety of different flavours and colours, plus the warm service.  We tried small and big plates, good portions too.

While it was absolutely delicious, some more Himachali apples in the dessert would have been appreciated, it did not seem in line with its menu description.

Extensive bar menu.  My margarita was quite strong, but the second cocktail - a wonderful gin kefir lime concoction - felt a little watered down.

Even for Bombay, the table for two is tight - too small really, especially when the other table for two next to us was occupied.  It would've been awful if the big table for six on the other side had been taken as well.

The decor is at odds, doesn't match the warmth of the food and booking a table is a slightly cumbersome process, but overall, a hearty experience...I'd definitely go back., name_person=Nive Raitz von Frentz}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Lovely restaurant serving unique food from the Himalayan states and countries like Nepal and Bhutan too.
The kothey momos, Bhatti chicken, duck leg and the desserts apple cremeschmitte and flourless brownie were good too., name_person=Sudarshan Pawar}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good music and inventive food (and also Cocktail but I did not try) menu.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Great service and good portion size !!}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good ambience, polite staff, but limited vegetarian options.}"]

I spoke with the head chef who has worked to maintain Thai flavors while respecting vegetarian majority. Nonetheless you request Thai style and she will turn it out authentic Thai style. All of our food was delicious - some of the tastiest Thai food I’ve had outside of Thailand. We shared the lotus and banana leaf salad, the red curry with shrimp, and the spicy basil rice. Everything was so delicious and satisfying. Our server was polite and attentive. The atmosphere is nice as well. Would love to return on our next trip to Mumbai!, name_person=Rishi Mistry}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=4 years ago, review=Went to Thai pavilion for dinner recently and had a great experience! I ordered the Tom yum soup which was spicy and nice. We also got the lotus root chips which also tasted good with the house sauces that they provide.

I’ve tried Odia cuisine before, including at Orchid Hotels, but nothing really stood out back then. This place completely changed my perception of Odia food!

They offer an à la carte menu as part of the unlimited brunch, which is a refreshing concept. They also serve some snacks and sweets directly on the table. The only thing I felt was that the portion sizes are quite small, served in tiny bowls — some might find that a bit annoying, but honestly, it’s a thoughtful approach to avoid food wastage.

The non-veg dishes were absolutely delicious, packed with authentic flavours. The place also has really good vibes, and the ambiance is great for a relaxed brunch. The staff and waiters were attentive, though since it was a Sunday, the service was a little laid-back because of the crowd — but nothing that would ruin the experience.

Overall, it’s totally worth it, especially if you want to explore Odia cuisine in Mumbai. 📍 Location: Fort, Kala Ghoda
💫 Ambience: Artistic, cozy, and perfect for catching a vibe with your loved ones. The décor sets the tone for a memorable evening.

🥂 Drinks
We kicked off our evening with two standout cocktails:

Gateway Walker – Unique, refreshing, and beautifully balanced.
Bombay 01 – This one stole the show! A creative mix with bold flavors that linger.
For mocktail lovers:
Kokum Sharbat and Virgin Musketeer were both super refreshing and hit the spot!
🍽️ Starters
Kheema Mutton Pattice – Rich, flavorful, and melts in the mouth.
Taleli Kolambi – Prawns cooked in Malwani masala; absolutely mind-blowing!
Bharille Pomfret – The star of the starters! Stuffed and spiced to perfection – a must-try.
🍛 Main Course
Non-Veg Thali – A powerhouse of flavors with Kolhapuri Kombdi, Kala Mutton, Chicken Kaleji – beautifully presented and even better in taste.
Seafood Thali – Tisrya Masala, Malwani Fish Curry, Bombil Rava Fry – pure bliss for seafood lovers. Every element was top-notch.
🍮 Dessert
Ode to Puran Poli – A creative and nostalgic twist on the classic dessert. Warm, sweet, and the perfect ending to a fantastic meal.
🌟 Service: 10/10 – The staff was courteous, well-informed, and guided us through the menu with genuine enthusiasm.

🔥 Final Verdict
If you’re at Kala Ghoda and looking for a place to unwind with great food and even better cocktails, Hylo is a must-visit. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=6 months ago, review=It’s an awesome , cozy place.
